## Goal

## Correctness findings

The review found 1351 possible errors or notation conflicts. 119 of them are verified (102 fixed, 9 partly, 8 rejected); the other 1232 are not verified yet. Each item links to the full suggestion entry.

- [[#N0058|N0058]] Quadratic Formula: The equation is written "$2\,a\,x^2+b^2\,x^1+c\,x^0 = 0$"; the quadratic whose roots are given by the formula is $ax^2+bx+c=0$ (no factor 2 on $a$, and $b$ not squared).
- [[#N0058|N0058]] Quadratic Formula: The alternative form "$\frac{2c}{-b \pm \sqrt{b^2-4ac}}$" pairs the signs wrongly: with the same choice of sign, $\frac{-b\pm\sqrt D}{2a}=\frac{2c}{-b\mp\sqrt D}$ (use $\mp$), and it requires $c\ne0$.

- [[#N0108|N0108]] Solve spherical triangles: In "Spherical curves and distances from coordinates", "apply the spherical cosine rule to their polar triangle" misuses the term defined in [[Geometry on a sphere]]; it should say "to the triangle formed by the north pole and the two points", whose sides are the colatitudes $\pi/2-\varphi_1$, $\pi/2-\varphi_2$ with included angle $\Delta\lambda$.
- [[#N0138|N0138]] Quadrics and motion along space curves: The physical-quantities table describes $\mechanical{\theta}$ also as "horizontal direction of the initial velocity measured from the positive $x$-axis", a meaning never used in the note; the cylindrical/spherical azimuth $\theta$ is written uncolored, so the row should describe only the rolling-circle rotation angle.
- [[#N0138|N0138]] Quadrics and motion along space curves: Symbol clash: in "Arc length and kinematics" $s$ is the integration variable in $\int_0^{t}\mechanical{\mathbf v}(s)\,ds$, while the next section and the cycloid use $s$ as arc length; rename the dummy variable to $\tau$ as the arc-length section already does.
- [[#N0138|N0138]] Quadrics and motion along space curves: Macro misuse: the helix example writes $\mechanical{\mathbf r}(t)=\langle\cos t,t,\sin t\rangle$ "in numerical coordinates" with an uncolored dimensionless $t$; either drop the mechanical macros there or give the example units and a colored time.
- [[#N0148|N0148]] 05.08 Lines and planes: "See [[05.07 Linear combinations]] for the difference between a span through the origin and its translated copy" points to a note that never discusses translated copies; link [[10.01 Vector spaces]] (which mentions translated lines and affine sets) or drop the claim.
- [[#N0150|N0150]] Basis change: In "Basis change on Covector", ${e'}_j = B^i_j\ a_i$ uses an undefined $a_i$; it should read ${e'}_j = B^i_j\ e_i$.
- [[#N0151|N0151]] Cross product: The index form $c_i = ε_{ijk} \, a_i \, b_j$ is wrong (free index $i$ repeated, $k$ dangling); it must be $c_i=\varepsilon_{ijk}\,a_j\,b_k$.
- [[#N0151|N0151]] Cross product: "Determinant of two 3D vectors" is not a valid definition (a determinant needs three rows); say that $\mathbf a\times\mathbf b$ is the formal determinant with rows $(\mathbf e_x,\mathbf e_y,\mathbf e_z)$, $\mathbf a$, $\mathbf b$, i.e. its components are $2\times2$ minors.
- [[#N0155|N0155]] Scalar Product: $c_i = a_i\,b_i$ defines a vector (the component-wise product), not the scalar product; the dot product is $c=a_ib_i=\sum_i a_ib_i$ with no free index, and writing $c=a\,b$ without a dot clashes with the geometric product $ab$ in [[Vector product]].
- [[#N0155|N0155]] Scalar Product: The angle formula is restricted to "$\forall a,b\in\mathbb{R}^2$" although it holds in any $\mathbb R^n$ with an orthonormal basis; generalize it and require $a,b\neq0$ for the $\cos\gamma$ formula.
- [[#N0159|N0159]] Vector product: "with $xy = -xy$ and $xx = 1$" is wrong as written; it should be $e_xe_y=-e_ye_x$ (distinct basis vectors) and $e_xe_x=1$.
- [[#N0159|N0159]] Vector product: The bivector basis lines $e_z e_x = -(e_z e_x) = j$ and $e_y e_z = -(e_y e_z) = k$ assert $X=-X$; they should read $e_ze_x=-e_xe_z=j$ and $e_ye_z=-e_ze_y=k$.
- [[#N0159|N0159]] Vector product: The overbrace labels the bivector part "cross product"; it is the wedge product $a\wedge b$, whose components equal those of $a\times b$ only through the Hodge dual ($a\wedge b=I\,(a\times b)$ with $I=e_xe_ye_z$).
- [[#N0169|N0169]] LU factorization and matrix practice: "On [[Linear maps, inverses, and determinants#Determinants by elimination|the section on Determinants by elimination]] the same symbol denotes the determinant of that submatrix" points to the wrong heading; $M_{ij}$ is defined under [[Linear maps, inverses, and determinants#Cofactors]].
- [[#N0170|N0170]] Linear algebra - Catalogue Guide: [[Planned Topics#4. Linear algebra|the detailed catalogue]] is broken: no note named "Planned Topics" exists in the vault; retarget it or remove it.
- [[#N0175|N0175]] Row reduction and the four fundamental subspaces: Wrong internal anchors: "The portfolio vectors on [[#Reduced row echelon form]]" (they are introduced under "Span and dependence"), "For the matrix on the section on Homework 2" (the matrix is in "Homogeneous systems"), and three references to [[#Forward elimination and back substitution]] for the matrix $B$, which is defined under "Rectangular matrix".
- [[#N0176|N0176]] Scaling Matrices: "A matrix $M$ is scaling a vector field, if it's Determinant is not equal to 1" is wrong: $\operatorname{diag}(2,1/2)$ scales both axes yet has determinant 1, and a rotation combined with a scaling has determinant $\ne1$ without being a scaling matrix; define a scaling matrix as $\operatorname{diag}(s_x,s_y,\ldots)$ and say $|\det|$ is the volume factor.
- [[#N0176|N0176]] Scaling Matrices: "Scaling Matrix in $ℝ^2$" shows a $3\times3$ matrix; the linear scaling on $\mathbb R^2$ is $\begin{pmatrix}s_x&0\\0&s_y\end{pmatrix}$, and the $3\times3$ form acts on homogeneous coordinates (same issue for the $\mathbb R^3$ and $\mathbb R^4$ sections).
- [[#N0178|N0178]] Subspaces, eigenvectors, and orthogonal projections: Wrong anchors: "The conditions on [[#Vector spaces and subspaces]] for injectivity" (they are listed under "The four fundamental subspaces"); "as on [[Coordinate matrices and diagonalization#Stretching along a basis direction]]" for the transpose matrix (it is under "Coordinate representation of a matrix"); "[[#Orthogonal projections|the section on Final review. Orthogonal projections]]" for inner-product preservation (the proof is under "Orthonormal sets", and "Final review" is not a heading).
- [[#N0179|N0179]] Symmetrization and Antisymmetrization: "Any real square matrix $A_{ii}$" and "$A_{ii}= A_{(ij)} + A_{[ij]}$" use a diagonal index; both should be $A_{ij}$.
- [[#N0179|N0179]] Symmetrization and Antisymmetrization: The general symmetrization formula is written with square brackets $A_{[i_1 i_2 \dots i_n]}$; it must use round brackets $A_{(i_1 i_2 \dots i_n)}$, since square brackets denote antisymmetrization in this note.
- [[#N0179|N0179]] Symmetrization and Antisymmetrization: "$\omega_{ij} = \epsilon_{ijk},\omega^k$" has a stray comma and is not an antisymmetrization formula; write $\omega_{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}\omega^k$ with inverse $\omega^k=\tfrac12\epsilon^{kij}\omega_{ij}$ and say it identifies 3D antisymmetric matrices with axial vectors.
- [[#N0180|N0180]] Vectors, projections, lines, and planes: The "Physical quantities" table lists $\lVert\mechanical{\mathbf v}\rVert$ as speed in $\unit{m\,s^{-1}}$, but the note uses $\mathbf v$ only as a generic geometric vector and never as velocity; remove the table (and the macro use) from this mathematics note.
- [[#N0184|N0184]] Determinant of a Matrix: The $3\times3$ formula $aei + bdi + ceg - afh - bdi - ceg$ is wrong (it cancels to $aei-afh$); the rule of Sarrus gives $aei+bfg+cdh-ceg-bdi-afh$.
- [[#N0184|N0184]] Determinant of a Matrix: The cofactor expansion $a_1\det(M_{11})-a_2\det(M_{12})+\cdots+(-1)^n a_n\det(M_{nn})$ is wrong in its last term and sign; it should be $\det A=\sum_{j=1}^n(-1)^{1+j}a_{1j}\det M_{1j}$ (Laplace expansion, not "Levi-Civita's expansion").
- [[#N0184|N0184]] Determinant of a Matrix: "$\det A=1$ ... representing rotations" and "$\det A\notin\{0,1,-1\}$ indicates scaling or skewing" are wrong: shears have determinant 1, and $\operatorname{diag}(2,1/2)$ scales with determinant 1; determinant only fixes the signed volume factor. Likewise in the second callout, $\det R=\pm1$ does not make a matrix orthogonal, so say "for orthogonal matrices".
- [[#N0184|N0184]] Determinant of a Matrix: "Volume of a Vector Space" puts a formal row $(\mathbf i,\mathbf j,\mathbf k,\ldots)$ into the matrix; the volume spanned by $n$ vectors in $\mathbb R^n$ is $|\det[a\;b\;c\;\cdots]|$ of the $n\times n$ matrix of their components, and "a positive determinant indicates that vectors form a volume" should say "nonzero".
- [[#N0184|N0184]] Determinant of a Matrix: "Orientation of a Vector Space" uses the determinant of an $n\times(n+1)$ matrix, which is undefined; orientation is the sign of the $n\times n$ determinant of the basis relative to a reference basis.
- [[#N0187|N0187]] Eigenvectors and Eigenvalues: "When eigenvectors and eigenvalues are imaginary, then every non-zero vector will change" is imprecise: the relevant case is non-real complex eigenvalues (for example $(1\pm i)/\sqrt2$ for a $45^\circ$ rotation, not purely imaginary), and the correct conclusion is that no nonzero real vector stays on its own line.
- [[#N0200|N0200]] Hermitian Conjungate: "$\|J\|^2 = J^{\dagger} J = J J^{\dagger}$" is wrong: $J^\dagger J$ is the scalar $\|J\|^2$, but $JJ^\dagger$ is an $n\times n$ matrix (the projector onto $J$ when $\|J\|=1$).
- [[#N0200|N0200]] Hermitian Conjungate: "we can't simply get the inverse of the vector using the transpose method" describes the wrong concept; the issue is the squared norm, since $J^TJ$ can be zero or complex for nonzero $J$ (for example $J=(1,i)$).

- [[#N0238|N0238]] Integral of a Derivative: The first integrand $\int_{t=0}^{n}\frac{F(t)}{dt}\,dt$ lacks the differential in the numerator; it must be $\int_0^n\frac{dF}{dt}\,dt$ (or $\int_0^n\dot F(t)\,dt$).
- [[#N0238|N0238]] Integral of a Derivative: The final equation $\int_0^n\dot f g\,dt=-\int_0^n f\dot g\,dt$ drops the boundary term; the correct statement is $\int_0^n\dot f g\,dt=\bigl[fg\bigr]_0^n-\int_0^n f\dot g\,dt$ (the pure sign swap holds only when $fg$ takes equal values at both endpoints).
- [[#N0238|N0238]] Integral of a Derivative: The "expansion" $(F(1)-F(0))+\dots+(F(n)-F(n-1))$ is a unit-step telescoping sum, not an expansion of the integral; present it as $\sum F'(\xi_i)\Delta t=\sum[F(t_i)-F(t_{i-1})]$ (mean value theorem) with $\Delta t\to0$, replace "the forces cancel" by "the intermediate terms cancel", and close the missing parenthesis in $(F(n)-F(n-1))$.
- [[#N0238|N0238]] Integral of a Derivative: In "Notation in Textbooks" the delimiters are swapped: use `\Bigl[ F(t) \Bigr]`, not "`\Bigr[` and `\Bigl]`"; also the product rule is a consequence, not the definition, of the derivative of $fg$.
- [[#N0239|N0239]] Integration by parts and trigonometric substitutions: Under Fig. 4 the text says the substitution angle "is complementary to the angle labeled $\theta$ in the sketch", so $\theta$ names two different angles; relabel the sketch angle (e.g. $\varphi=\pi/2-\theta$) or replace the figure so it matches $x=a\sin\theta$.

- [[#N0405|N0405]] Periodic forcing and Laplace-transform problems: The "Physical quantities" table describes content absent from this note: $\mechanical{m}$ "slice of the conducting rod", $\mechanical{x}$ "distance along the wave and heat models", $\signal{t}$ "vibration and heat models"; restrict the descriptions to the forced oscillator.
- [[#N0413|N0413]] Energy Conservation Example: Step 4: $\varphi_0=\arctan(x_0\omega/v_0)$ gives the wrong phase for $v_0<0$ and is undefined for $v_0=0$; for $x=A\sin(\omega t+\varphi_0)$ use $\varphi_0=\operatorname{atan2}(x_0\omega,\,v_0)$ (equivalently $\sin\varphi_0=x_0/A$, $\cos\varphi_0=v_0/(\omega A)$); likewise Step 3's $\varphi_0=\arcsin(x_0/A)$ only covers $v_0\ge0$.
- [[#N0414|N0414]] Hamiltonian Flow Example: Step 4: "The flow matrix above rotates the vector $\mathbf{u}$" is false unless $m\omega=1$; $\mathrm{e}^{At}$ is not orthogonal and moves $\mathbf{u}$ along an ellipse; it is a rotation only in the scaled coordinates $(x,\,p/(m\omega))$.
- [[#N0417|N0417]] Substitution Example: Second section: the first derivative is written $\frac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}t^2}$ (should be $\frac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}t}$) and the last equation writes $\frac{\mathrm{d}^2x^2}{\mathrm{d}t^2}$ (should be $\frac{\mathrm{d}^2x}{\mathrm{d}t^2}$).
- [[#N0417|N0417]] Substitution Example: Second section: the ansatz is stated as $x=A\cos(\Omega t)$ but then differentiated as $A\cos(\Omega t)+B\sin(\Omega t)$; the table omits $B$, calls $\Omega$ "Oscillation Frequency" (it is an angular frequency), and $\Omega$ duplicates the first section's $\omega$; the conclusion $\Omega^2=k/m$ is never stated.
- [[#N0418|N0418]] Algebraic Rules for Ordinary Differential Equations (ODE): Logarithmic derivatives: "$\frac{d}{dt}\ln f=f'/f$ applies whenever $f(t)$ stays away from zero" is wrong for $f<0$, where $\ln f$ is undefined; require $f>0$ or write $\frac{d}{dt}\ln|f|=f'/f$ for $f\neq0$ (matching the integral section's $\ln|f|$).
- [[#N0420|N0420]] Types of Differentials: Exterior derivative: "$d\omega=\partial_\nu\omega_\mu\wedge dx^\nu\wedge dx^\mu$" wedges a function component; the correct form is $d\omega=\partial_\nu\omega_\mu\,dx^\nu\wedge dx^\mu$ (equivalently $\tfrac12(\partial_\nu\omega_\mu-\partial_\mu\omega_\nu)\,dx^\nu\wedge dx^\mu$).
- [[#N0420|N0420]] Types of Differentials: Covariant derivative key point: it is not "the unique derivative operator"; uniqueness holds only for the Levi-Civita connection (torsion-free and metric-compatible), so state that condition.
- [[#N0420|N0420]] Types of Differentials: Laplacian: "measures how a scalar deviates from its average value" holds for the Riemannian Laplacian, not for the Lorentzian d'Alembertian $\Box$ that the same section names; separate $\nabla^2$ (elliptic) from $\Box$ (wave operator).
- [[#N0420|N0420]] Types of Differentials: Table row for $u^\mu\nabla_\mu$ says a connection is required, but on scalars $u^\mu\nabla_\mu f=u^\mu\partial_\mu f=df/d\tau$ needs none; note that the connection enters only for tensors. The Lie derivative key point "captures changes due to coordinate motion" should read "changes relative to the flow of $v$".
- [[#N0442|N0442]] Linearization, phase portraits, and nonlinear maps: The Physical quantities table lists $\beta$ twice with conflicting meanings ("Crowding coefficient, $\unit{s^{-1}}$" and "Predator effect coefficient, 1"), gives $\lambda$ as a Lyapunov exponent although here $\lambda$ is always a Jacobian eigenvalue or recurrence root, and contains rows for symbols that never occur in this note ($T$ sampling period, $x,y$ ingredient amounts in oz, $s$ protein surplus, $t$ iron surplus); rebuild it from the symbols actually used.
- [[#N0442|N0442]] Linearization, phase portraits, and nonlinear maps: Symbol clashes: $\beta$ is the predator-effect coefficient in $R'=\alpha R(1-\beta W)$ but also the logistic-map parameter $\beta=1+\alpha\Delta t$, and $\alpha$ is the rabbit growth rate, the multiplier in $y_n=\alpha y_{n-1}$, and the logistic rate; rename the map parameter (e.g. $r$) and the recurrence multiplier.

- [[#N0510|N0510]] Taylor error bounds and finite-digit arithmetic: "Choosing a degree for sine": $(\pi/4)^{n+1}/(n+1)!$ equals $3.59\times10^{-6}$ at $n=7$, $3.13\times10^{-7}$ at $n=8$ and $2.46\times10^{-8}$ at $n=9$, i.e. orders $10^{-6},10^{-7},10^{-8}$, not $10^{-5},10^{-6},10^{-7}$ as stated; the conclusion $n=8$ is right.

- [[#N0572|N0572]] Group: "Group homomorphisms ... given a morphism $f$ on the group $(G,·)$ we can define $f(a\cdot b)=f(a)\cdot f(b)$" is wrong as stated: a homomorphism is a map between two groups, $f:(G,\cdot)\to(H,\ast)$ with $f(a\cdot b)=f(a)\ast f(b)$, and it is not a rule "derived from the rules of groups" as the section's first sentence claims.
- [[#N0572|N0572]] Group: The axiom list omits closure and never says that $\cdot$ is a binary operation $G\times G\to G$, so "a special set with additional rules" does not define a group; add closure or define the operation as a map into $G$.
- [[#N0593|N0593]] Lp spaces and integral norms: Worked answer 1 writes $\|f\|_2=\sqrt2$ for $t^{-1/4}$, but $f$ already denotes $t^{-1/3}$ in this note; name the new function (e.g. $g(t)=t^{-1/4}$, $\|g\|_2=\sqrt2$).
- [[#N0604|N0604]] Cauchy integrals and boundary jumps: In "Worked example on an interval", "The answer diverges near some endpoints" is imprecise: $2+x\log[(1-x)/(1+x)]\to-\infty$ logarithmically at both $x\to1^-$ and $x\to-1^+$; say "near both endpoints".
- [[#N0620|N0620]] Box counting and random-walk distributions: The "Physical quantities" table lists symbols from other notes that are never used here and clash with this note: $M$ as carrying capacity (here $M$ is the square side length), $\delta$ as wolf decline rate (here $\delta$ is the Dirac delta), $x,y$ as ingredient amounts in oz (here positions), $s$ as protein surplus (here the signed step), $t$ as iron surplus and $1/\alpha$ (here time, $\alpha$ unused); keep only $\Delta x$, $\Delta t$, $D$, $U$ and add $L$ (box size) and $p$, $C$ if desired.
- [[#N0655|N0655]] 2.11 Laplacian: Symbol clash: $\phi$ denotes the scalar field in Eqs. (2.43)–(2.50) and the $k/r$ example, but the azimuth angle in Eqs. (2.51)–(2.52) (where the field is renamed $\psi$); use $\psi$ for the scalar field throughout the note.
- [[#N0670|N0670]] 3.5 Chapter 3 problems: Problem 3.3 gives a push of 10 N on a box of unspecified mass $m$; the speed at the top depends on $m$ ($a=F/m-g(\sin25^\circ+0.33\cos25^\circ)$, and the box only accelerates up the ramp if $m<1.41\,\mathrm{kg}$), so state a numerical mass.

(5.16)–(5.18) and the scalar field in the gradient and Laplacian formulas; $\theta$ is both the angle between $\vec A$ and $\vec B$ and the polar angle. (6.12) and the frame speed in the boost, and $\vec A$ is a generic vector field in Eq. (6.12) while $A$ is the Lorentz matrix in Eq. (6.18); rename the wave-equation field (e.g. $\vec\Psi$) and speed ($u$), and update the table.
- [[#N0697|N0697]] 6.4 Chapter 6 problems: The table lists $\theta$ only as the rotation angle of Problem 6.3, but Problem 6.9 uses $\theta$ as the polar angle in $ds^2=d\mechanical{r}^2+\mechanical{r}^2d\theta^2$; add the polar-angle meaning to that row (or use a different letter, e.g. $\alpha$, for the 20° rotation).
- [[#N0731|N0731]] Surface geometry curvature and geodesics: Symbol clash: $f$ is the graph function in $r(u,v)=(u,v,f(u,v))$ and also the second-form coefficient $f=n\cdot r_{uv}$, and $F$ is both the level-surface function $F(x,y,z)=0$ and the first-form coefficient $F=r_u\cdot r_v$; rename the second-form coefficients (e.g. $L,M,N$) and the implicit function (e.g. $\Phi$).
- [[#N0751|N0751]] Exterior Product: "$(a\wedge b)_i = ε_{ijk}\ a_j e_j\ b_k e_k$" mixes components with basis vectors and gives a vector, not a bivector; the bivector components are $(a\wedge b)_{jk}=a_jb_k-a_kb_j$, and in 3D its Hodge dual is the cross product $(a\times b)_i=\varepsilon_{ijk}a_jb_k$.
- [[#N0751|N0751]] Exterior Product: "$c_i = ε_{ijkl} \, a_j \, b_k \, e_l$" uses a four-index Levi-Civita symbol in three dimensions with a free basis vector; delete it or replace it by $a\wedge b=\tfrac12(a_jb_k-a_kb_j)\,e_j\wedge e_k$.
- [[#N0751|N0751]] Exterior Product: "2D exterior product: Special case of the cross product" writes $a\times b=a_xb_y-a_yb_x$; in 2D the wedge is $a\wedge b=(a_xb_y-a_yb_x)\,e_x\wedge e_y$ (a multiple of the unit bivector), and the wedge exists in every dimension while only in 3D is it dual to the cross product, so "higher order version of the cross product" inverts the relation.
- [[#N0753|N0753]] Algebra of Rotation: The heading "Algebraic Spaces of Rotation $SO(n)$" lists complex numbers, quaternions and spinors, which represent $U(1)\cong SO(2)$ and $SU(2)=\mathrm{Spin}(3)$ (a double cover), not $SO(n)$ itself; retitle e.g. "Representations of rotations" and state which group each item realizes.
- [[#N0754|N0754]] Homotopology classes in the Axis-Angle Space: "Those loops may have a winding number greater than 0" suggests an integer invariant; the fundamental group of $SO(3)$ is $\mathbb Z_2$, so there are exactly two classes and no integer winding number. Say this explicitly.
- [[#N0754|N0754]] Homotopology classes in the Axis-Angle Space: The space is described only as "a loop around a spherical space ... represented as a circle"; state precisely that the axis-angle space is the solid ball of radius $\pi$ with antipodal boundary points identified ($\mathbb{RP}^3$), and that a "teleport" is passing through the boundary to the antipodal point.
- [[#N0755|N0755]] Homotopology: "Two curves are called homotopic when they have the same Topology" is wrong: all curves have the topology of an interval or circle; homotopy is a continuous deformation inside a given space (with fixed endpoints, or freely for loops). Replace with the definition $H:[0,1]\times[0,1]\to X$, $H(\cdot,0)=\gamma_0$, $H(\cdot,1)=\gamma_1$.
- [[#N0755|N0755]] Homotopology: "A homotopic class is defined by the winding number" is only true for spaces with fundamental group $\mathbb Z$ (circle, annulus, cylinder); for $SO(3)$, used in the companion note, the classes form $\mathbb Z_2$. State the general notion (fundamental group $\pi_1(X)$) and give winding number as the $\mathbb Z$ example.
- [[#N0756|N0756]] Rotation using Axis-Angle Vector: "can be represented by some (one or more) axis" contradicts Euler's rotation theorem cited right below: every rotation of $\mathbb R^3$ is a rotation about exactly one axis (unique unless the rotation is the identity).
- [[#N0756|N0756]] Rotation using Axis-Angle Vector: The callout "Rotations in 3 dimensions can't be properly represented by an 3d vector ... requires 4 dimensions" is misleading: every rotation is represented by the 3-parameter axis-angle vector ($SO(3)$ is 3-dimensional); what fails is that axis-angle vectors do not compose by addition and do not record the path class, which the unit quaternion on $S^3\subset\mathbb R^4$ captures.
- [[#N0756|N0756]] Rotation using Axis-Angle Vector: Symbol clash: the angle is $Θ$ in the first section and $θ$ in "Angular velocity"; also state that $\dot{\hat x}_b=ω_s\times\hat x_b$ requires all vectors expressed in frame $s$.
- [[#N0758|N0758]] Rotation using Matrices: "Because $SO(3)$ is fully contained in $SU(2)$" is wrong: $SO(3)$ is not a subgroup of $SU(2)$ but the quotient $SU(2)/\{\pm I\}$ via a 2-to-1 homomorphism; the line "$v'\leftrightarrow\pm s'$" should be replaced by the map $s\mapsto s^\dagger\vec\sigma s$ from spinors to vectors.
- [[#N0758|N0758]] Rotation using Matrices: Gimbal lock is a property of Euler-angle parametrizations, not of $SO(3)$ matrices; rotation matrices and unit quaternions are both free of it. Rewrite the warning accordingly.
- [[#N0758|N0758]] Rotation using Matrices: "Rotation matrices are not commutative" contradicts $SO(2)$, which the note treats at length and which is abelian ($R_θR_ϑ=R_{θ+ϑ}$); say $SO(n)$ is non-commutative for $n\ge3$.
- [[#N0758|N0758]] Rotation using Matrices: "In the special case of a matrix with determinant of $-1$, it is considered to be in the group $S(n)$" is wrong: there is no such group; orthogonal matrices with $\det=-1$ form $O(n)\setminus SO(n)$, which is not a group (not closed under products).
- [[#N0758|N0758]] Rotation using Matrices: Product rule: if $R_{AB}$ maps column components from frame A to frame B, then $R_{AC}=R_{BC}R_{AB}$, not $R_{AB}R_{BC}$; either reverse the order or define $R_{AB}$ as the orientation of B relative to A (Modern Robotics convention). Also the set definitions "$O(n)={R∈ℝ^{n×n}∣R^TR=I}$" lose their braces when rendered; use escaped braces.
- [[#N0760|N0760]] Jones Vectors: "we can assume it to be complex, with a complex value of zero" is wrong: the added imaginary part is $iA\sin(ωt-kz+φ)$, not zero; the physical field is $\mathrm{Re}\,E$.
- [[#N0760|N0760]] Jones Vectors: The "Conventions" section attributes the sign of $L=(1,\pm i)$ to the metric signature $(+,-,-,-)$ vs $(-,+,+,+)$; it actually depends on the phase convention $e^{i(ωt-kz)}$ vs $e^{i(kz-ωt)}$ and on whether handedness is defined from the source or the receiver view.
- [[#N0760|N0760]] Jones Vectors: Under "Jones Matrices", waveplates do not "filter circular polarization" (they are lossless retarders), and $\frac1{\sqrt2}\begin{pmatrix}1&i\\i&i\end{pmatrix}$ is not unitary; the 45° quarter-wave plate is $\frac1{\sqrt2}\begin{pmatrix}1&i\\i&1\end{pmatrix}$ up to a global phase.
- [[#N0760|N0760]] Jones Vectors: In "Phase Shift", adding $φ=\pi/2$ gives $\cos(θ+\pi/2)=-\sinθ$, not $\sinθ$; the quoted identity $\sinθ=\cos(θ-\pi/2)$ corresponds to $φ=-\pi/2$.
- [[#N0760|N0760]] Jones Vectors: Symbol inconsistency: amplitudes appear as $A_x$, $Aʸ$ (Unicode superscript) and $A^x,A^y$, components as bold $\mathbf E^x$ and plain $E^x$; also fix the typos "$eit$", "$\mathbf{_x}$", "_x-direction", "non-traverse", and replace "density in time/space" by frequency $ω/2\pi$ and inverse wavelength $k/2\pi$.
- [[#N0761|N0761]] Pointcaré Sphere: "$Q''=\frac12\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\-1&1\end{pmatrix}$" is not unitary; the factor must be $\frac1{\sqrt2}$, as the note's own later callout uses.
- [[#N0761|N0761]] Pointcaré Sphere: The name is "Poincaré", not "Pointcaré", in the filename, text and reference label (also "Wikipdia").
- [[#N0762|N0762]] Waveplates: In "Rotated Quarter Waveplate", "$\cos 45° = \cos\frac{π}{2}$" is wrong; $45°=\pi/4$ (the final numeric matrix is correct).
- [[#N0762|N0762]] Waveplates: After $QL=A$, "we get the original polarization direction, but with a half cycle phase change" is wrong: $A$ is perpendicular to the original $D$; two quarter-wave passes act as a half-wave plate that maps $D$ to $A$.
- [[#N0762|N0762]] Waveplates: "$e^{i \frac{π}{4}}{4}$" contains a stray "{4}"; the verified result is $G^{-1}QG=e^{i\pi/4}\frac1{\sqrt2}\begin{pmatrix}1&i\\i&1\end{pmatrix}$.
- [[#N0763|N0763]] Dirac Equation: "$\hat{p}^μ = -i\hbar \partial_\mu$" has the wrong sign and mismatched index placement for the stated equation; with $\psi\propto e^{-ip\cdot x/\hbar}$ and signature $(+,-,-,-)$, $\hat p_μ=i\hbar\partial_μ$, which turns $(\gamma^μ\hat p_μ-mc)\psi=0$ into $(i\hbar\gamma^μ\partial_μ-mc)\psi=0$.
- [[#N0763|N0763]] Dirac Equation: $(\psi_1,\psi_2)$ and $(\psi_3,\psi_4)$ are not "electron spinor" and "positron spin" in general; in the Dirac representation they are the large and small components, which separate into particle and antiparticle parts only in the nonrelativistic limit (in the Weyl representation they are the left- and right-handed parts).
- [[#N0763|N0763]] Dirac Equation: "Klein-Gordon let's derive the Lorentz Invariance without Spinors, so electrons are not neccessarily Fermions" is confused: Klein–Gordon is the spin-0 equation; Dirac's first-order equation needs $\{\gamma^μ,\gamma^ν\}=2\eta^{μν}$ and four-component spinors, which is why it describes spin-1/2 particles.
- [[#N0764|N0764]] Pauli Exclusion Principle: "Two or more fermions cannot occupy the same quantum state" must say identical fermions; different species (e.g. an electron and a muon) are not constrained.
- [[#N0765|N0765]] Spin-Statistics-Theorem: The sentence describes the exchange property of fermions, not the theorem; the theorem states that in relativistic quantum field theory integer-spin particles obey Bose statistics (symmetric) and half-integer-spin particles obey Fermi statistics (antisymmetric), and the sign applies to exchange of identical particles only.
- [[#N0766|N0766]] Spinors in Physics: "Quarks, Electron, Muon, Tau Neutrino (Tauons)" omits the tau lepton as such and the electron and muon neutrinos; list the six quarks and the six leptons $e,\mu,\tau,\nu_e,\nu_\mu,\nu_\tau$.
- [[#N0766|N0766]] Spinors in Physics: "spin, is $\frac{n}{2}\hbar$, where $n$ is an integer" includes integer spins; $n$ must be odd. Also the spin quantum number $s$ gives magnitude $\sqrt{s(s+1)}\hbar$ while $s\hbar$ is the maximal projection; say which is meant in both sections.
- [[#N0767|N0767]] Stern-Gerlach-Experiment: "Born Rule: If two states are mutually exclusive, they must be orthogonal" is not the Born rule; the Born rule is $P=|\braket{\beta|\alpha}|^2$, and orthogonality of perfectly distinguishable outcomes follows from it.
- [[#N0768|N0768]] Vector Representation of Spinors in Physics: "$\bra{\phi} = \alpha \ket{\uparrow} + \beta \ket{\uparrow}$" should be the ket $\ket{\phi}=\alpha\ket{\uparrow}+\beta\ket{\downarrow}$ (bra on the left side and a repeated $\ket{\uparrow}$).
- [[#N0768|N0768]] Vector Representation of Spinors in Physics: The table calls $\alpha,\beta$ probabilities; they are complex probability amplitudes, the probabilities are $|\alpha|^2$ and $|\beta|^2$, with $|\alpha|^2+|\beta|^2=1$.
- [[#N0782|N0782]] Quaternions: The Pauli list repeats $\sigma_2$ twice and omits $\sigma_3=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}$.
- [[#N0782|N0782]] Quaternions: "They can be used to replace i, j, k in Quaternions" is wrong as stated: $\sigma_a^2=+I$, not $-I$. The correct substitution is $i\mapsto-i\sigma_1$, $j\mapsto-i\sigma_2$, $k\mapsto-i\sigma_3$, which satisfies $i^2=j^2=k^2=ijk=-1$.
- [[#N0782|N0782]] Quaternions: "Properties of i, j, k" mixes cross products of basis vectors ($i\times i=0$) with quaternion products ($i^2=-1$) for the same letters; as quaternions $ii=-1$, $ij=k$, $ik=-j$. Use quaternion products throughout, or label the cross-product lines as the vector part of $uv$.
- [[#N0796|N0796]] 27.07 Transition functions: Symbol clash: $B$ is the base space ($\pi:E\to B$) and also a matrix in Practice 2 ($g_{23}=B$), and $A$ names an overlap component in the worked example and a matrix in Practice 2; rename the practice matrices (for example $M,N$).
- [[#N0798|N0798]] 27.09 Connections and holonomy: Symbol clash: $a$ is the rectangle width in "$[0,a]\times[0,b]$" and $\oint A=cab$, and later the real coefficient in $A=a\alpha$ with holonomy $e^{-2\pi ian}$; rename one (for example rectangle sides $w,h$ or coefficient $\kappa$).
- [[#N0803|N0803]] Category of Categories: "The Category set of all possible [[Category]]" is incorrect and runs into a size paradox; $\mathbf{Cat}$ is the category whose objects are small categories and whose morphisms are functors, with functor composition and identity functors. Also add a quoted title, a TLDR, and a trailing newline.
- [[#N0804|N0804]] Category: Under "Compositions", for $f:A\to B$ and $g:B\to C$ the composite is $g\circ f:A\to C$, not $h=f\circ g$; the note's own associativity law $(h\circ g)\circ f$ uses the right-to-left convention, so the composition line contradicts it.
- [[#N0804|N0804]] Category: The identity law "$I_e(e)=e$" applies a morphism to an element, which a general category does not provide; the law is $f\circ\mathrm{id}_A=f=\mathrm{id}_B\circ f$ for every $f:A\to B$.
- [[#N0804|N0804]] Category: "Objects are Elements in a Set" with the set-order and repetition examples is wrong and irrelevant: objects need not form a set (e.g. in $\mathbf{Set}$ itself) and need not have elements, and morphisms need not be functions between sets ("transformation functions"). Remove the set examples and give $\mathbf{Set}$, $\mathbf{Grp}$, $\mathbf{Vect}$ and a poset as examples.
- [[#N0805|N0805]] Equivalence: "Two groups $C$ and $D$" should be "two categories"; an equivalence consists of functors $F:C\to D$ and $G:D\to C$ with natural isomorphisms $G\circ F\cong1_C$ and $F\circ G\cong1_D$ (the categories themselves are not "natural isomorph").
- [[#N0805|N0805]] Equivalence: The natural-transformation paragraph omits the defining condition: $\nu:F\Rightarrow G$ is a family $\nu_X:F(X)\to G(X)$ with $G(f)\circ\nu_X=\nu_Y\circ F(f)$ for every $f:X\to Y$; it is a natural isomorphism when every $\nu_X$ is invertible, which is what $\nu^{-1}$ should express.
- [[#N0806|N0806]] Functor: "A Functor is a map between two sets" is wrong; a functor maps between categories (objects to objects, morphisms to morphisms), as the next sentence correctly says. Delete the first sentence.
- [[#N0807|N0807]] Isomorphism: The text calls the equations "$f\circ f^{-1}=I_B$ and $f^{-1}\circ f=I_A$" the isomorphisms; correctly, $f:A\to B$ is an isomorphism if some $g:B\to A$ satisfies $g\circ f=\mathrm{id}_A$ and $f\circ g=\mathrm{id}_B$, and then $g=f^{-1}$ is unique.
- [[#N0807|N0807]] Isomorphism: "isomorphisms between two sets" should be "between two objects" of a category; in $\mathbf{Set}$ isomorphisms are bijections, in $\mathbf{Grp}$ group isomorphisms, in $\mathbf{Top}$ homeomorphisms. Add these examples, a quoted title, and a TLDR.
- [[#N0809|N0809]] Definite integral tables: In "Definite integrals and improper limits", "At $0<p<1$, the power grows without bound" is misleading because the integrand $x^{-p}$ decays; it is the partial integral $(R^{1-p}-1)/(1-p)$ that grows without bound as $R\to\infty$.
- [[#N0810|N0810]] Elliptic integral tables: In "Worked example and a convention trap", $8E(0.5)\approx11.739696$ comes from multiplying the rounded table entry; the six-place value is $8E(0.5)=11.739698$.

- [[#N1145|N1145]] Impulse: The "Quantum kick operator" $\hat U = \exp(-\tfrac{i}{\hbar}\Delta\mathbf p\cdot\hat{\mathbf x})$ shifts momentum by $-\Delta\mathbf p$; a kick of $+\Delta\mathbf p$ needs $\hat U = \exp(+\tfrac{i}{\hbar}\Delta\mathbf p\cdot\hat{\mathbf x})$ since $\hat U^\dagger\hat{\mathbf p}\hat U = \hat{\mathbf p}+\Delta\mathbf p$. **Fixed:** Changed to exp(+i Δp·x̂/ħ), since U†p̂U = p̂ + Δp
- [[#N1146|N1146]] Momentum: The "Radiation pressure (ideal reflector)" row writes "$p_{\perp} = \dfrac{2I}{c} \Delta t /A$", which is dimensionally wrong; the pressure is $2I/c$ and the momentum transferred is $\Delta\mathbf p = (2IA\,\Delta t/c)\,\hat{\mathbf n} = (2\mathcal E_{\text{inc}}/c)\,\hat{\mathbf n}$. **Fixed:** Now P_rad = 2I/c ⇒ Δp = (2IAΔt/c) n̂ = (2E_inc/c) n̂ (renamed pressure symbol to P_rad to avoid clash with momentum p)
- [[#N1146|N1146]] Momentum: The row "Fluid momentum equation (Euler form)" includes the viscous stress term $\nabla\cdot\boldsymbol\tau$; with that term it is the Cauchy momentum (Navier–Stokes) equation, while the Euler equation is the inviscid case $\boldsymbol\tau=0$; relabel or drop the term. **Fixed:** Relabelled to "Cauchy form" and added note that the Euler equation is the inviscid case τ = 0

- [[#N1567|N1567]] 10.06.04 Specific Heat near the Lambda Transition: Fig. 10.4 puts the $T>T_\lambda$ branch above the $T<T_\lambda$ branch at equal $|t|$ ($A_->A_+$ in $C=C_c-A_\pm|t|^{0.013}$). Swap the amplitudes so the figure shows the lambda shape.

For 3D XY, theory gives $\alpha\approx-0.015$ and $\delta\approx4.78$ (the $-0.013$ is the helium-4 experimental value). Update the rows or mark them as dated.

- [[#N1628|N1628]] Ising mean field and transfer-matrix calculations: "Mean-field approximation": with $\energy{H}=-\energy{J}\sum_{\langle ij\rangle}\sigma_i\sigma_j$ (each pair once) the mean-field equation is $\bar\sigma=\tanh[\thermal{\beta}(q\energy{J}\bar\sigma+\energy{h})]$, so $\thermal{k}_{\mathrm B}\thermal{T}_{\mathrm c}=q\energy{J}$, not $q\energy{J}/2$; the factor $1/2$ belongs only in $\energy{U}=-Nq\energy{J}\bar\sigma^2/2$. Consequently the heat-capacity jump is $\tfrac32N\thermal{k}_{\mathrm B}$ (not $3N\thermal{k}_{\mathrm B}$) and the susceptibility prefactor is $N\magnetic{\mu}^2/(\energy{J}q)$ (not $2N\magnetic{\mu}^2/(\energy{J}q)$); fix these or state explicitly that the notebook's convention double-counts pairs.
- [[#N1628|N1628]] Ising mean field and transfer-matrix calculations: Physical-quantities table lists symbols the note never uses or uses differently: Planck's constant as $\energy{h}$ (clashes with the Ising field parameter; only $\energy{\hbar}$ appears), Landé $g$, internal partition function $j$, internal degeneracy $g$ (clashes with density of states $g(\energy{E})$), $\energy{F}$; and $\thermal{T}_{\mathrm c}$ is described as "onset of macroscopic ground-state occupation". - [[#N2036|N2036]] Hermitian operators and uncertainty derivations: Symbol clash in the opening: $a(x)$, $b(x)$ denote functions while $a$, $b$ are also the integration limits in the Schwarz inequality, and later $a,b,c,d$ are real coefficients in Problem 3.12; rename the functions (e.g. $u(x),v(x)$) or the limits.
- [[#N2036|N2036]] Hermitian operators and uncertainty derivations: The quantities table gives $\Psi$ in $\unit{m^{-3/2}}$ "in three dimensions", but the note is one-dimensional ($\Psi(x,t)$, $dx$), so the unit is $\unit{m^{-1/2}}$; also add the symbols used ($\mechanical{p}$, $q$, $\sigma_Q$, $c_n$).
- [[#N2060|N2060]] 06.05 Attractive Delta Potential: The source link [[Orbital angular momentum, rings, and spheres#Atkins problems 3.29 and 3.30|Physics 137]] targets a section about hydrogenic orbital and spin angular momentum, which has nothing to do with point interactions. The relevant heading in that note is "#Double delta well".
- [[#N2063|N2063]] 06.08 One-Dimensional Systems Exercises: Symbol clash: $T$ denotes both the transmission coefficient (exercises 2, 8, and 10) and the oscillation period (exercise 6), and the table lists both. Rename the period, for example to $\tau$.
- [[#N2064|N2064]] Free particles, finite barriers, and point interactions: $\alpha$ denotes three different things: the delta strength in $V=-\alpha\delta(x)$, the Gaussian parameter in $\phi(k)=\frac{2N}{\sqrt\alpha}\cos(kx_0)e^{-k^2/(2\alpha)}$, and the cosine coefficient in the centered infinite well $\psi_{\mathrm{II}}=\alpha\cos(kx)+\beta\sin(kx)$; rename the last two (e.g. $C,D$ and $a_G$); equation tags (1),(2) are also reused for both the Fourier pair and the even-state matching equations.
- [[#N2065|N2065]] Square-well, oscillator, and tunneling problems: The physical-quantities table lists $R$ as "Activity" in $\unit{Bq}$, but here $R$ is the dimensionless reflection coefficient; $E_n$ is described as "relative to ionization" in eV, which is wrong for the infinite well (measured from the well floor); add $T$, $k$, $\kappa$, $\eta$, $L$, $m$, $\psi$.
- [[#N2065|N2065]] Square-well, oscillator, and tunneling problems: Symbol clashes: in "Barrier boundary conditions" region III is $De^{ik_3x}+Fe^{-ik_3x}$ with $F=0$, but two paragraphs later it is $Fe^{ik_3x}+Ge^{-ik_3x}$ with $F$ the transmitted amplitude; the finite-well decay uses $\eta=1/\alpha$ with $\alpha$ never defined (use $\kappa$ as later in the note).

- [[#N2082|N2082]] Harmonic oscillator wavefunctions and ladder calculations: Symbol clashes: $\alpha$ is the Hermite scale $\sqrt{m\omega/\hbar}$, then $n\pi/a$ in the $\langle x\rangle$ integral, then the delta strength in $V=+\alpha\delta(x)$; $y$ is both the dimensionless oscillator coordinate and the unknown function in $y''+y=0$; $E_0$ is the oscillator ground energy $\hbar\omega/2$ and also "the constant multiplying $n^2$" for the well (the comparison table correctly uses $E_1$); $k$ and $k'$ swap roles between "Strategy for wavefunctions" and the last paragraph.
- [[#N2092|N2092]] Orbital angular momentum, rings, and spheres: The physical-quantities table lists $J_x$ as a probability flux with unit $\unit{s^{-1}}$, but the note uses $\hat J_x$ only as a generalized angular momentum component (section "General angular momentum"); also $R,T$ (reflection/transmission) never appear as symbols, while the mass $m$, $m_\ell$, $\hat J$, and $\Lambda^2$ are missing; rebuild the table from the symbols actually used.
- [[#N2092|N2092]] Orbital angular momentum, rings, and spheres: In the "Physics 137 — Midterm 2 review" block, "Its inner product is $\int_a^b\lvert f\rvert^2dx<\infty$, $\langle f\mid g\rangle=\ldots$" labels the square-integrability condition as the inner product; separate the two statements.
- [[#N2093|N2093]] Spatial rotations and the angular momentum generators: In "The three-dimensional rotation group", $O_y(\epsilon)O_x(\epsilon)-O_x(\epsilon)O_y(\epsilon)=\epsilon^2[L_x,L_y]$ with the given passive matrices equals $-i\epsilon^2L_z=\begin{pmatrix}0&\epsilon^2&0\\-\epsilon^2&0&0\\0&0&0\end{pmatrix}=O_z(+\epsilon^2)-I_3$, not the displayed $\begin{pmatrix}0&-\epsilon^2&0\\\epsilon^2&0&0\\0&0&0\end{pmatrix}$ and not $O_z(-\epsilon^2)-I_3$.
- [[#N2093|N2093]] Spatial rotations and the angular momentum generators: The physical-quantities table lists $\mechanical{L}$ both as "Box side length" (m) and as orbital angular momentum, and includes symbols the note never uses ($\mathbf p,\mathbf p'$, $c$, emission coefficients $A,B$); remove them and add the dimensionless generators $L_i,T_a,J_i$, $O$, $D(R)$, $\boldsymbol\omega$, $\ell,m$.
- [[#N2102|N2102]] Spin in magnetic fields and atomic Zeeman splitting: The physical-quantities table lists $\mechanical{v}$ twice (particle speed and molar volume) and $A,B$ twice (emission coefficients and virial coefficients), includes unused symbols ($\mechanical t_0$, $\Delta\mechanical t$, oscillator $\mechanical x$, $E$ in N, box length $\mechanical L$, $\Delta E,\delta E$), and omits the spin-coupling constant $A$, $a,\tilde a$, $b_i$, $g$, $g_J$, $\mu_B$, $m_j$, $\chi$, $R_{n\ell}$; rebuild it and rename the spin-coupling constant to avoid the clash with $\magnetic{\mathbf A}$ and the virial $A(T)$.
- [[#N2103|N2103]] Unitary rotations of spinors and Pauli matrices: The Physical quantities table lists symbols the note never uses ($\mechanical{L}$ as "Box side length", $c$, and $A$, $B$ as mode emission/absorption coefficients); $\mechanical{L}$ as a length also clashes with the orbital angular momentum $\mechanical{\mathbf L}$ in the same table. Remove these rows.
- [[#N2103|N2103]] Unitary rotations of spinors and Pauli matrices: In "Spinor rotation" the Cartesian rotation is written $O=e^{-i\phi\widehat{\mathbf n}\cdot\mathbf L}$ with dimensionless generators, while the same letter $\mechanical{\mathbf L}$ is the dimensionful orbital operator elsewhere in the note; rename the $3\times3$ generators (e.g. $\mathcal J_i$) or write $e^{-i\phi\widehat{\mathbf n}\cdot\mechanical{\mathbf L}/\hbar}$.
- [[#N2114|N2114]] 11.10 Addition of Angular Momentum Exercises: Exercise 10 calls the ladder relation the "Racah recurrence"; the Racah formula is the closed-form expression for CG coefficients, while this is the standard ladder recursion relation. Rename it.

Rebuild the table from the symbols actually used.
- [[#N2115|N2115]] Coupled angular momentum and Clebsch–Gordan calculations: "measured to about ten significant figures" is outdated: the 2023 Northwestern measurement gives $g/2=1.00115965218059(13)$ (0.13 ppt), about 14 significant figures; also drop the quoted wrong handwritten estimate $(\alpha/4\pi)^2$ and keep only $g-2=\alpha/\pi+O(\alpha^2)$.

- [[#N2126|N2126]] Atomic spectra and wave mechanics review problems: Electron in an infinite well: $h^2/(8m_eL^2)$ with $L=0.100\,\mathrm{nm}$ gives $6.02\times10^{-18}\,\mathrm J=37.6\,\mathrm{eV}$, not $37.7\,\mathrm{eV}$; the derived levels should be $E_2=150.4$, $E_3=338.4$, and $E_4=601.6\,\mathrm{eV}$.

- [[#N2128|N2128]] Three-dimensional wells and hydrogen wavefunctions: Physical quantities table: $R,T$ are listed as reflection and transmission coefficients, but here $R$ is the radial (or spatial) function and $T(t)$ the time factor, and $Z$ is listed as atomic number but only appears as the Cartesian factor $Z(z)$; fix those rows and add $m$, $\ell$, $Y_\ell^m$, $P_\ell^m$, $j_\ell$, $n_\ell$, $\beta_{n\ell}$, $a$, and $u$.

- [[#N2251|N2251]] Quantum rotations, unitarity, and course review calculations: Semantic macros: the complex-plane helper variables $\rho$, $\varphi$, $y$ and the short time step $\epsilon$ are wrapped in the mechanical macro, while $\hbar$ is left uncolored throughout; use $\mechanical{\hbar}$ as in the rest of the course and keep contour coordinates uncolored.
- [[#N2252|N2252]] Hamiltonian of the Hydrogen Atom: Relativistic correction: $\hat H_{\mathrm{rel}}=-\frac{\hbar^2}{8\mu^2c^2}\nabla^4$ has the wrong dimension; the correct form is $\hat H_{\mathrm{rel}}=-\hat p^4/(8m^3c^2)=-\frac{\hbar^4}{8m^3c^2}\nabla^4$.
- [[#N2252|N2252]] Hamiltonian of the Hydrogen Atom: Spin–orbit term: $\frac{e\hbar}{2\mu c^2r}\mathbf L\cdot\mathbf S$ is not an energy; the SI form is $\hat H_{\mathrm{so}}=\frac{e^2}{8\pi\varepsilon_0m^2c^2r^3}\hat{\mathbf L}\cdot\hat{\mathbf S}$ (including the Thomas factor 1/2).
- [[#N2252|N2252]] Hamiltonian of the Hydrogen Atom: Darwin term: $\frac{e^2\hbar^2}{8\mu c^2\epsilon_0}\delta(\mathbf r)$ is missing a mass factor; the correct form is $\hat H_D=\frac{e^2\hbar^2}{8\varepsilon_0m^2c^2}\delta^3(\mathbf r)$. - [[#N2263|N2263]] 01.04.02 Plane-Wave Solutions: In (1.14) and (1.15) the measure is $d^{3}\mechanical{k}$ while the integrand depends only on $\mechanical{\mathbf p}$, so the integrals are ill-formed as written; write $\int d^{3}\mechanical{p}/(2\pi)^3\,1/(2\energy{\omega}_{\mathbf p})$ and delete the explanatory callout.

- [[#N2281|N2281]] 01.08.01 From Particles to Fields: In (1.64) the measure is $d^{3}\mechanical{k}$ but the integrand depends on $\mechanical{\mathbf p}$; as written the integral is ill-formed; use $d^{3}\mechanical{p}$ and drop the callout.

- [[#N2286|N2286]] 01.09.01 The Beginnings (1925–1932): "In 1925, Born and Jordan showed that the quantized harmonic oscillator ... could be described with creation and annihilation operators" is misattributed: Born–Jordan (1925) established the matrix-mechanics commutator; the first field quantization (a vibrating string as a set of oscillators) is the Born–Heisenberg–Jordan paper (1926), and creation/annihilation operators for the radiation field were introduced by Dirac (1927).
- [[#N2296|N2296]] 01.12.01 Natural units and conversions: Part (c): with the stated inputs $1.0546\times10^{-34}$, $2.998\times10^{8}$ and $1.602\times10^{-13}$ the result is $197.36\approx197.4\,\mathrm{MeV\,fm}$, not $197.3$; use $1.602177\times10^{-13}\,\mathrm{J/MeV}$ (and $\hbar=1.054572\times10^{-34}\,\mathrm{J\,s}$) to obtain $197.33\,\mathrm{MeV\,fm}$.

- [[#N2321|N2321]] 02.05.04 Rotations and Angular Momentum: "a vector has $\Delta\signal{A}^{\mu}=-\omega^{\mu}{}_{\nu}\signal{A}^{\nu}$" is inconsistent with $\mechanical{x}^\mu\to\mechanical{x}^\mu+\omega^\mu{}_\nu\mechanical{x}^\nu$ (and with 02.08.04, whose vector generator gives $+\omega^\mu{}_\nu$); write $\Delta\signal{A}^\mu=+\omega^\mu{}_\nu\signal{A}^\nu$ and delete the correcting callout.
- [[#N2324|N2324]] 02.06.02 The Belinfante–Rosenfeld Tensor: Eq. - [[#N2327|N2327]] 02.07.02 The Complex Scalar Field: "The source writes $O(2)\cong U(1)$" is kept in the text with a correcting callout; state directly that the phase rotation is $SO(2)\cong U(1)$ (the full $O(2)$ also contains the reflection $\signal{\phi}\to\signal{\phi}^*$) and remove the callout.
