- [[#N3191|N3191]] 7.11 The Hierarchy Problem: "$\mechanical{M_{\mathrm{Pl}}}=(\hbar\mechanical{c}/G_{\mathrm{N}})^{1/2}\approx1.2\times10^{19}\,\unit{GeV}$" mixes units: with the SI units in the table $(\hbar c/G_N)^{1/2}$ is a mass ($2.18\times10^{-8}$ kg); write $\mechanical{M_{\mathrm{Pl}}}c^2=(\hbar c^5/G_N)^{1/2}\approx1.22\times10^{19}\,\unit{GeV}$ or state natural units.
- [[#N3192|N3192]] 7.12 The Vacuum Energy Problem: Intro: the gravitational to electrostatic attraction ratio for an electron and a proton is $Gm_em_p/(e^2/4\pi\varepsilon_0)\approx4.4\times10^{-40}$, so it is about 39 to 40 orders of magnitude smaller, not 41. Correct the number or give the explicit ratio.
- [[#N3194|N3194]] 7.2 Electroweak Gauge Bosons: Eq. 7.2.11, first line: "$3[2\cdot\Gamma(Z^0\to u\bar u)+3\cdot\Gamma(Z^0\to d\bar d)]$" mixes widths into a dimensionless ratio, and it double-counts color because $\Gamma(Z^0\to q\bar q)$ in 7.2.10 already contains the factor 3. Write $3[2(L_u^2+R_u^2)+3(L_d^2+R_d^2)]$, or equivalently $[2\Gamma(u\bar u)+3\Gamma(d\bar d)]/\Gamma(\nu\bar\nu)$.
- [[#N3195|N3195]] 7.3 Electron-Positron Annihilations: Eq. 7.3.10: "$1-\frac{8x_W}{3}+\frac{32x_W^2}{3}$" should be $1-\frac{8x_W}{3}+\frac{32x_W^2}{9}$, as in 7.2.11 and 7.3.19b. With $/3$, $R_{\mathrm{peak}}^{(u\bar u)}$ becomes 1066 instead of the tabulated 693.
- [[#N3195|N3195]] 7.3 Electron-Positron Annihilations: Text before 7.3.14: "$(R_i-L_i)=\tau_3^{(i)}$" has the wrong sign. With $L_e=-1+2x_W$ and $R_e=2x_W$, one gets $R_e-L_e=+1$ while $\tau_3^{(e)}=-1$, so it must read $(R_i-L_i)=-\tau_3^{(i)}$, which is consistent with 7.3.14 as written.
- [[#N3196|N3196]] 7.4 Deeply Inelastic Lepton-Hadron Scattering: (7.4.70) has prefactor $\frac{G_F^2}{2\pi}\energy{E'}\energy{E}$, which gives $\unit{GeV}^{-3}$ instead of $\unit{GeV}^{-5}$ for $d^2\sigma/dQ^2d\nu$ (with $W_i\sim\unit{GeV}^{-1}$); it must be $\frac{G_F^2}{2\pi}\frac{\energy{E'}}{\energy{E}}$, matching (7.4.27) and the Jacobian $2ME^2y$ that leads to (7.4.71).
- [[#N3196|N3196]] 7.4 Deeply Inelastic Lepton-Hadron Scattering: (7.4.97) $A/Q^2\simeq-7.2\times10^{-5}$ is missing its unit: it should read $-7.2\times10^{-5}\,\unit{GeV}^{-2}$ (recomputed: $G_F\cdot\frac45/(4\pi\alpha\sqrt2)=7.19\times10^{-5}\,\unit{GeV}^{-2}$).
- [[#N3196|N3196]] 7.4 Deeply Inelastic Lepton-Hadron Scattering: Symbol slips: the table defines $N$ only as "parton count", but the note also uses $N$ for the target nucleon in (7.4.1), (7.4.69), (7.4.85)-(7.4.89); in (7.4.28) one form factor is written $\Gamma_2^2(\mechanical{q}^2)$ while all the others take $\mechanical{Q}^2$; the rule (7.4.47) needs an absolute value, $1/|\partial h/\partial x|$.
- [[#N3196|N3196]] 7.4 Deeply Inelastic Lepton-Hadron Scattering: The world average $M_W=80.399\pm0.023\,\unit{GeV}$ (PDG 2010) near the end is outdated; add an editorial note giving the current PDG value ($80.369\pm0.013\,\unit{GeV}$, PDG 2024) and mark "most precise to date" and "recent" (BoNuS, HERA) as statements made at the source's date.
- [[#N3197|N3197]] 7.5 Hadron-Hadron Interactions: Eq. (7.5.9) has the wrong Jacobian: $\partial(x,\tau)/\partial(x_a,x_b)=x_a+x_b=(x^2+4\tau)^{1/2}$, so it should read $F(\tau,x)=x_ax_b\,g(x_a,x_b)/(x^2+4\tau)^{1/2}$. Only with the square root does integrating over $x$ give (7.5.11) and the standard $d^2\sigma/dM^2dx_F=(4\pi\alpha^2/9M^4)\,x_ax_b/(x_a+x_b)\sum e_i^2[\dots]$.
- [[#N3197|N3197]] 7.5 Hadron-Hadron Interactions: In the paragraph after (7.5.15), "studying $1.96$-GeV proton–antiproton collisions" should say $1.96\,\mathrm{TeV}$. In the Fig. 7.17 caption, CMS stands for "Compact Muon Solenoid", not "Compact Muon Spectrometer".
- [[#N3197|N3197]] 7.5 Hadron-Hadron Interactions: Several values are out of date and should be marked as 2012 values or updated: the LHC has run at $13$ and $13.6\,\mathrm{TeV}$; the PDG 2024 average is $M_W=80.369\pm0.013\,\mathrm{GeV}$ (CDF 2022 reported $80.434\pm0.009$); the sequential $W'$ is now excluded below about $6\,\mathrm{TeV}$ and the sequential $Z'$ below about $5\,\mathrm{TeV}$ (ATLAS/CMS full Run 2), not "$>2\,\mathrm{TeV}$".
- [[#N3198|N3198]] 7.6 Further Tests of the Electroweak Theory: Paragraph 3: "$B(B_s\to\mu^+\mu^-)<(3.5\pm0.2)\times10^{-9}$" is the standard-model expectation, not a bound, so the "$<$" with an uncertainty is wrong. Write the SM value with "$=$" and give the 2012 bound separately. Also note that $B_s\to\mu^+\mu^-$ has since been observed (world average about $3.3\times10^{-9}$, consistent with the SM value $\approx3.66\times10^{-9}$).
- [[#N3198|N3198]] 7.6 Further Tests of the Electroweak Theory: "departures from the CMK paradigm" should read "CKM".
- [[#N3198|N3198]] 7.6 Further Tests of the Electroweak Theory: Several statements are outdated: the first-row sum is now $\mathcal S_u\approx0.9985\pm0.0007$ (PDG 2024, the "Cabibbo-angle anomaly"), not $0.9999\pm0.0006$; CP violation in charm was established by LHCb in 2019 ($\Delta A_{CP}\approx-1.5\times10^{-3}$); top FCNC limits are now about $10^{-5}$–$10^{-4}$; a sequential fourth generation is excluded by the measured Higgs production rate. Add a dated "status update" callout.
- [[#N3199|N3199]] 7.7 A Brief Look at Quantum Corrections: The values have been superseded: the 2023 Northwestern measurement gives electron $g/2=1.001\,159\,652\,180\,59(13)$, and QED is now known through $(\alpha/\pi)^5$; $m_t=172.57\pm0.29\,\mathrm{GeV}$ (PDG 2024) rather than $173.2\pm0.9$; the Higgs boson has been found at $M_H=125.20\pm0.11\,\mathrm{GeV}$, so the fit discussion around Fig. 7.22 should say that the fitted $92^{+34}_{-26}$ GeV is consistent with it at about $1\sigma$.
- [[#N3200|N3200]] 7.8 The Scale of Fermion Masses: The last paragraph ("Until the Higgs boson is discovered and shown to couple to fermion pairs…") is outdated. Since 2012–2020, Higgs couplings to $t$, $b$, $\tau$ and $\mu$ have been observed and found proportional to mass, while the $He\bar e$ coupling is still unestablished. Add a dated update note.
- [[#N3201|N3201]] 7.9 Search for the Higgs Boson: Add a dated update callout: $M_H=125.20\pm0.11\,\mathrm{GeV}$ (PDG 2024); spin-parity $0^+$ is established (not just "even-integer spin"); $H\to b\bar b$, $\tau\tau$, $\mu\mu$ and $t\bar tH$ have been observed; a fourth generation, which the text says "would raise the $gg\to H$ rate", is excluded by exactly that rate.
- [[#N3203|N3203]] 7.P Problems: Problem 7.3(a): "Express $V_{ub}=A\lambda^2$" should be "$V_{cb}=A\lambda^2$". The next sentence then correctly sets $V_{ub}=0$, and part (b) assigns $s_{23}=A\lambda^2$, i.e. $V_{cb}$.
- [[#N3203|N3203]] 7.P Problems: Problem 7.4: "(for $j\ne k$ and $i\ne j$, respectively)" should be "$i\ne k$", since the second condition is $\sum_jV_{ij}V_{kj}^*=\delta_{ik}$.
- [[#N3203|N3203]] 7.P Problems: Problem 7.19 has two parts labelled "(b)"; the second, on $\delta p/p$, should be "(c)". Also add the missing comma in "$e^+e^-$ $\mu^+\mu^-$".
- [[#N3206|N3206]] 8.1 A Color Gauge Theory: Eq. (8.1.20): the left side reads $\sum_{i<j}\langle\mathbf T^{(i)}\cdot\mathbf T^{(i)}\rangle$ and should be $\sum_{i<j}\langle\mathbf T^{(i)}\cdot\mathbf T^{(j)}\rangle$.
- [[#N3208|N3208]] 8.11 Strong-Interaction Symmetries: Discussion of the U(1) problem: "the obvious candidate, $\eta(958)$" should be $\eta'(958)$. The $\eta$ is at 548 MeV.
- [[#N3208|N3208]] 8.11 Strong-Interaction Symmetries: Eqs. (8.11.10) and (8.11.11) are inconsistent. For the $e^{in\theta}$ weighting of (8.11.9) to be reproduced, the action $\int d^4x\,\mathcal L_\theta$ must equal $n\theta$, so the coefficients must match: $1/8\pi^2$ in $n$ requires $\theta/8\pi^2$ in $\mathcal L_\theta$, not $\theta/16\pi^2$. With the unrescaled fields of (8.1.4)–(8.1.6), both also need a factor $g^2$. The standard forms are $n=\frac{g^2}{16\pi^2}\int d^4x\,\mathrm{tr}\,G\tilde G$ and $\mathcal L_\theta=\frac{\theta g^2}{16\pi^2}\mathrm{tr}\,G\tilde G$ with $\tilde G^{\mu\nu}=\tfrac12\epsilon^{\mu\nu\alpha\beta}G_{\alpha\beta}$.
- [[#N3208|N3208]] 8.11 Strong-Interaction Symmetries: The last paragraph says the new U(1) "is spontaneously broken in the course of electroweak symmetry breaking". That is the original Peccei–Quinn–Weinberg–Wilczek axion, which was excluded long ago. Viable "invisible" axions (KSVZ, DFSZ) break the PQ symmetry at $f_a\gg v$, and $\bar\theta$ relaxes to zero through the axion potential. Also introduce $\bar\theta=\theta+\arg\det M_q$ explicitly, since the text mentions that the two phases combine.
- [[#N3208|N3208]] 8.11 Strong-Interaction Symmetries: The nEDM limit in (8.11.12) is outdated: the current bound is $|d_n|<1.8\times10^{-26}\,e\,\mathrm{cm}$ (90% CL, PSI 2020). It still gives $|\bar\theta|\lesssim10^{-10}$.
- [[#N3209|N3209]] 8.12 Assessment: AdS/CFT paragraph: "$\mathrm{AdS}^5\otimes S_5$" should read $\mathrm{AdS}_5\times S^5$ (five-dimensional anti-de Sitter space times the five-sphere), as the bracketed gloss itself says.
- [[#N3210|N3210]] 8.2 Charge Renormalization in Electrodynamics: (8.2.12): the $z_1$ exponent is printed as $iz_1(k^2-m^2-i\epsilon)$; it must be $+i\epsilon$, as in (8.2.11) and as used in (8.2.16), where $-(m^2-i\epsilon)(z_1+z_2)$ appears.
- [[#N3210|N3210]] 8.2 Charge Renormalization in Electrodynamics: (8.2.27) still carries $i\sigma$ in the exponent although $\sigma=1$ was already set (it should be $\exp\{i[q^2z_1z_2/(z_1+z_2)-(M_i^2-i\epsilon)(z_1+z_2)]\}$), and (8.2.28) reads $\delta(\sigma-x_1-x_2)$ where it should be $\delta(\sigma-z_1-z_2)$.
- [[#N3210|N3210]] 8.2 Charge Renormalization in Electrodynamics: Sign of (8.2.51)–(8.2.53): the $-e^2$ in (8.2.44) and $\int d^nl\,e^{il^2z}/(2\pi)^n=ie^{-i\pi n/4}/(4\pi z)^{n/2}$ give the prefactor $-ie^2e^{-i\pi n/4}/(4\pi)^{n/2}$, so the pole term is $+\frac{ie^2}{16\pi^2}(q^\mu q^\nu-q^2g^{\mu\nu})\frac{2}{4-n}\int(1-2z)^2$. As printed, the expansion $\Gamma(2-n/2)X^{n/2-2}=\frac{2}{4-n}-\ln X$ gives a log term with the opposite sign to (8.2.54). (8.2.54)–(8.2.56) themselves are correct.
- [[#N3210|N3210]] 8.2 Charge Renormalization in Electrodynamics: Symbol clash: $\epsilon$ denotes both the dielectric constant $\electric{\epsilon}$ (8.2.1) and the Feynman $i\epsilon$ in every propagator. Rename one, for example $\varepsilon_{\mathrm r}$ for the dielectric constant, and fix "the effective electric charges increases" after (8.2.36).
- [[#N3211|N3211]] 8.3 The Running Coupling Constant in QCD: Symbol clash for $\alpha$: it is the gauge function $\alpha(x)$ in (3.5.14)/(8.3.6), quark color indices $\alpha,\beta,\gamma$ in (8.3.9) and (8.3.19)–(8.3.22), and part of $\alpha_s$. Also, the ghost is called a color octet, yet (8.3.14) gives it triplet-style indices $\alpha,\beta$; use adjoint indices $a,b$ there.
- [[#N3212|N3212]] 8.4 Perturbative QCD -  A First Example: After (8.4.3): "which vanishes in the soft-gluon limit … also vanishes if $k\cdot q_i=0$" is backwards. The denominator $k^2+2q_i\cdot k$ vanishes, so the propagator diverges; that divergence is the soft and collinear singularity.
- [[#N3212|N3212]] 8.4 Perturbative QCD -  A First Example: The physical-quantities table lists $p_1,p_2$, which the note never uses. $\theta$ is used both for the step function in (8.4.1) and for the angles $\theta_{1g},\theta_{2g}$ in (8.4.12). Also fix "three-jet cross differential cross section".
- [[#N3213|N3213]] 8.5 QCD Corrections to Deeply Inelastic Scattering: (8.5.49): the third term must be $1/[(n+1)(n+2)]$, not $1/[n(n+1)(n+2)]$, since $\int_0^1z^{n-1}z(1-z)\,dz=1/[(n+1)(n+2)]$. Check: only the corrected form gives $A_2(g\leftarrow g)=-n_f/3$, as required by (8.5.27) and used in (8.5.70); the printed form gives $-1/4-n_f/3$.
- [[#N3213|N3213]] 8.5 QCD Corrections to Deeply Inelastic Scattering: (8.5.75): the momentum fraction per quark or antiquark species is $\Sigma_2^\infty/(2n_f)=\frac{9/17}{12}=\frac{3}{68}$, not $\tfrac12\Sigma_2^\infty$ (which would be $9/34$). The numerical value $3/68$ and the check (8.5.77) are correct.
- [[#N3213|N3213]] 8.5 QCD Corrections to Deeply Inelastic Scattering: (8.5.50)/(8.5.51): with (7.4.86)–(7.4.87), where $u(x)$ is a number density, the cross-section difference gives $x\mathcal F_3=x[u-\bar u+d-\bar d]$, so the first line is missing a factor $x$. The nonsinglet moment should then be $\Delta_n=\int_0^1dx\,x^{n-1}\mathcal F_3=\int_0^1dx\,x^{n-1}(q-\bar q)$, so that $\Delta_1$ counts valence quarks, consistent with $A_1=0$ expressing fermion-number conservation.
- [[#N3213|N3213]] 8.5 QCD Corrections to Deeply Inelastic Scattering: Several typos: (8.5.53) the denominator should be $\ln(\Delta_k(\tau)/\Delta_k(0))$, not $\Delta_n(0)$; in (8.5.67) $F_2(x,Q^2)$ inside $\int_x^1du/u^3$ must be $F_2(u,Q^2)$; (8.5.10)–(8.5.11) write $(x,t)$ for $(x,\tau)$; "the beam prepared in (8.27)" should say figure 8.27. Also $y$ is both the parent momentum fraction in (8.5.5) and the inelasticity in (8.5.62), and the table lists it twice; rename one.
- [[#N3214|N3214]] 8.6 Jets in Hadron-Hadron Collisions: Physical-quantities table: with dimensionless number densities $f_i$ and the left side of (8.6.3) in $\mathrm{GeV}^{-3}$, the prefactor $2\pi p_\perp/s$ (in $\mathrm{GeV}^{-1}$) requires $\hat\sigma_{ij}$ in $\mathrm{GeV}^{-2}$, not $\mathrm{GeV}^{-4}$. Correct the unit, or state that $\hat\sigma_{ij}$ is the Owens–Reya–Glück scaled form $\hat s\,d\hat\sigma/(\pi\,d\hat t)$.
- [[#N3214|N3214]] 8.6 Jets in Hadron-Hadron Collisions: The text calls figure 8.37 "the doubly differential dijet cross section", but the caption (and the figure) show the inclusive jet cross section against $p_\perp$ in rapidity bins. Make them consistent.
- [[#N3215|N3215]] 8.7 Two-Photon Processes and the Photon-Structure Function: (8.7.32): each $q_i$ and $\bar q_i$ receives a photon source $\propto e_i^2$, so $d\Sigma/d\tau\supset2\sum_ie_i^2$ and $\Delta^{(i)}$ gets $e_i^2-\frac{1}{n_f}\sum_je_j^2$. For (8.7.31) and (8.7.33) to agree, $\langle e^2\rangle$ must be $\frac{1}{n_f}\sum_ie_i^2$, not $\frac{1}{2n_f}\sum_ie_i^2$. The table's "printed flavor sum" wording hints at this.
- [[#N3215|N3215]] 8.7 Two-Photon Processes and the Photon-Structure Function: Integrand arguments: in (8.7.31), $\Delta^{(i)}(x,\tau)$ inside $\int_x^1dy/y$ should be $\Delta^{(i)}(y,\tau)$; in (8.7.33), $\gamma(x,\tau)$ and $\Sigma(x,\tau)$ should be $\gamma(y,\tau)$ and $\Sigma(y,\tau)$. "Taking moments of (8.7.30)" should refer to (8.7.31).
- [[#N3215|N3215]] 8.7 Two-Photon Processes and the Photon-Structure Function: Symbol clash: $y$ is the inelasticity in (8.7.18) and (8.7.20) and the convolution variable in (8.7.22)–(8.7.33); $x$ is also the argument of the flux factor $f(x)$ in (8.7.3). Rename the convolution variable, for example $\xi$.
- [[#N3216|N3216]] 8.8 Color Confinement: (8.8.6): in the Gaussian units used throughout ($W=\frac1{8\pi}\int D\cdot E$, $\sigma=(1-\epsilon)D/4\pi\epsilon$), the relation is $\mathbf D=\mathbf E+4\pi\mathbf P$, not $\mathbf D=\mathbf E+\mathbf P$.
- [[#N3216|N3216]] 8.8 Color Confinement: Figure 8.47 caption: the lattice temperature is $T=1/(aN_\tau)$, not $a/N_\tau$; the latter has units of length (the table gives $a$ in $\mathrm{GeV}^{-1}$).
- [[#N3217|N3217]] 8.9 QCD-induced Electroweak Symmetry Breaking: (8.9.4): with off-diagonal $+gg'$, the massless eigenvector in $(b_3,\mathcal A)$ is $\propto(g',-g)$, i.e. $A\propto g'b_3-g\mathcal A$, which contradicts the stated $A=(g\mathcal A+g'b_3)/\sqrt{g^2+g'^2}$ and $Z=(gb_3-g'\mathcal A)/\sqrt{g^2+g'^2}$. For those eigenvectors (and $Q=T_3+Y/2$), the off-diagonal entries must be $-gg'$.
- [[#N3219|N3219]] 8.P Problems: Problem 8.4: right after defining $V(r)=\frac{\alpha_s}{r}\langle\mathbf T^{(1)}\cdot\mathbf T^{(2)}\rangle$, the four potentials are printed as $-\frac43\alpha_s r$, $+\frac16\alpha_s r$, $-\frac23\alpha_s r$, $+\frac13\alpha_s r$. They must be $-\frac43\alpha_s/r$, $+\frac16\alpha_s/r$, $-\frac23\alpha_s/r$, $+\frac13\alpha_s/r$.
- [[#N3219|N3219]] 8.P Problems: Problem 8.5 table: the single box is the $6$ of $\mathrm{SU}(6)$ with $(3,2)$ and $G^2=35/12$, not dimension "1". Also, the embedded pair images are swapped relative to their content: the $21$ [$(6,3)\oplus(3^*,1)$, $G^2=20/3$] is the symmetric (horizontal) pair, and the $15$ [$G^2=14/3$] is the antisymmetric (vertical) pair, as the filenames vertical-pair and horizontal-pair indicate the opposite.
- [[#N3219|N3219]] 8.P Problems: Problem 8.22 table: at $90^\circ$, $\hat\sigma(gg\to q\bar q)/\hat\sigma(ud\to ud)=\frac{7/48}{20/9}=\frac{21}{320}\approx0.066$, not $\approx0.66$. All other ratios check (0.1, 22/15, 7/6, 7/15, 11/4, 2187/160).
- [[#N3219|N3219]] 8.P Problems: Problem 8.10 cites "the Feynman rules for the Faddeev–Popov ghost given in figure 8.10". Figure 8.10 is the dielectric polarization; the ghost vertex is figure 8.17.
- [[#N3219|N3219]] 8.P Problems: Problem 8.27(c): $\sum_{i=u,d,s}e_i^4=2/9$; the quoted $2/3$ includes the color factor and should read $3\sum_ie_i^4=2/3$. The Han–Nambu citation should be *Phys. Rev.* **139**, B1006 (1965), not "149B, 1006".
- [[#N3219|N3219]] 8.P Problems: Problem 8.9: for the attractive Coulomb potential $-\alpha/r$, the factor $1+\alpha|\mathbf q|^2/(15\pi m^2)$ yields the contact term $-\frac{4\alpha_{\mathrm R}^2}{15m^2}\delta^3(\mathbf x)$. The printed $\frac{4}{15}\frac{\alpha_{\mathrm R}}{m^2}\delta^3(\mathbf x)$ is missing one power of $\alpha_{\mathrm R}$ and the sign.
- [[#N3220|N3220]] 8.R For Further Reading: HQET list: the second Eichten–Hill paper is *Phys. Lett.* **B243**, 427 (1990), not "*Phys. Rev.* **B243**".
- [[#N3223|N3223]] 9.2 The SU(5) Model: (9.2.19), hypercharge term: the coefficient must be $-\frac{g_5}{2}\sqrt{\frac35}\,\mathcal A_\mu\sum\bar f\gamma^\mu Yf$ (i.e. $-\frac{g'}{2}$), not $-\frac{g_5}{2}\frac35$, to agree with (9.2.21) $g'=g_5\sqrt{3/5}$ and (9.2.26).
- [[#N3223|N3223]] 9.2 The SU(5) Model: Outdated bounds and status: (9.2.28) should be updated to Super-Kamiokande (2020), $\tau/B(p\to e^+\pi^0)>2.4\times10^{34}\,\mathrm{yr}$ and $\tau/B(p\to\mu^+\pi^0)>1.6\times10^{34}\,\mathrm{yr}$. (9.2.29) has been superseded by SNO+ ($\sim10^{30}\,\mathrm{yr}$ for invisible proton decay). "the normal Higgs scalar $H^0$, still with unknown mass" should note $M_H\approx125\,\mathrm{GeV}$ (2012).
- [[#N3224|N3224]] 9.3 Coupling-Constant Unification: In (9.3.9), with the vault convention $Q=I_3+\tfrac12 Y$ of (6.3.6), $\tfrac12[\operatorname{tr}(Y_{\mathrm L}^2)+\operatorname{tr}(Y_{\mathrm R}^2)]=20/3$ per generation, not $5/3$; the traces must be of $(Y/2)^2$, i.e. write $\tfrac12[\operatorname{tr}(Y_{\mathrm L}/2)^2+\operatorname{tr}(Y_{\mathrm R}/2)^2]=\tfrac53 n_g$ so that $4\pi b_Y=-20n_g/9$ follows.
- [[#N3224|N3224]] 9.3 Coupling-Constant Unification: (9.3.15): solving (9.3.13) with $\alpha^{-1}=128.957$, $\alpha_s^{-1}=8.446$ gives $\mechanical{u}=1.45\times10^{15}\,\mathrm{GeV}$ ($\log_{10}u=15.161$, exactly the endpoint used in Fig. 9.3), not $1.44\times10^{15}$; state 1.45 or note the rounding.
- [[#N3224|N3224]] 9.3 Coupling-Constant Unification: Inputs are dated: current PDG values are $\alpha_s(M_Z^2)=0.1180\pm0.0009$, $M_Z=91.1876\,\mathrm{GeV}$, and $M_W\approx80.37\,\mathrm{GeV}$ gives $x_W^{(\mathrm{os})}=1-M_W^2/M_Z^2\approx0.2232$ rather than 0.2226 in (9.3.22); add a dated-values callout and recompute $u$ and (9.3.21).
- [[#N3225|N3225]] 9.4 Nucleon Decay: "Super-Kamiokande ... has a fiducial volume of $32{,}000\,\mathrm{m^3}$": 32 kt is the inner-detector volume; the standard fiducial volume is 22.5 kt ($22{,}500\,\mathrm{m^3}$) of the 50 kt tank.
- [[#N3225|N3225]] 9.4 Nucleon Decay: The bound $8.2\times10^{33}$ yr for $p\to e^+\pi^0$ is superseded: Super-K (2020) gives $\tau/B>2.4\times10^{34}$ yr, so (9.4.14) is now more than 100 times below the limit; update the sentence and the "megaton-class detectors" remark (Hyper-Kamiokande and DUNE are under construction).
- [[#N3225|N3225]] 9.4 Nucleon Decay: The physical-quantities table assigns $B$ to both baryon number and branching fraction; rename the branching fraction (e.g. $\mathcal{B}$) in the table and in the Fig. 9.5 caption.
- [[#N3226|N3226]] 9.5 The Baryon Number of the Universe: With the convention (9.5.9) $S_{ba}=S(a\to b)$, (9.5.10) $(SS^\dagger)_{aa}=\sum_i S_{ai}S^*_{ai}=\sum_i\lvert S(i\to a)\rvert^2$, whereas $\sum_i\lvert S(a\to i)\rvert^2$ is $(S^\dagger S)_{aa}$; relabel the first line (both equal 1, so the conclusion stands).
- [[#N3226|N3226]] 9.5 The Baryon Number of the Universe: (9.5.1) is outdated: Planck CMB plus BBN give $\eta=n_B/n_\gamma=(6.1\pm0.04)\times10^{-10}$; add the current value next to the source range.
- [[#N3227|N3227]] 9.6 The Problem of Fermion Masses: Subtracting (9.6.4) from (9.6.3) gives $+\frac{3}{20n_f}+\frac{27}{20n_f}=+\frac{3}{2n_f}$, so (9.6.5) must read $+\frac{3}{2n_f}\ln(\alpha_1(\mu^2)/\alpha_u)$, not $-\frac{3}{2n_f}$; only the plus sign reproduces $m_b/m_\tau=e^{(4/7)\ln8-(1/4)\ln(65/40)}=2.91$, while the printed minus gives 3.70.
- [[#N3233|N3233]] A.1 Four-Vectors and Scalar Product: The letter $x$ denotes both the four-vector $x^\mu$ and its first spatial component in (A.1.1), and $x^2$ means the invariant (A.1.4) while $x^2$ with an index means a component; note this explicitly or write the spatial components as $x^1,x^2,x^3$ only.
- [[#N3236|N3236]] A.4 Dirac Equation and Dirac Spinors: Symbol clashes: $\lambda$ is the helicity label and also the Fierz matrix $\lambda_{ij}$ in (A.4.30), and $\mu$ is a helicity label in (A.4.7)–(A.4.9) as well as a Lorentz index; use e.g. $\lambda,\lambda'$ for helicities and $C_{ij}$ for the Fierz coefficients.
- [[#N3236|N3236]] A.4 Dirac Equation and Dirac Spinors: The physical-quantities table lists $\mechanical{s}$ twice (as "spin state" and as polarization four-vector); merge into one row for the polarization four-vector.
- [[#N3237|N3237]] A.5 Color Algebra: (A.5.19): with $[T^b,T^c]=if^{bcd}T^d$ and $f^{abc}f^{dbc}=N\delta^{ad}$, $if^{abc}T^bT^c=\tfrac{i}{2}f^{abc}[T^b,T^c]=-\tfrac{N}{2}T^a$, not $+\tfrac{C_A}{2}T^a$; either correct the sign or state that the vertex factor is taken as $-if^{abc}$ in this diagram.
- [[#N3242|N3242]] B.1 Phase-Space Formulas -  Decay Rates and Cross Sections: (B.1.4) must read $d\Gamma/d\Omega_{\mathrm{cm}}=\lvert\mathcal M\rvert^2 S_{12}/(64\pi^2 m_\alpha^3)\cdot S$ (equivalently $\lvert\mathcal M\rvert^2\lvert\mathbf p\rvert/(32\pi^2m_\alpha^2)$); with $m_\alpha^2$ the right side has dimension $\mathrm{GeV}^2$ instead of GeV.
- [[#N3242|N3242]] B.1 Phase-Space Formulas -  Decay Rates and Cross Sections: $S$ denotes the statistical weight and $S_{12},S_{34}$ the kinematic factor; rename one (e.g. $\lambda^{1/2}_{12}$ for the kinematic factor) to avoid the clash.
- [[#N3243|N3243]] B.2 Feynman Rules -  Generalities: $\epsilon$ is used for the polarization vector and for the $+i\epsilon$ prescription in the propagators; write the infinitesimal as $i0^+$ or $i\eta$.
- [[#N3244|N3244]] B.3 Feynman Integrals: Wick rotation gives $\mathcal I_{mn}=(-1)^{n-m+1}B(m,n-m)/[16\pi^2 i(a^2)^{n-m}]$; the printed form without the sign factor is right for $n-m$ odd (e.g. $m=2,n=3$: $-i/(32\pi^2a^2)$) but wrong for $n-m$ even (e.g. $m=2,n=4$ gives $+i/(96\pi^2a^4)$, not $-i/(96\pi^2a^4)$).
- [[#N3244|N3244]] B.3 Feynman Integrals: $m$ is both a mass ($m_j$, $m_k$ in (B.3.2)) and the power index in (B.3.12) and (B.3.17), and $\lambda$ here is a Schwinger parameter; rename the index (e.g. $r$) to avoid the clash.
- [[#N3252|N3252]] Nuclear and quantum statistics review calculations: The physical-quantities table lists symbols the note does not use with those meanings: $F$ as Faraday constant (the note uses $F_G$, $F_C$ for forces and $F(v)$ for a density), $R$ as activity (the note uses $R$ for nuclear radius, interaction range, and $3R$ gas constant), $T$ "determines the blackbody spectrum", and $\lambda$ only as decay constant (the note uses $\lambda=m/(2k_BT)$ and de Broglie wavelength); rebuild the table from the symbols actually used ($A$, $Z$, $N$, $L$, $m_\ell$, $k_B$, $g(E)$, $f$, $R_{21}$, $a_0$, $C_V$, $N_A$, $R$, $F_G$, $F_C$).
- [[#N3252|N3252]] Nuclear and quantum statistics review calculations: Symbol clashes: $A$ is mass number and also the normalization constant in $f_{\mathrm{MB}}$ and $F(v)=Av^3e^{-\lambda v^2}$; $N$ is neutron number and particle number in $P=(2/3)N\langle E\rangle/V$; rename the normalization constants (e.g. $C$) and the particle count.
- [[#N3254|N3254]] Nuclear mass, decay channels, and dating problems: Neutron-discovery sketch: the recoil protons from paraffin had energies up to about 5.7 MeV (Chadwick 1932), not "5.7 keV"; note the handwritten label as a slip.
- [[#N3254|N3254]] Nuclear mass, decay channels, and dating problems: The physical-quantities table lists $\varepsilon$ as emissivity, but the note only uses $\varepsilon_0$ (vacuum permittivity); also $R$ is activity in the table but the note uses $\mechanical{R}$ for nuclear radius and $R$, $S$ for breakup products, and $N$ for both neutron number and $N(t)$; rename the products and fix the table.
- [[#N3254|N3254]] Nuclear mass, decay channels, and dating problems: Be-8 two-alpha value: $[2(4.002603)-8.005305]\times931.5=-0.0922$ MeV, not $-0.093$ MeV (as correctly given in the review-calculations note).
- [[#N3255|N3255]] Standard Model: Covariant derivative: the SU(2) term must be $-ig\,\tfrac{\tau^i}{2}W^i_\mu$ (generators $T^i=\tau^i/2$), not $-ig\tau^iW^i_\mu$; otherwise $m_W=\tfrac12gv$ is off by a factor 2.
- [[#N3255|N3255]] Standard Model: With $\mathcal L\supset-\mu^2\phi^\dagger\phi-\lambda(\phi^\dagger\phi)^2$ and $\mu^2<0$, the minimum is at $v=\sqrt{-\mu^2/\lambda}$, not $\sqrt{\mu^2/\lambda}$.
- [[#N3255|N3255]] Standard Model: Yukawa terms: "$-\ldots-\text{h.c.}$" makes the Lagrangian anti-Hermitian; write $-(\bar Q_LY_d\phi d_R+\bar Q_LY_u\tilde\phi u_R+\bar L_LY_e\phi e_R+\text{h.c.})$, and fix the Compact Form, whose inner minus signs flip the up-type and lepton terms relative to the Yukawa section.
- [[#N3255|N3255]] Standard Model: Rendering errors: column vectors written as `\begin{pmatrix} u_L \ d_L \end{pmatrix}` (also $L_L$ and $\langle\phi\rangle$) need `\\`, $m_Z=\tfrac12\sqrt{g^2+g'^2},v$ needs `\,v`, and the Higgs doublet mixes Unicode `φ⁺`/`ϕ⁰`; also "left-handed means only one spin orientation" conflates chirality with helicity, and right-handed singlets do couple to the $Z$ via hypercharge.
- [[#N3257|N3257]] Inertial frames, light clocks, and simultaneity problems: The Physical quantities table lists $\mechanical{V}_A,\mechanical{V}_B,\mechanical{V}_C$ (ship speeds) and $\energy{\mathrm{BE}}/A$ (binding energy per nucleon), which this note never uses. Remove both rows.
- [[#N3257|N3257]] Inertial frames, light clocks, and simultaneity problems: Symbol clash for $\tau$: it is a proper interval in "Longitudinal length" ($\tau=t/\gamma$), a clock reading in "Clock synchronization", and the dilated laboratory lifetime in the muon example ($\tau=\gamma\tau_0$). The table also lists $\tau$ in two rows with opposite meanings. Rename the lab lifetime $t_{\mathrm{lab}}$.
- [[#N3257|N3257]] Inertial frames, light clocks, and simultaneity problems: Symbol clash for $L$: in example 4 and "Proper length…", $L$ (or $L_0$) is the Earth-frame proper distance of about 4 light-years, but in "Longitudinal length" $L=D/\gamma$ is the contracted length. Use $L_0$ consistently for the proper length.
- [[#N3257|N3257]] Inertial frames, light clocks, and simultaneity problems: Airplane example: with $v=100$ m/s, $\beta=3.3\times10^{-7}$ gives $\gamma-1=5.6\times10^{-14}$, about 200 ps per hour. Even the rounded $\beta=3\times10^{-7}$ gives $4.5\times10^{-14}\times3600$ s $\approx160$ ps, not "roughly 150 ps". State about 160–200 ps.
- [[#N3258|N3258]] Lorentz transformations and clock comparisons: Macro misuse: the note writes $\mechanical{\Delta x}$, which colors the operator $\Delta$. The preamble rules keep operators uncolored, so write $\Delta\mechanical{x}$. Also, $\gamma$ is uncolored and $c$ uses `\signal`, while the sibling notes use $\mechanical{\gamma}$ and $\mechanical{c}$; align them.
- [[#N3259|N3259]] Lorentz transformations and spacetime diagram problems: The Physical quantities table lists symbols this note never uses: $\tau_0,\tau$ as muon lifetimes, $\Delta t_{\mathrm{rest}}$, $\theta'$, and $\Delta t$ described as the "interferometer travel-time difference". It also omits symbols the note does use: $\mechanical{V}_A,\mechanical{V}_B,\mechanical{V}_C$, $t_{\mathrm f}$, $t_1$, $t_0$ and $\mechanical{v}'$ (upward rod speed). Rebuild the table from this note.
- [[#N3260|N3260]] Proper time and spacetime interval review problems: "Four-position and proper time": $\mechanical{X}_{\mu}=(ct,x,y,z)$ uses a lower index for contravariant components. With signature $(+,-,-,-)$, $X_\mu=(ct,-x,-y,-z)$. Write $X^\mu$.
- [[#N3260|N3260]] Proper time and spacetime interval review problems: The table describes $\mechanical{M}_0,\mechanical{M}$ as masses "before and after photon absorption or rocket acceleration", but no rocket appears here. It also lists $\energy{E}',\energy{E}_{\mathrm{tot}}$, the muon lifetimes $\tau_0,\tau$, the interferometer $\Delta t$ and $\theta'$, none of which the note uses. It omits $\mechanical{m}_{\mathrm f}$, $\mechanical{V}_{\mathrm f}$, $\mechanical{V}_0$, $\mechanical{V}_1$, $\mechanical{V}_2$ and $\mechanical{M}$ (Problem 10-7).
- [[#N3261|N3261]] Relativistic collisions, decays, and threshold exercises: The Physical quantities table lists $\mechanical{m}_{K^0}$ (the kaon does not appear here), muon lifetimes, and $\mechanical{p}_{\mathrm{tot}}$. It describes $\signal{\nu},\signal{\nu}'$ as frequencies "before and after scattering", but here they are the frequencies in the two frames of a Doppler problem. It also omits $\mechanical{V}$, $\mechanical{u}$, $\mechanical{\gamma}_m$, $\mechanical{p}_0$, $\mechanical{p}_x$ and $\mechanical{V}_{\mathrm f}$.
- [[#N3261|N3261]] Relativistic collisions, decays, and threshold exercises: Sigma-minus decay: $1.5\times10^{-10}$ s is the $\Sigma^-$ mean lifetime (PDG $1.48\times10^{-10}$ s), not its half-life. Relabel it, or note that the value does not enter the kinetic-energy ratio.
- [[#N3261|N3261]] Relativistic collisions, decays, and threshold exercises: Torpedo: $\mechanical{p}_{\mu}'=(\tfrac54mc,\tfrac34mc,0,0)$ uses a lower index with all spatial components positive. Write $p^\mu$ (upper index). In part (d), state the final result $u=(15/17)c$ explicitly.
- [[#N3262|N3262]] Relativistic energy, Compton scattering, and Doppler calculations: $\mechanical{X}_{\mu}$, $\mechanical{U}_{\mu}$ and $\mechanical{p}_{\mu}=(E/c,\vec p)$ are written with lower indices, although with the note's $(-,+,+,+)$ convention the lower-index time component carries a minus sign. Use $X^\mu$, $U^\mu$ and $p^\mu$ throughout.
- [[#N3262|N3262]] Relativistic energy, Compton scattering, and Doppler calculations: $\theta$ means three things in one note: the Lorentz-axis tilt ($\tan\theta=\beta$), the Compton scattering angle, and the Doppler propagation angle. $\nu'$ is the scattered frequency in the Compton section but the source-frame frequency in the Doppler section. The table describes $\nu,\nu'$ only as "before and after scattering" and also lists unused rows (muon lifetimes, interferometer $\Delta t$). Rename the axis tilt $\alpha$ and fix the table.
- [[#N3263|N3263]] Relativistic formulation of Agular Momentum: $K^i=x^iE/c-tp^i$ is dimensionally inconsistent: the first term has units m·kg·m/s, the second s·kg·m/s. From $M^{i0}=x^iP^0-x^0P^i$ with $x^0=ct$, the correct form is $K^i=x^iE/c-ct\,p^i$; equivalently, the conserved mass moment is $x^iE/c^2-tp^i$.
- [[#N3263|N3263]] Relativistic formulation of Agular Momentum: "Conservation law" writes $\partial_\alpha M^{\mu\nu\alpha}=0$ with a three-index object the note never defines. Define the angular-momentum current $M^{\mu\nu\alpha}=x^\mu T^{\nu\alpha}-x^\nu T^{\mu\alpha}$, which needs a symmetric $T^{\mu\nu}$, and show how $\partial_\alpha M^{\mu\nu\alpha}=0$ integrates to a conserved $M^{\mu\nu}$.
- [[#N3263|N3263]] Relativistic formulation of Agular Momentum: $L^i=\epsilon^{ijk}x^jp^k$ is called "the relativistic version" of $\mathbf L=\mathbf r\times\mathbf p$, but it is the same expression. State the relation to the tensor, $L^i=\tfrac12\epsilon^{ijk}M^{jk}$.
- [[#N3264|N3264]] Spacetime Coordinates: "$dl^2=dx^2+dt^2$" is wrong: the spatial line element is $dl^2=dx^2+dy^2+dz^2$, and time does not enter.
- [[#N3264|N3264]] Spacetime Coordinates: "$ds^2=\eta_xdx^2+\eta_tdt^2$ with $\eta_t=-1$" drops $c^2$, which makes it dimensionally inconsistent. Write $ds^2=\eta_{\mu\nu}dx^\mu dx^\nu$ with $x^0=ct$ and $\eta=\mathrm{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$.
- [[#N3264|N3264]] Spacetime Coordinates: $ds=\sqrt{dx^2+dy^2+dz^2-c^2dt^2}$ is imaginary for timelike separations. Define $ds^2$ as the invariant, and $d\tau=\sqrt{-ds^2}/c$ for timelike pairs.
- [[#N3265|N3265]] Spacetime Interval: "$a(t)\approx1+H\,dt$" is wrong. The scale factor expands as $a(t)\approx a_0[1+H_0(t-t_0)]$, in coordinate time, not in the differential $dt$, so the $(1+2H\,dt)$ factors in all later lines are invalid.
- [[#N3265|N3265]] Spacetime Interval: "Time Dilation": substituting $dx'=dx-v\,dt$ gives $ds'^2=-c^2(1-v^2/c^2)dt^2-2v\,dx\,dt+dx^2$; the note drops $dx$ in the cross term ("$-2v\,dt$"). In coordinates $(t,x)$ the metric's off-diagonal entries are $-v$, not $-v/c$. The bullet "$g_{00}=-(1-v^2/c^2)$" contradicts the matrix entry $-c^2(1-v^2/c^2)$. Also fix the typos "glocks" and "intertial".
- [[#N3265|N3265]] Spacetime Interval: Galilean transformation: applying a Galilean boost to the Minkowski metric does not give special-relativistic time dilation. The resulting off-diagonal term is a coordinate artifact of a non-Lorentz frame, not a "gravitomagnetic potential" representing "the origin of inertia". Either use a Lorentz boost (the metric stays $\eta$) or clearly label this as a Galilean-coordinate exercise.
- [[#N3265|N3265]] Spacetime Interval: With $A_g=-v/c$ and $\nabla\times v=2\Omega$, $\nabla\times A_g=-2\Omega/c$, not $-2\Omega$. The claim $\Phi_U'=\gamma\Phi_U$ is unsourced and nonstandard; cite the source (it appears to be a Machian framework) or remove it.
- [[#N3266|N3266]] Centenary Einstein Equation: "Empty Space: $R_{ik}=0$ … the condition for spacetime to be flat" is wrong. Ricci-flat spacetimes can be strongly curved (the Schwarzschild and Kerr exteriors); flatness requires the full Riemann tensor to vanish. The Weyl tensor carries the vacuum curvature, not only gravitational waves.
- [[#N3266|N3266]] Centenary Einstein Equation: The "Centenary Einstein Equation" with a separate $T_{ik(U)}$ is not standard GR. Moved to the right-hand side, it is just the EFE with total source $T+T_U$. State its origin and status (author, year), and say that a cosmological constant term is normally written $\Lambda g_{ik}$, not as part of a "universe" stress tensor.
- [[#N3266|N3266]] Centenary Einstein Equation: The "Empty space" section sets $T_{ik(U)}=0$, which contradicts the earlier description of $T_{ik(U)}$ as a universal background present everywhere. Clarify when, if ever, it vanishes.
- [[#N3267|N3267]] Christoffel Symbols: Fig. 1.1 is clipped: its bounds are $[-4.5,2.55,4.5,-2.55]$, but the Cartesian grid spans $x\in[-6.4,-1.5]$, the polar circles reach $x\approx6.7$ (outer $e_r$ arrow at $x\approx7.2$), and the titles and bottom captions sit at $y=\pm3.3$ to $3.5$. Large parts of the figure are outside the view. Widen the bounds to about $[-7,3.9,8,-3.7]$ (with matching width and height) and check it in reading mode.
- [[#N3268|N3268]] General Relativity (MIT 8.962 self-study): Linearized gravity with dynamic sources (~l.1954): $\Theta=\frac12(H-\nabla^2\lambda)$ should be $\Theta=\frac13(H-\nabla^2\lambda)$ (Flanagan–Hughes); only the 1/3 form gives $G_{tt}=-\nabla^2\Theta$. Line ~1962 writes "$G_{\alpha\beta}=8\pi T_{\alpha\beta}$", dropping the $G$ used in the following equations ($8\pi GT_{\alpha\beta}$).
- [[#N3268|N3268]] General Relativity (MIT 8.962 self-study): Field tensor (~l.1876–1887): with $\eta=\mathrm{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, $A^0=q/r$ and $F^{\mu\nu}=\partial^\mu A^\nu-\partial^\nu A^\mu$, $F^{0i}=+qx^i/r^3$. The printed matrix is $F_{\mu\nu}$, so relabel it or flip the first row and column. Elsewhere: "Principle of equivalence" (~l.788) quotes a test precision of $10^{-13}$, which is outdated (MICROSCOPE 2022: about $10^{-15}$). "Buchdahl's theorem" (~l.3201) gives the neutron-star $T_F\simeq10^{13}$ K, which should be about $10^{11}$–$10^{12}$ K.
- [[#N3268|N3268]] General Relativity (MIT 8.962 self-study): The symbol table and the overloaded symbols need repair. $\Lambda$ is the Lorentz matrix, an EM gauge function, the cosmological constant and the radial metric function $e^{2\Lambda(r)}$. $H$ is the Hubble parameter and the trace of $h_{ij}$. $\rho_0$ is the rest-frame density, the present-day cosmological density and the rest-mass density. $a$ is the four-acceleration, a cube constant, the scale factor and the Kerr spin. $R$ is the Ricci scalar, the scale factor, the Kruskal coordinate and the receiver radius. In the perfect-fluid section, $\rho$ silently switches from the moving-frame value $\gamma^2\rho_0$ to the rest-frame density. Rename the clashes and add the missing core rows ($G$, $R^\alpha{}_{\beta\gamma\delta}$, $T_{\mu\nu}$, $h_{\mu\nu}$, $\bar h_{\mu\nu}$, $I_{ij}$, $V_{\mathrm{eff}}$, $M$, $Q$).
- [[#N3270|N3270]] Schwarzschild Metric: The note says "natural units ($c=1$)" but keeps $G$ in $1-2GM/r$, lists $c=299\,792\,458$ m/s, and then gives $r_s=2GM/c^2$; use either $G=c=1$ throughout ($1-2M/r$, $r_s=2M$) or the full SI form $-(1-2GM/(c^2r))\,c^2\mathrm dt^2+\dots$ with $r_s=2GM/c^2$.
- [[#N3270|N3270]] Schwarzschild Metric: "**r** the radial distance from the object" is wrong: $r$ is the areal (circumferential) radius, defined so the sphere area is $4\pi r^2$; the proper radial distance is $\int\mathrm dr/\sqrt{1-r_s/r}$ and exceeds $\Delta r$.
- [[#N3296|N3296]] 2.1 Energy conditions: Table 2.1, weak row: "$\rho+p_i>0$" should be $\rho+p_i\ge0$ (a cosmological constant with $\rho=-p>0$ satisfies the WEC with $\rho+p=0$).
- [[#N3298|N3298]] 2.1.2 Weak energy condition: "$0\le\rho+a^2p_1<\rho+p_1$" holds only for $p_1>0$; the correct argument lets $a^2\to1$ and gives $\rho+p_1\ge0$, so Eq. (2.7) should read $\rho\ge0$, $\rho+p_i\ge0$ (not $>0$).
- [[#N3302|N3302]] 2.1.6 Violations of the energy conditions: "recent work suggests" and "Its status in curved spacetimes is not yet fully settled ... as of 1994" are outdated: the ANEC has since been proven in flat spacetime for general unitary Lorentz-invariant QFTs (Faulkner, Leigh, Parrikar, Wang 2016; Hartman, Kundu, Tajdini 2017); add a dated update note.
- [[#N3302|N3302]] 2.1.6 Violations of the energy conditions: $\energy{\hbar}$ is coloured as an energy, but $\hbar$ is an action (J s, or m$^2$ in geometrized units); use the appropriate macro group or leave it uncoloured.
- [[#N3304|N3304]] 2.2.1 Two-dimensional medium: The physical-quantity table lists $\mechanical{B}_{ab}$, $\mechanical{r}_1$, and $\mechanical{\phi}'$, which this note never uses; trim the table to the symbols in the note.
- [[#N3305|N3305]] 2.2.2 Expansion: The table lists $\mechanical{B}_{ab}$ and $\mechanical{\phi}'$, which this note does not use; remove them.
- [[#N3306|N3306]] 2.2.3 Shear: The table lists $\mechanical{B}_{ab}$, $\mechanical{\sigma}_{ab}$, and $\mechanical{\phi}'$, which this note does not use; remove them.
- [[#N3307|N3307]] 2.2.4 Rotation: The table lists $\mechanical{B}_{ab}$, $\mechanical{r}_1$, and $\mechanical{\omega}_{ab}$, which this note does not use; remove them.
- [[#N3313|N3313]] 2.3.3 Frobenius' theorem: "$\omega_{\alpha\beta}=-\Phi_{[\alpha}\mu_{,\beta]}$" is missing a comma; it should be $-\Phi_{,[\alpha}\mu_{,\beta]}$.
- [[#N3314|N3314]] 2.3.4 Raychaudhuri's equation: The physical-quantity table lists $\mechanical{\theta}_0$, $\mechanical{u}^t$, $\mechanical{u}^r$, $\mechanical{u}^\theta$, $\mechanical{u}^\phi$, and $\mechanical{u}_t$, none of which appear in this note; trim it.
- [[#N3315|N3315]] 2.3.5 Focusing theorem: The physical-quantity table lists $\mechanical{u}^t$, $\mechanical{u}^r$, $\mechanical{u}^\theta$, $\mechanical{u}^\phi$, and $\mechanical{u}_t$, which this note never uses; trim it.
- [[#N3316|N3316]] 2.3.6 Example: The table lists $\mechanical{u}^r$, $\mechanical{u}^\theta$, $\mechanical{u}^\phi$, $\mechanical{u}_t$, $\mechanical{\theta}_0$, and $\mechanical{B}^{\alpha\beta}$, none of which appear in this note; trim it.
- [[#N3317|N3317]] 2.3.7 Another example: Symbol clash: $\mechanical{\theta}$ is both the polar angle in $\mathrm d\Omega^2$ and the expansion scalar, and the table lists both meanings; rename the angle (for example $\vartheta$) or add an explicit warning.
- [[#N3318|N3318]] 2.3.8 Interpretation of θ: Eq. (2.21) is written with $\mathrm d/\mathrm d\mechanical{t}$, but the note (and Eq. 2.27) uses proper time; write $\theta=\delta V^{-1}\,\mathrm d\delta V/\mathrm d\tau$ and drop $\mechanical{t}$ from the table.
- [[#N3319|N3319]] 2.4 Congruence of null geodesics: The table lists $\mechanical{\tilde\xi}^\alpha$ and $h'_{\alpha\beta}$, which appear only in later notes; trim it to the symbols used here.
- [[#N3323|N3323]] 2.4.4 Raychaudhuri's equation: The table lists $\mechanical{\theta}_0$ and the $\mechanical{k}^{\rm out}$, $\mechanical{k}^{\rm in}$ variants, none of which appear in this note; trim it.

- [[#N3325|N3325]] 2.4.6 Example: Symbol clash: $\mechanical{\theta}$ is the polar angle in $h_{\alpha\beta}=\operatorname{diag}(0,0,r^2,r^2\sin^2\theta)$ and also the expansion $\theta=2/r$, and the table lists both; rename the angle or add a warning.
- [[#N3326|N3326]] 2.4.7 Another example: Symbol clash: the table lists $\mechanical{\theta}$ both as a sphere angle and as the expansion; the index placement also switches between $k^{\rm out}_\alpha$ and $k_{\rm out}^\alpha$; make both consistent.
- [[#N3336|N3336]] 3.10 Slowly rotating shell: Symbol clash: $\mechanical{\Omega}$ is the frame angular velocity (3.72-3.73) while $\mathrm d\Omega^2$ in (3.71) is the solid-angle element; write the angular part explicitly or call the frame rate $\mechanical{\Omega_{\mathrm{in}}}$ from the start.
- [[#N3339|N3339]] 3.11.2 Surface stress-energy tensor: Symbol clash: $\gamma_{\alpha\beta}$ (the jump tensor of Eq. 3.94) appears in the same equations as the free index $\gamma$ (for example $[g_{\alpha\beta,\gamma}]=-\gamma_{\alpha\beta}\mechanical{k}_\gamma$ and $[\Gamma^\alpha_{\beta\gamma}]$ in 3.95); relabel the free index or note the clash explicitly.
- [[#N3339|N3339]] 3.11.2 Surface stress-energy tensor: Missing semantic macro: $k^\beta$ is written bare in (3.98) ($\gamma_{\alpha\beta}e^\alpha_Ak^\beta$) and (3.99) ($e^\alpha_Ak^\beta$); use $\mechanical{k}^\beta$ as everywhere else.
- [[#N3340|N3340]] 3.11.3 Intrinsic formulation: Index typo in the jump calculation: $[C_{ab}]=[N_{\alpha;\beta}]e^\alpha_ae^\alpha_b$ (repeated in all three lines) should read $e^\alpha_ae^\beta_b$.
- [[#N3340|N3340]] 3.11.3 Intrinsic formulation: Missing semantic macro: $k^\beta$ is bare in $[C_{A\mechanical{\lambda}}]=\frac12\gamma_{\alpha\beta}e^\alpha_Ak^\beta$; use $\mechanical{k}^\beta$.
- [[#N3341|N3341]] 3.11.4 Summary: Missing semantic macro: $e^\alpha_Ak^\beta$ in the $\energy{S^{\alpha\beta}}$ formula should use $\mechanical{k}^\beta$.
- [[#N3342|N3342]] 3.11.5 Parameterization of the null generators: The observer factor is mis-transformed: "$(-\bar{\mechanical{k}}_\mu\mechanical{u}^\mu)^{-1}=e^\beta(-\mechanical{k}_\mu\mechanical{u}^\mu)$" should be $e^\beta(-\mechanical{k}_\mu\mechanical{u}^\mu)^{-1}$, since $\bar{\mechanical{k}}^\alpha=e^{-\beta}\mechanical{k}^\alpha$; only then is $(-\mechanical{k}_\mu\mechanical{u}^\mu)^{-1}\energy{S^{\alpha\beta}}$ invariant.
- [[#N3342|N3342]] 3.11.5 Parameterization of the null generators: Symbol clashes: $e^\beta$ (exponential of the reparameterization function $\beta$) sits next to basis vectors $e^\alpha_A$ and the index $\beta$; $\mechanical{\sigma}_{\alpha\beta}$ (shear) and $\sqrt\sigma$ (determinant) clash with the two-metric $\sigma_{AB}$; $\mechanical{\theta}$ (expansion) clashes with $\theta^A$; use an upright $\mathrm e^{\beta}$ (or a named factor) and a distinct shear symbol.
- [[#N3344|N3344]] 3.11.7 Accreting black hole: "$\mechanical{\Omega_{\mathrm{relative}}}=\mechanical{j^\psi}/\energy{\mu}=3\mechanical{M}\mechanical{a}f/(2\mechanical{m}\mechanical{r}^2)$" is inconsistent: $\mechanical{j^\psi}/\energy{\mu}=3\mechanical{M}\mechanical{a}/(2\mechanical{m}\mechanical{r}^2)$ without $f$; since $\mathrm d\mechanical{\phi}/\mathrm d\mechanical{t}=\mechanical{\ell}^\phi/\mechanical{\ell}^t=f\mechanical{\ell}^\phi$, the correct statement is $\mechanical{\Omega_{\mathrm{relative}}}=f\,\mechanical{j^\psi}/\energy{\mu}$.
- [[#N3345|N3345]] 3.11.8 Cosmological phase transition: Index typo: $\energy{S^{\alpha\beta}}=\mechanical{p}\sigma^{AB}e^\alpha_Ae^\alpha_B$ should be $\mechanical{p}\sigma^{AB}e^\alpha_Ae^\beta_B$.

- [[#N3350|N3350]] 3.2.2 Surface element (null case): In the inverse-metric matrix, the $\Phi\lambda$ entries should be $-1$, not $+1$: with $k_\Phi\stackrel{*}{=}-1$, $k^\lambda\stackrel{*}{=}1$ and $N^\Phi\stackrel{*}{=}1$, Eq. - [[#N3351|N3351]] 3.2.3 Element of two-surface: The physical-quantities table lists $dS_{tx},dS_{xt}$ and $n^\Phi$, which this note never uses; remove them.

- [[#N3369|N3369]] 3.6.5 Spherical space, moment of time symmetry: Symbol clash: a prime means $d/dr$ in $m'$, but $r'$ in the integral is a dummy integration variable. Rename the dummy variable (for example $\bar r$) so that $r'$ is not read as a derivative.
- [[#N3379|N3379]] 3.8 Oppenheimer-Snyder collapse: Symbol clash: $\mechanical{a}$ is the scale factor and $\mechanical{a^\alpha}$ is the four-acceleration in the same note (for example $K_{\tau\tau}=-a^\alpha n_\alpha$ next to $K^\theta{}_\theta=a^{-1}\cot\chi_0$). Rename the acceleration (for example $\alpha^\alpha$ or $\dot u^\alpha$) and update the table.
- [[#N3389|N3389]] 4.1.7 Nondynamical term: Symbol clash: $R$ is the Ricci scalar ("Then $R=0$") and $\mechanical{R}$ is the cylinder radius ("$r=R$", "$R\to\infty$") in the same note; rename the radius (e.g. $r_0$) and update the table.
- [[#N3397|N3397]] 4.2.6 Gravitational Hamiltonian: The table describes $\mathcal H_G$ as "The gravitational energy density"; this is misleading because the volume part $N(K^{ab}K_{ab}-K^2-{}^3R)-2N_a(K^{ab}-Kh^{ab})_{|b}$ is a combination of the constraints and vanishes for vacuum solutions (4.2.8–4.2.9); describe it as the volume (constraint) part of the Hamiltonian density.
- [[#N3398|N3398]] 4.2.7 Variation of the Hamiltonian: The "three-dimensional version of Eq. (4.17)" and $\delta k=\tfrac12h^{ab}\delta h_{ab,c}r^c$ should use the projector onto $S_t$, $\sigma^{ab}=\sigma^{AB}e^a_Ae^b_B$, not the full $h^{ab}=r^ar^b+\sigma^{ab}$ (the $r^ar^br^c\delta h_{ab,c}$ piece does not vanish in general, exactly as $h^{\alpha\beta}$ in Eq. (4.17) is the boundary projector); the cancellation between $\delta_h\hat H_\Sigma$ and $\delta_h\hat H_S$ is unaffected because both terms change the same way.
- [[#N3403|N3403]] 4.3.2 Mass and angular momentum for stationary, axially symmetric spacetimes: The table calls $K_{\phi r}$ a "mixed coordinate component"; it is a fully covariant off-diagonal component ("mixed" normally means one upper and one lower index). Reword to "off-diagonal covariant component".
- [[#N3406|N3406]] 4.3.5 Distinction between ADM and Bondi-Sachs masses -  Vaidya spacetime: Symbol clash for $t$: in $u=t-r-2M\ln(r/2M-1)$ it is the Schwarzschild time, but later $t\equiv u+r$ defines the slicing time, which differs from it by $2M\ln(r/2M-1)$; rename one (e.g. $t_s$ for Schwarzschild time) and note the difference.
- [[#N3406|N3406]] 4.3.5 Distinction between ADM and Bondi-Sachs masses -  Vaidya spacetime: Symbol clash for $M$: it denotes the constant Schwarzschild mass in the definition of $u$ and also the surface functional $M(S)$, while the table lists only "original mass"; rename $M(S)$ (e.g. $\mathcal M(S)$) or add it to the table.
- [[#N3407|N3407]] 4.3.6 Transfer of mass and angular momentum: In $\varepsilon^\alpha{}_{;\alpha}=-T^{\alpha\beta}{}_{;\alpha}\xi_{(t)\beta}+T^{\alpha\beta}\xi_{(t)\beta;\alpha}$ the second term must carry a minus sign, $-T^{\alpha\beta}\xi_{(t)\beta;\alpha}$ (both terms vanish, so the conclusion is unchanged).
- [[#N3416|N3416]] 5.1.4 Painlevé-Gullstrand coordinates: "an alternative coordinate system is produced that covers regions **VI** and **I**" — there is no region VI; it should be regions **IV** and **I** (the white-hole and exterior regions), as in [[5.1.3 Eddington-Finkelstein coordinates]].
- [[#N3419|N3419]] 5.1.7 Apparent horizon: Symbol clash: $\theta$ is both the expansion ($\theta=k^\alpha{}_{;\alpha}$) and the polar angle in $|g|^{1/2}=|g_{UV}|r^2\sin\theta$; the table lists both. Rename the angle locally (for example $\vartheta$) or write the expansion as $\Theta$.
- [[#N3421|N3421]] 5.1.9 Killing horizon: "$g_{\alpha\beta}t^\alpha t^\beta=1-\frac{2M}{r}$" has the wrong sign: $g_{\alpha\beta}t^\alpha t^\beta=g_{tt}=-(1-2M/r)$, negative (timelike) outside and positive (spacelike) inside, as the preceding sentence says.
- [[#N3424|N3424]] 5.2.2 Kruskal coordinates: With Eq. (5.26) as written ($U_-=\mp e^{\kappa_-u}$, $V_-=e^{-\kappa_-v}$), $U_-V_-=-\kappa_-(r-r_-)$, so $f\simeq+2U_-V_-$ and $\mathrm ds^2\simeq+\frac{2}{\kappa_-^2}\mathrm dU_-\mathrm dV_-$, not "$f\simeq-2U_-V_-$" and "$-\frac{2}{\kappa_-^2}$". Fix the sign convention, for example $V_-=-e^{-\kappa_-v}$, after checking the source.
- [[#N3435|N3435]] 5.3.4 Event horizon -  stationary observers: "where $\omega=-g_{t\phi}/g_{tt}$" is wrong; the frame-dragging rate is $\omega=-g_{t\phi}/g_{\phi\phi}$ (Eq. 5.45). Only this form makes the last line of the $\gamma^{-2}$ derivation correct.
- [[#N3440|N3440]] 5.3.9 Maximal extension of the Kerr spacetime: Eq. (5.75) reads "$U_-=\mp e^{\kappa_-u},\ V_+=-e^{-\kappa_-v}$"; the second coordinate must be $V_-=-e^{-\kappa_-v}$ (the metric is then written in terms of $\mathrm dU_-\,\mathrm dV_-$).
- [[#N3446|N3446]] 5.5.1 Preliminaries: "$\xi_\alpha e^\alpha_A=0=\xi^\alpha e^A_\alpha$": the object $e^A_\alpha$ is never defined; the conditions needed for the completeness relation are $\xi_\alpha e^\alpha_A=0$, $N_\alpha e^\alpha_A=0$, $N_\alpha N^\alpha=0$ and $N_\alpha\xi^\alpha=-1$ (and $\xi_\alpha\xi^\alpha=0$); state these explicitly after introducing $N^\alpha$.
- [[#N3446|N3446]] 5.5.1 Preliminaries: Symbol clash: $\theta^A$ labels the generators while $\theta$ (mechanical colour) is the expansion in Eq. (5.97); rename the generator labels (e.g. $\vartheta^A$ or $y^A$) or add an explicit warning.

- [[#N3464|N3464]] KK 06 Algebraic decomposition of the metric: Symbol clash: $B_\mu(t,x,y,z)$ uses $y$ as an ordinary coordinate, while Eq. (6.1) uses $y$ for the circle.
- [[#N3469|N3469]] KK 11 Full coordinate transformation calculation: The sentence "Thus the adjusted base metric is unchanged: $g\prime_{\mu …u}=g_{\mu …u}$" contains a literal line break inside `\nu` (the `\n` was turned into a newline), so it renders incorrectly; replace with $g'_{\mu\nu}=g_{\mu\nu}$.
- [[#N3472|N3472]] KK 14 Reducing the Einstein-Hilbert action: "Worked normalization check": if the coefficient multiplying the squared potential in the metric ($\kappa^2\Phi^2$) is doubled, the Maxwell coefficient doubles, not quadruples; the factor four applies if $\kappa$ itself is doubled; reword accordingly.
- [[#N3473|N3473]] KK 15 Deriving the curvature split: The text "Ricci curvature is symmetric in this setting…" is placed on the same line as the closing `$$` of the preceding aligned block; move it to its own paragraph so the display math renders.
- [[#N3473|N3473]] KK 15 Deriving the curvature split: A stray period ends the $F_{\mu\nu}F^{\mu\nu}=2(|\mathbf B|^2-|\mathbf E|^2)$ display before "in a local inertial frame", splitting one sentence; remove it.
- [[#N3474|N3474]] KK 16 Fourier modes and periodicity: Physical quantities: the $\mechanical{\theta}$ row refers to a "spherical-coordinate inset" that does not exist in this note, and $\signal{k}_5$ is described generically as "Angular frequency and wave vector" although only the compact wave number is used; make the rows describe this note's quantities.
- [[#N3475|N3475]] KK 17 Klein-Gordon equation and dispersion: Physical quantities lists $\signal{\psi}$ twice with conflicting units (GeV and —), lists $\signal{\psi}_n$ and an "unnormalized expansion" that this note never uses, and lists both $\mechanical{\mathbf x}$ and $\mechanical{x}$ as coordinates; remove the duplicates.
- [[#N3476|N3476]] KK 18 Deriving the Kaluza-Klein mass tower: Physical quantities: $\signal{\psi}_n$ appears twice with conflicting units (GeV and —), and the $\mechanical{\theta}$ row mentions a nonexistent "spherical-coordinate inset"; clean up the duplicates.
- [[#N3477|N3477]] KK 19 Deriving charge from phase winding: "Each mass eigenmode is also a charge eigenmode" is false: modes $\pm n$ are mass-degenerate, so a combination such as $\cos(n\theta)$ is a mass eigenmode with no definite charge; say instead that each Fourier mode $e^{in\theta}$ is simultaneously a mass and a charge eigenmode.
- [[#N3477|N3477]] KK 19 Deriving charge from phase winding: Physical quantities: the $\mechanical{\theta}$ row mentions a nonexistent "spherical-coordinate inset", and $\signal{\psi}_n$ is listed twice with conflicting units.
- [[#N3478|N3478]] KK 20 General covariance and gauge symmetry: Physical quantities: the $\mechanical{\theta}$ row mentions a "spherical-coordinate inset" that is not in this note.
- [[#N3479|N3479]] KK 21 Visualizing local phase choices: Symbol clash: $\mechanical{y}$ is an ordinary spatial coordinate in the plane example and in the table, but the note's own length-coordinate paragraph defines $y$ as the compact coordinate; rename one of them in this note.
- [[#N3479|N3479]] KK 21 Visualizing local phase choices: Physical quantities: $\mechanical{m}$ is listed although it is never used, and the $\mechanical{r}$ and $\mechanical{\theta}$ rows refer to a nonexistent "spherical inset".
- [[#N3484|N3484]] Kaluza-Klein - Study Guide: "Notation and units" opens with "The collection uses a mostly-plus metric", but the next section and the first section of every chapter from KK 16 to KK 24 use a mostly-minus angular calculation; say the collection uses two signatures, as stated later.
- [[#N3487|N3487]] 01 References: Ref. 10 should read R. A. Lyttleton and H. Bondi, "On the physical consequences of a general excess of charge", Proc. R. Soc. Lond. A 252, 313–333 (1959); it is not "Littleton" and not Proc. Phys. Soc.
- [[#N3487|N3487]] 01 References: Ref. 4: volume 13 of the Collected Papers was published by Princeton University Press in 2012; 1922 is the date of Einstein's original comment, not of the translation volume.
- [[#N3487|N3487]] 01 References: Ref. 16: replace the impossible year "2919" (most likely 2019) after checking the citation, and resolve the callout.
- [[#N3493|N3493]] 01.05 The Cosmic Gravitational Metric and the Potentials: Eqs. (1.4)–(1.6): substituting $dx'=dx-v\,dt$ into a form written in primed coordinates yields the line element in unprimed coordinates. The Galilean transform of the rest metric ($H\to0$) is $ds^2=-(c^2-v^2)dt'^2+2v\,dx'dt'+dx'^2$, with cross coefficient $+v$ for $x'=x-vt$, and $\sqrt{1-v^2/c^2}$ describes a clock at $dx'=0$. In the printed (1.6), a comoving clock ($dx=v\,dt$) shows no dilation at all; add this to the source callout.
- [[#N3493|N3493]] 01.05 The Cosmic Gravitational Metric and the Potentials: After Eq. (1.8): with $A_g=-v/c$, the curl is $\nabla\times A_g=-2\Omega/c$, not $-2\Omega$. Only $-\nabla\times\mathbf v$ equals $-2\Omega$; list this among the dimensional inconsistencies.
- [[#N3494|N3494]] 01.06 A Phenomenological Assertion: $\sqrt{1-v^2/\Phi_U}$ (and $\sqrt{1-v^2/c^2}$) is called a "Lorentz factor", but the Lorentz factor is $\gamma=1/\sqrt{1-v^2/c^2}$; say "the reciprocal Lorentz factor" or "time-dilation factor" in the added text and the callout.
- [[#N3495|N3495]] 01.07 Summary of the Primary Results of Cosmic Relativity: Eq. (1.17): for $\mathbf v=\boldsymbol\Omega\times\mathbf r$, $-m\,\mathbf v\times\boldsymbol\Omega=m\,\boldsymbol\Omega\times(\boldsymbol\Omega\times\mathbf r)=-m\Omega^2\mathbf r$ points inward, so the final outward $\hat{\mathbf r}\,mv^2/r$ has the opposite sign. With $\mathbf A=-\mathbf v/c$ dimensionless, $m_g\,d\mathbf A/dt$ also lacks a factor $c$ to be a force.
- [[#N3495|N3495]] 01.07 Summary of the Primary Results of Cosmic Relativity: Coriolis paragraph: $\mathbf F=m_g\mathbf u\times\mathbf B_g$ with $\mathbf B_g=-2\boldsymbol\Omega$ gives $+2m\,\boldsymbol\Omega\times\mathbf u$, the opposite sign of the standard Coriolis force $-2m\,\boldsymbol\Omega\times\mathbf u$; flag this in a source callout.
- [[#N3495|N3495]] 01.07 Summary of the Primary Results of Cosmic Relativity: "The farthest 1/3 of the Universe has 4 times the amount of matter than the nearer 2/3" is wrong: the volume ratio is $(1-8/27)/(8/27)=19/8\approx2.4$. Only the potential share of the outer third, $1-(2/3)^2=5/9$, matches "more than half".
- [[#N3495|N3495]] 01.07 Summary of the Primary Results of Cosmic Relativity: Eq. (1.19) closes the spinless orbit phase at $2\pi n$, but the quoted levels $(i+\tfrac12)\hbar\omega$ imply the semiclassical condition $\Phi/\Phi_0=n+\tfrac12$ (Maslov phase $\pi$). The supposedly missing $\pi$ is this omitted term, and the Zeeman $\pi$ for $g\approx2$ gives the standard spin-split levels; the interpretation section should state this standard resolution.
- [[#N3496|N3496]] 01.08 The Universal Clock of Cosmic Relativity: "The same everywhere to ... better than a part in a million" overstates the isotropy: the CMB dipole is about $1.2\times10^{-3}$, and the intrinsic anisotropies are about $10^{-5}$ after the dipole is removed; add a callout with these values.
- [[#N3500|N3500]] 02 References: Ref. 3: the book title is "Einstein, Tagore and the Nature of Reality" (ed. P. Ghose, Routledge Studies in the Philosophy of Mathematics and Physics). The printed entry scrambles the series name into the title and misspells Einstein.
- [[#N3502|N3502]] 02.01 Newton's Space and Time: The Scholium on time and space follows the Definitions and precedes the Axioms (Laws of Motion), outside Book 1. The note says it is the first Scholium of Book 1, "after the definitions and 'axioms'".
- [[#N3505|N3505]] 02.04 Space and Time in Einstein's Relativity: "Since any two points in space-time can be connected by light, it follows that their interval remains invariant" is wrong: spacelike-separated events cannot be joined by a light signal, and invariance of the null cone alone gives only $ds'^2=\lambda(v)\,ds^2$. Fixing $\lambda=1$ needs isotropy and the group property; correct this in the interpretation.
- [[#N3505|N3505]] 02.04 Space and Time in Einstein's Relativity: The local-time term $vx/c^2$ is described as making clocks run "at rates that depend on both the relative velocity and the distance". It is a position-dependent synchronization offset (relativity of simultaneity), not a rate; the rate effect is the separate factor $\gamma$.
- [[#N3505|N3505]] 02.04 Space and Time in Einstein's Relativity: Einstein–Barnett quotation: per Lehmkuhl (2014) it reads "which we are wont to look at" and "is not logically founded", not "which we wont" and "not logically found".
- [[#N3507|N3507]] 02.06 Space and Time in the Factual Universe: "globally synchronised, but for the small fluctuations amounting a part in a million": the primary CMB temperature anisotropies are about $\Delta T/T\sim10^{-5}$ (tens of μK on 2.725 K), and the dipole is about $10^{-3}$. Add a short callout with the correct order of magnitude.
- [[#N3509|N3509]] 02.08 Space, Time, and the Principle of Relativity: In the quotation from 'The Meaning of Relativity', "every other system K which moves uniformly ... relatively to K" must read "every other system K′". As printed, the statement compares K with itself.
- [[#N3512|N3512]] 03.00 Electrodynamics, Light and Relativity: The Maxwell quotation spells the name "Kohlrauch"; the physicist is Rudolf Kohlrausch (Weber–Kohlrausch measurement of 1856). Correct it, or mark it as a source typo.
- [[#N3514|N3514]] 03.01.01 Roemer's Method: The note defines $\signal{\Delta T}=2\mechanical{v}\signal{T}/\mechanical{c}$ for the difference between the observed periods, then uses "varies by about 30 s" with $\mechanical{c}=\mechanical{v}\signal{T}/30\,\unit{s}\approx1.5\times10^8\,\unit{m/s}$. If 30 s is the approach–recession difference, then $\mechanical{c}=2\mechanical{v}\signal{T}/\signal{\Delta T}\approx3.06\times10^5\,\unit{km/s}$. The one-sided shift $\mechanical{v}\signal{T}/\mechanical{c}$ is only about 15 s. State which quantity is 30 s and fix the estimate.
- [[#N3514|N3514]] 03.01.01 Roemer's Method: "the average maximum delay is $42.48\times3600\times30/\mechanical{c}$" is the one-sided per-eclipse shift $\mechanical{v}\signal{T}/\mechanical{c}$, not the difference $\signal{\Delta T}$ given below it. Use one name for each quantity, so that the reader does not apply the factor 2 twice or not at all.
- [[#N3517|N3517]] 03.03 Stellar Aberration: "A. Fresnel had made the important theoretical discovery in 1815": Fresnel proposed partial drag in his 1818 letter to Arago. Correct the year.
- [[#N3518|N3518]] 03.04 The Speed of Light in Moving Media - Fresnel Drag: Fig. 3.4 caption and the sentence after it: for complete drag (speed $\mechanical{c}/\signal{n}\pm\mechanical{v}$) the fringe shift is $\Delta N\approx4\mechanical{L}\signal{n}^2\mechanical{v}/(\signal{\lambda}\mechanical{c})$, not proportional to $\mechanical{L}(\signal{n}-1)\mechanical{v}/(\signal{\lambda}\mechanical{c})$. With Fresnel drag it is $4\mechanical{L}(\signal{n}^2-1)\mechanical{v}/(\signal{\lambda}\mechanical{c})$.
- [[#N3518|N3518]] 03.04 The Speed of Light in Moving Media - Fresnel Drag: Caption: "the observed effect was still smaller, second order in the refractive index n" is wrong. The observed shift is the fraction $1-1/\signal{n}^2\approx0.44$ of the complete-drag value, which is first order in $\mechanical{v}/\mechanical{c}$. The body text ("about half the effect") is correct.
- [[#N3518|N3518]] 03.04 The Speed of Light in Moving Media - Fresnel Drag: Caption: "At about 5 m/s the expected shift is only about 1/100 of a fringe". With Fizeau's tubes ($\mechanical{L}\approx1.5\,\unit{m}$ each, $\signal{\lambda}\approx0.53\,\unit{\mu m}$), complete drag at 5 m/s gives $\Delta N\approx0.3$ fringe. Fizeau observed about 0.23 fringe on reversing a 7 m/s flow. Replace the estimate.
- [[#N3519|N3519]] 03.05 The Doppler Effect: "the situation where the observer is in transverse motion ... is not yet adequately probed in experiments" is outdated. Mössbauer rotor experiments with a moving absorber, for example Hay et al. (1960) and Kündig (1963), measured the transverse shift of a moving receiver and agreed with special relativity.
- [[#N3519|N3519]] 03.05 The Doppler Effect: Eqs. (3.13)–(3.14) mix $\mechanical{u}_s$ and $\mechanical{v}$ for the same speed (the callout mentions only $\mechanical{u}_s$ in 3.14). Use one symbol, $\mechanical{u}_s$ for the source case and $\mechanical{u}_o$ for the observer case, in both the exact and the approximate forms.
- [[#N3519|N3519]] 03.05 The Doppler Effect: Ives–Stilwell (1938) did not observe at 90°. They compared the forward- and backward-shifted lines, and the second-order shift of their mean gives $\sqrt{1-\mechanical{u}^2/\mechanical{c}^2}$. Say this, so that "what was verified was Eq. (3.13)" is not read as a transverse measurement.
- [[#N3520|N3520]] 03.06 Experiments Designed to Detect the Stationary Ether: The length-contraction paragraph after Eq. (3.27) switches from frames O, O′ to "F′" and "F" without definition. Use O and O′ throughout, or define F, F′.
- [[#N3521|N3521]] 03.07 The Trouton-Noble Experiment: Fitzgerald "had proposed the length contraction hypothesis in 1892". FitzGerald published it in 1889 (Science, ref. [16] in 03.06); 1892 is Lorentz's independent proposal.
- [[#N3521|N3521]] 03.07 The Trouton-Noble Experiment: "The total energy remains the same because the capacitance increases by the factor γ, but the volume decreases ... by the same factor" is inconsistent. At fixed charge, the longitudinal field is unchanged and the volume shrinks by $1/\gamma$, so $\energy{\mathcal E}=Q^2/2\circuit{C}$ falls by $1/\gamma$. At fixed $\electric{V}$, $\circuit{C}\electric{V}^2/2$ rises by γ. Rewrite or remove this claim.
- [[#N3521|N3521]] 03.07 The Trouton-Noble Experiment: Eq. (3.29) writes $\mechanical{T}=d\energy{\mathcal E}_m/d\mechanical{\theta}$. The torque is $\mechanical{T}=-d\energy{\mathcal E}_m/d\mechanical{\theta}$. With $\energy{\mathcal E}_m\propto\sin^2\mechanical{\theta}$, the printed minus sign on the right is correct, so the callout's "extra minus sign" comment is misleading. Fix the definition and the $\sin\mechanical{\theta}\to\sin^2\mechanical{\theta}$ exponent together.
- [[#N3521|N3521]] 03.07 The Trouton-Noble Experiment: $\mechanical{V}$ (volume, caption) and $\electric{V}$ (voltage, body) are both used. Rename the integration volume, for example to $d\tau$, so that one letter has one meaning.
- [[#N3523|N3523]] 03.09 Experiments on the Unipolar Induction: $\electric{E}$ is used both for the electric field vector and for the emf in Figs. 3.9–3.10, as the table admits. Use $\mathcal{E}$ (or $U$) for the emf.
- [[#N3528|N3528]] 04.01 Einstein's Motivations for a Theory of Relativity: "Einstein mentioned the astronomical evidence of light received from double stars for this fact [3, 4]" sits inside the account of 1905. The 1905 paper cites no double-star evidence. De Sitter's argument [4] dates from 1913, and the remark about school children is in the 1916 popular book. State the dates, so that it is not read as part of Einstein's 1905 reasoning.
- [[#N3529|N3529]] 04.02 The Lorentz Transformations: "A clock in O′ at the position $\mechanical{x}$ of the frame O runs behind a clock at the origin ... by the amount $\mechanical{v}\mechanical{x}/\mechanical{c}^2$": from Eq. (4.7), at fixed $t$ the offset is $\gamma\mechanical{v}\mechanical{x}/\mechanical{c}^2=\mechanical{v}\mechanical{x}'/\mechanical{c}^2$. Write it with $\mechanical{x}'$, or add γ.
- [[#N3531|N3531]] 04.03.01 The Doppler Effect in the STR: "All the experiments use a moving source and a stationary detector" is false. Mössbauer rotor experiments with the absorber on the rim (Hay et al. 1960, Kündig 1963) used a moving receiver and agreed with special relativity.
- [[#N3531|N3531]] 04.03.01 The Doppler Effect in the STR: "the spectral shift that is confirmed in experiments, like the Ives-Stilwell experiment, directly contradicts this": Eq. (4.21) uses φ = 90° in the observer frame, while Eq. (4.22) is emission at 90° in the source frame. These are different geometries related by aberration, and Ives–Stilwell measured the forward and backward lines, not 90°. No contradiction follows. The note's "Interpretation and checks" says this, but the lecture text calls it a refutation.
- [[#N3531|N3531]] 04.03.01 The Doppler Effect in the STR: "For the special case φ = 0, the important difference between the two expressions ... cannot be discerned" compares Eq. (4.18) (observer receding for $\mechanical{v}>0$) with Eq. (4.20) (source approaching). These are reciprocal, opposite senses of motion. State the sign convention, so that the reader sees that the same sense of relative motion gives the same formula.
- [[#N3532|N3532]] 04.03.02 The Unipolar Phenomena and the STR: "requires only the local magnetic field $\magnetic{\mathbf B}$ and the instantaneous relative velocity $\mechanical{\mathbf v}$": in the co-rotating case the relative velocity of conductor and magnet is zero, yet an emf appears. The velocity in $\electric{\mathbf E}=\mechanical{\mathbf v}\times\magnetic{\mathbf B}$ must be the conductor's velocity in the frame where the field is static (the lab), not the velocity relative to the magnet.
- [[#N3532|N3532]] 04.03.02 The Unipolar Phenomena and the STR: "hidden under a several rug" is a typo. Use "swept under the rug" or similar.
- [[#N3534|N3534]] 04.03.04 The Empirical Status of the Light Hypothesis: Correct in place: "$\mechanical{v}\delta t=\mechanical{v}\mechanical{x}/\mechanical{c}^2$ is the duration the signal saves" should read $(\mechanical{v}/\mechanical{c})\delta t=\mechanical{v}\mechanical{x}/\mechanical{c}^2$. The callout notes the unit mismatch but leaves the wrong expression in the text.
- [[#N3540|N3540]] 05.01 Introduction: "the average temperature is the same everywhere in the Universe to very high accuracy (of a part in a million)": CMB anisotropies are about $10^{-5}$ (and the observer's dipole is about $10^{-3}$). Correct the figure, as in 02.06.
- [[#N3542|N3542]] 05.03 Einstein's Discussion of Simultaneity in the STR: "the light signals from A and B will reach the observer O′ simultaneously, after the delay $\mechanical{L}/(2\mechanical{c})$" is not what special relativity predicts. The meeting of the two rays is one spacetime event on O's worldline, which all frames agree on. In O′'s frame the two emissions are not simultaneous (they differ by $\gamma\mechanical{v}\mechanical{L}/\mechanical{c}^2$), so O′ receives the B flash first. The "catastrophe" paragraph follows from assuming that "when the events occurred" is the same in both frames.
- [[#N3543|N3543]] 05.04 Einstein's Fallacy on the Relativity of Simultaneity: "The light signals that were emitted when O′ was at the midpoint M′ ... will necessarily reach O′ simultaneously" assumes that the emissions are simultaneous in O′'s frame. For flashes simultaneous on the platform, the Lorentz transformation gives a train-frame emission difference $\gamma\mechanical{v}\mechanical{L}/\mechanical{c}^2$, with B earlier. Einstein's conclusion therefore follows within the light postulate, with no inconsistency, and the boxed note "Einstein's light hypothesis is inconsistent" states a refuted claim as fact.
- [[#N3543|N3543]] 05.04 Einstein's Fallacy on the Relativity of Simultaneity: The claim that light reaching distant walls is "untestable and unverifiable" ignores that each wall can carry a local detector and clock, so that each arrival is a recorded event. What is frame-dependent is only the time order of two spacelike-separated events, which is the content of the relativity of simultaneity.
- [[#N3544|N3544]] 05.05 H. Bergson's Critique of Einstein's Relativity of Simultaneity: "there is not a single written account from anybody that counters and disproves Bergson's ... demonstration" is false. Jean Becquerel and André Metz published rebuttals in 1922–24, and Bergson answered Becquerel in the appendices added to the second edition of Durée et simultanéité (1923). Mention this exchange.
- [[#N3545|N3545]] 05.06 The Synchronisation of Time: "the midpoint of the two-way time delay is determined as $t_{A0}=(t_{A2}-t_{A1})/2$" defines half the round-trip delay, not a midpoint time. The midpoint instant is $(t_{A1}+t_{A2})/2$, as in Eq. (5.3). Rename $t_{A0}$, for example $\tau=(t_{A2}-t_{A1})/2$, in the text and the table.
- [[#N3549|N3549]] 06.01 The Universality of Free Fall: "the UFF is verified ... to the level of 1 part in $10^{13}$–$10^{14}$" is outdated. MICROSCOPE (2022) gives the Eötvös parameter $\eta(\mathrm{Ti,Pt})=(-1.5\pm2.7)\times10^{-15}$. Update the number.
- [[#N3549|N3549]] 06.01 The Universality of Free Fall: "The gravitational mass is the source of a gravitational field; it is the 'charge' of gravity" describes the active gravitational mass, while the WEP and the UFF concern the passive gravitational mass (the coupling to an external field). Distinguish $\mechanical{m}_p$ from $\mechanical{m}_a$, and link to [[06.07.04 The Active and the Passive Gravitational Masses]].
- [[#N3550|N3550]] 06.02 The Equivalence of Inertia and Mass - The Weak Equivalence Principle: "the WEP implies that any form of energy is also a source of gravity, with mass $\mechanical{m}_g=\mechanical{m}_i$" is wrong. The WEP equates inertial and passive gravitational mass. That energy also sources gravity is the equality of active and passive mass, which is a separate statement tested by Kreuzer (ref. [21]) and lunar laser ranging. Correct the parenthesis.
- [[#N3551|N3551]] 06.03 Galileo's Thought Experiment Proof of the UFF: "Nobody seems to have found any defect in Galileo's proof till now" is incorrect. The argument and its hidden assumptions (for example that speed depends only on weight and that weight is additive) have been analysed at length, for example by J. R. Brown (1991), J. D. Norton (1996) and T. Gendler (1998). Cite this literature or soften the claim.
- [[#N3552|N3552]] 06.04 Einstein's Equivalence Principle: "the additional apparent force $\mechanical{\mathbf F}=-\mechanical{m}\mechanical{\mathbf a}$, acting opposite to the direction of motion": the inertial force is opposite to the frame's acceleration, not to its velocity. A decelerating rocket gives apparent weight towards its nose.
- [[#N3552|N3552]] 06.04 Einstein's Equivalence Principle: The physical-quantities table lists $\mechanical{g}'$, which the note never uses. Remove it or use it in the text.
- [[#N3555|N3555]] 06.07 A Brief Account of Experimental Tests: Eötvös paragraph: the horizontal torque comes from the centrifugal acceleration having a horizontal component relative to the true gravitational pull (the plumb line follows their sum), and the effect scales as $\Omega^2R_E\sin\varphi\cos\varphi$, maximal at $45^\circ$ latitude; Budapest ($47^\circ$) is a mid-latitude site, so "high-latitude location" and "Earth's gravity ... has a small horizontal component" should be corrected.
- [[#N3555|N3555]] 06.07 A Brief Account of Experimental Tests: "Washington University in Seattle" should be "the University of Washington, Seattle" (Eöt-Wash group); Washington University is in St. Louis.
- [[#N3555|N3555]] 06.07 A Brief Account of Experimental Tests: Sign convention of (6.4): with $a=(m_g/m_i)g$, one gets $\delta a/g=(m_g/m_i)_1-(m_g/m_i)_2\approx-\eta$ as $\eta$ is defined from $m_i/m_g$; either define $\eta$ with $m_g/m_i$ or write $|\eta|=|\delta a|/g$.
- [[#N3557|N3557]] 06.07.02 Laser Ranging to the Moon and the WEP: "precision of a few parts in $10^{14}$": a few millimetres over $3.84\times10^8\,\mathrm{m}$ is $\approx10^{-11}$ ($3\,\mathrm{mm}/3.84\times10^8\,\mathrm{m}=7.8\times10^{-12}$); the interpretation section's "parts in $10^{12}$" should also read "about $10^{-11}$". The $10^{-13}$–$10^{-14}$ figure applies to the inferred differential acceleration $\delta a/g$, not the range.
- [[#N3557|N3557]] 06.07.02 Laser Ranging to the Moon and the WEP: "Lunakhod" should be "Lunokhod".
- [[#N3558|N3558]] 06.07.03 Tests of the SEP: Symbol clash: the same self-energy appears as $\epsilon_g$ (defined as $GM^2/R$) and $E_g$, and the same mass as $M$ and $m$; use one symbol each, and note that for a uniform sphere $E_g=\tfrac35GM^2/R$, so Earth's actual fraction $\approx4.6\times10^{-10}$ differs from $GM/(Rc^2)=7.0\times10^{-10}$.
- [[#N3560|N3560]] 06.08 The First Applications of the EEP - Prelude to the GTR: Eq. (6.9) with the table entry "clock periods": the lower clock ($S_1$, lower potential) runs slow, so its period seen from $S_2$ is longer and $(T_1-T_2)/\bar T=+gd/c^2$; the printed sign $-gd/c^2$ is correct only if $T_1,T_2$ are elapsed proper-time readings over a common interval. Define $T$ as accumulated readings (and update the table) or flip the sign.
- [[#N3560|N3560]] 06.08 The First Applications of the EEP - Prelude to the GTR: "runs at a smaller rate $\phi/c^2$ relative to a stationary clock in gravity-free space" should read "runs slower by the fraction $|\phi|/c^2$", i.e. $d\tau/dt\approx1+\phi/c^2$ with $\phi<0$.
- [[#N3560|N3560]] 06.08 The First Applications of the EEP - Prelude to the GTR: The Planck constant is wrapped in \energy{h}; it is an action ($\mathrm{J\,s}$), so use the macro group for action or leave it uncolored as a constant.
- [[#N3563|N3563]] 06.11 The Equivalence Principle and the Quantum Theory: "the classical path in a gravitational field $g$ is exactly the same as the classical path in an accelerated frame with acceleration $-a$" contradicts (6.11) and the earlier statement $a=-g$; it should read "with acceleration $a=-g$".
- [[#N3565|N3565]] 07 References: Refs 9 and 10: Collected Papers Vol. 6 is "The Berlin Years: Writings, 1914–1917", not "1912–1914"; ref 11: Vol. 8 is "The Berlin Years: Correspondence, 1914–1918", not "1912–1914"; also "Abrahams expression" should be "Abraham's expression".
- [[#N3568|N3568]] 07.02 General Theory of Relativity as a Theory of Gravity: "$g_{00}\simeq-(1+\phi/c^2)$" is missing a factor 2 and uses the $(-,+,+,+)$ signature, while later "$g_{00}=1+h_{00}$" uses $(+,-,-,-)$; pick one signature and write $g_{00}\simeq-(1+2\phi/c^2)$ or $g_{00}\simeq1+2\phi/c^2$ consistently.
- [[#N3568|N3568]] 07.02 General Theory of Relativity as a Theory of Gravity: Eq. (7.10): with $(+,-,-,-)$, $g^{ij}=-\delta^{ij}$ and $h_{00}=2\phi/c^2$, (7.8) and (7.9) give $d^2x^i/dt^2=-c^2\Gamma^i_{00}=-(c^2/2)\partial_ih_{00}=-\partial_i\phi$; the printed $+(c^2/2)\nabla h_{00}$ has the wrong sign, and the following statement "$\Gamma^i_{00}=\nabla h_{00}$" drops the factor $1/2$.
- [[#N3568|N3568]] 07.02 General Theory of Relativity as a Theory of Gravity: The main text still states "full contraction gives $R=\kappa T$"; the callout correctly notes $R=-\kappa T$. Fix the sentence itself rather than keeping a wrong sign with a disclaimer, since (7.5) follows only from $R=-\kappa T$.
- [[#N3568|N3568]] 07.02 General Theory of Relativity as a Theory of Gravity: "time derivatives for the car are small" contains a stray word ("car"); it should read "time derivatives of the metric are small for a static field".
- [[#N3569|N3569]] 07.03 The GTR from an Action Principle: Eq. (7.12) with $d^4x$ in $\mathrm{m}^4$ (time as $ct$) has units of $\mathrm{J\,m}$, not $\mathrm{J\,s}$; the standard form is $S=\frac{1}{c}\int\left(\frac{c^4}{16\pi G}R+\mathcal L_m\right)\sqrt{-g}\,d^4x$, equivalently $\frac{c^3}{16\pi G}\int R\sqrt{-g}\,dt\,d^3x$ for the gravitational part.
- [[#N3569|N3569]] 07.03 The GTR from an Action Principle: Write the particle action as $S=-mc^2\int d\tau$ (with $\tau$ in seconds) in the text instead of keeping $-c\int m\,d\tau$ with a disclaimer.
- [[#N3570|N3570]] 07.04 The GTR as the Geometric Theory of Gravity: Eq. (7.16): Baez–Bunn give $\ddot V/V=-4\pi G(\rho+(P_x+P_y+P_z)/c^2)$, i.e. $\ddot V/V=-\tfrac12\kappa c^2(T_{00}+T_{11}+T_{22}+T_{33})$ with $T_{00}=\rho c^2$; the printed $-\kappa\sum T_{ii}$ lacks $c^2/2$ and has units $\mathrm{m^{-2}}$ instead of $\mathrm{s^{-2}}$.
- [[#N3570|N3570]] 07.04 The GTR as the Geometric Theory of Gravity: "Its components are typically $v\phi/c$": $g_{0i}$ is dimensionless; its order of magnitude is $(v/c)(\phi/c^2)$, with a factor of about 4 in linearised GR.
