- [[#N3570|N3570]] 07.04 The GTR as the Geometric Theory of Gravity: "Space-time symmetries and physical constraints reduce the geometric object to the symmetric ten-component Ricci tensor" is misleading: the Ricci tensor is a contraction of the Riemann tensor; the remaining ten Weyl components are not removed and carry the vacuum tidal field, which is why $R_{ik}=0$ outside the Sun still has curvature. Say this explicitly, consistent with 07.02.
- [[#N3571|N3571]] 07.05 Einstein's Hole Argument: "restricted to metric determinant 1": the 4 November 1915 restriction was to coordinate transformations with Jacobian (substitution) determinant 1, as the quoted sentence itself says, not to metrics with determinant 1.
- [[#N3571|N3571]] 07.05 Einstein's Hole Argument: The trace assumption $\sum T^\mu{}_\mu=0$ was introduced in the 11 November 1915 addendum, not in the first (4 November) paper; "At this stage" should say so.
- [[#N3572|N3572]] 07.05.01 Revisiting the Hole Argument: The Galilean map $x'=x-vt$ does not reduce to the identity outside L, so it is not a hole-type transformation and cannot support the conclusion drawn for the hole; it also changes the description of the matter outside L.
- [[#N3572|N3572]] 07.05.01 Revisiting the Hole Argument: Comparing $\sqrt{-\gamma_{00}}\,dt$ with $\sqrt{-\gamma'_{00}}\,dt$ at the same coordinate label compares two different physical clocks: a clock at rest in the old chart inside L is generally not at rest in the new chart, so its proper time is $\int\sqrt{-\gamma'_{\mu\nu}\dot x'^\mu\dot x'^\nu}\,dt'$, which equals the original value. Add this computation (as the interpretation section requests) or mark the claim as the author's contested view.
- [[#N3573|N3573]] 07.06 The GTR and Its Galilean Metrics: Eq. (7.21): with $x'=x-vt$, $dx=dx'+v\,dt$ gives $ds^2=-c^2dt^2(1-v^2/c^2)+2v\,dx'\,dt+dx'^2$; the cross term is $+2v$, not $-2v$, and likewise (7.22) should read $+2R^2\Omega\,d\phi'\,dt$ for $\phi'=\phi-\Omega t$.
- [[#N3573|N3573]] 07.06 The GTR and Its Galilean Metrics: Painlevé derivation: $r'=r+vt$ with $v=\sqrt{2GM/r}$ does not produce (7.23) because $v$ depends on $r$; (7.23) follows from the non-integrable substitution $dr\to dr+v(r)\,dt$ in $-c^2dt^2+dr^2+\dots$. A genuine coordinate transformation of flat spacetime cannot generate Schwarzschild curvature (Kretschmann scalar $48G^2M^2/(c^4r^6)\neq0$), and the frame is not "uniformly accelerated".
- [[#N3573|N3573]] 07.06 The GTR and Its Galilean Metrics: "the Langevin metric ... is evidently not special or general relativity": it is the Minkowski metric written in rotating coordinates (zero Riemann tensor) and is therefore a special-relativistic result; keep the claim only as an explicitly labelled author's interpretation.
- [[#N3573|N3573]] 07.06 The GTR and Its Galilean Metrics: Notation: the text uses $R,\Omega$ while the Fig. 7.4 caption uses $r,\omega$, and (7.22) contains $dR^2$ although $R$ is constant on the loop; use one set and drop $dR^2$ or explain it as the radial coordinate.
- [[#N3576|N3576]] 07.09 The GTR and Gravitomagnetism: "The potentials are of order $v/c$" should be "of order $(v/c)(GM/Rc^2)$", consistent with $B_g\sim\Omega GM/(Rc^2)$ in the next sentence.
- [[#N3576|N3576]] 07.09 The GTR and Gravitomagnetism: "measured to about 5% accuracy through LAGEOS ... and in Gravity Probe-B": the GP-B frame-dragging result $37.2\pm7.2\,\mathrm{mas/yr}$ is a 19% measurement; LAGEOS analyses claim about 10%. Quote each separately.
- [[#N3579|N3579]] 07.12 The GTR and Mach's Principle: In (7.32)–(7.33) the left side is Einstein's 1918 notation, where $G_{\mu\nu}$ denotes the Ricci tensor; with the chapter's convention ($G_{ik}$ = Einstein tensor, 07.02 and 07.04) the trace-reversed right side is wrong. Write $R_{\mu\nu}$ (or state the notation change) so that (7.32) matches (7.5).
- [[#N3579|N3579]] 07.12 The GTR and Mach's Principle: "the energy–momentum trace would then represent abnormal matter, now called the cosmological constant" is garbled: the $\lambda g_{\mu\nu}$ term acts like a source with $\rho_\Lambda=-p_\Lambda/c^2$; rephrase. Also fix the typo "Machs principle".
- [[#N3580|N3580]] 07.13 The GTR and Cosmology: Eq. (7.35) is written with $-\Lambda g_{\mu\nu}$ while (7.34) uses the $(-,+,+,+)$ signature, in which the standard Einstein equation is $G_{\mu\nu}+\Lambda g_{\mu\nu}=\kappa T_{\mu\nu}$ (positive $\Lambda$ repulsive); either change the sign or state that a $(+,-,-,-)$ convention is meant.
- [[#N3582|N3582]] 07.15 What Lies Beyond the GTR: Fig. 7.7 caption and the following line give the metric factor $1-GM/(rc^2)$; the weak-field component is $g_{00}=-(1-2GM/(rc^2))$, and $1-GM/(rc^2)$ is the clock-rate factor $\sqrt{-g_{00}}$. State which one is meant.
- [[#N3584|N3584]] 08 References: Ref 12 (Sandage, ApJ 127, 513) is from 1958, not 1948 (08.02.03 itself says 1958); ref 9 (Eddington, MNRAS 90, 668) is from 1930, not 1931; ref 8 (Lemaître translation) is MNRAS 91, 483–490 (1931), not volume 90.
- [[#N3586|N3586]] 08.01 Our Physical Universe Before 1930: Telescopes: the 100-inch Hooker telescope (1917) and the 60-inch (1908) were on Mt. Wilson, not Mt. Palomar (the 200-inch came to Palomar in 1948); Herschel's largest reflector (1789) had a 48-inch aperture. The disclaimer "The source states" does not fix the error; correct the facts.
- [[#N3586|N3586]] 08.01 Our Physical Universe Before 1930: "adding a constant potential to Poisson's equation" is wrong; Einstein added a term $-\lambda\phi$, $\nabla^2\phi-\lambda\phi=4\pi G\rho$, as 08.03 states, which then admits a constant-potential solution.
- [[#N3586|N3586]] 08.01 Our Physical Universe Before 1930: "de Sitter soon showed that the Einstein Universe expands even without matter": de Sitter's 1917 solution is a different, empty model with $\Lambda$; it was originally presented in static coordinates and its expanding interpretation came later (Lemaître 1925, Robertson 1928). Also write (8.1) and the 1915 form with $\tfrac12g_{ik}R$ in the text instead of keeping the omission with a callout.
- [[#N3586|N3586]] 08.01 Our Physical Universe Before 1930: "$\Lambda=\kappa\rho/2=1/R^2$" with $\kappa=8\pi G/c^4$ and mass density needs $\kappa\rho c^2/2$ for units of $\mathrm{m^{-2}}$.
- [[#N3587|N3587]] 08.02 The Universe as Observed: Over $5000\,\mathrm{yr}$ the scale factor changes by $H_0\Delta t\approx5000/(1.4\times10^{10})\approx3.6\times10^{-7}$, about one part in three million, not one part in ten million.
- [[#N3588|N3588]] 08.02.01 The Large Scale Distribution of Matter: "below $10^{-27}\,\mathrm{kg/m^3}$, about one hydrogen atom per cubic metre": one H atom per $\mathrm{m^3}$ is $1.7\times10^{-27}\,\mathrm{kg/m^3}$, above the quoted bound; the Planck baryon density $\Omega_b\rho_c\approx4.2\times10^{-28}\,\mathrm{kg/m^3}$ corresponds to about 0.25 H atoms per $\mathrm{m^3}$.
- [[#N3589|N3589]] 08.02.02 The Expansion of the Universe: "the period was inversely related to the 'breathing' star's size": larger, more luminous Cepheids have longer periods (pulsation period $\propto(G\bar\rho)^{-1/2}$, lower mean density for larger stars), which is why period indicates luminosity. Also Leavitt's Cepheids were in the Small Magellanic Cloud, a fact that made them all lie at a common distance.
- [[#N3589|N3589]] 08.02.02 The Expansion of the Universe: Lemaître's result is $a_o/a_e=1+z$ with $z$ the redshift; $1+v/c$ holds only for $v\ll c$. Write $1+z$ and give the low-velocity Doppler limit separately, together with the fractional form $\delta\nu/\nu=-v/c$ in the text instead of the callout.
- [[#N3590|N3590]] 08.02.03 The Velocity-Distance Relation from Observations: "a new 200-inch telescope, described in the source as at Mt. Wilson of the Palomar observatory": the 200-inch Hale telescope is on Mt. Palomar (Palomar Observatory); correct the text.
- [[#N3590|N3590]] 08.02.03 The Velocity-Distance Relation from Observations: Modern values are outdated: SH0ES gives $73.0\pm1.0\,\mathrm{km/(s\,Mpc)}$ and Planck 2018 $67.4\pm0.5\,\mathrm{km/(s\,Mpc)}$; the quoted $\pm4$ and $\pm3$ hide the 5σ "Hubble tension" that this paragraph should mention.
- [[#N3591|N3591]] 08.03 Einstein's Cosmological Constant: Eq. (8.6) mixes $\kappa=8\pi G/c^4$ with mass density $\rho$; in SI it should read $\lambda=\kappa\rho c^2/2=4\pi G\rho/c^2=1/R^2$, which also lets the reader evaluate $R$ for a given density.
- [[#N3592|N3592]] 08.03.01 The Cosmological Principle and the Expansion: Eq. (8.8) prints $f^2(t)\,d\Sigma^2$; it must be $f^2(r)\,d\Sigma^2$ as the following sentence defines. Fix it in the text rather than with a callout, and use one metric signature for (8.7) and (8.2).
- [[#N3592|N3592]] 08.03.01 The Cosmological Principle and the Expansion: Eq. (8.9): $\ddot V/V=3\ddot a/a+6(\dot a/a)^2$ for $V\propto a^3$, so the identification $\ddot V/V=3\ddot a/a$ is false as written; state that the Baez–Bunn relation applies to a small ball of test particles initially at rest relative to each other, for which the result is $3\ddot a/a$. Also write $E=\rho Vc^2$ consistently with (8.10).
- [[#N3592|N3592]] 08.03.01 The Cosmological Principle and the Expansion: Eqs. (8.15)–(8.16) drop the $\Lambda c^2/3$ terms that (8.12) and (8.14) contain; add them, otherwise the later dark-energy discussion (8.03.03) has no equation to refer to.
- [[#N3592|N3592]] 08.03.01 The Cosmological Principle and the Expansion: "this model is not entirely excluded by observations": the empty Milne model ($\Omega_k=1$) is excluded by CMB and BAO data, which give $|\Omega_k|\lesssim0.002$; update the statement.
- [[#N3593|N3593]] 08.03.02 The Concept of a Critical Density: Replace $\rho_c=H^2/(8\pi G)$ by $\rho_c=3H^2/(8\pi G)$ in both places; the quoted $9\times10^{-27}\,\mathrm{kg/m^3}$ is the value of the correct formula ($H_0=70$ gives $9.2\times10^{-27}$; the printed formula would give $3\times10^{-27}$), so the callout's "numerical estimate retained" should go.
- [[#N3593|N3593]] 08.03.02 The Concept of a Critical Density: "For $\rho>\rho_c$ the model ... eventually ... collapses" holds only for $\Lambda=0$; with the observed $\Lambda>0$ a closed model can expand forever. Add the condition in the text.
- [[#N3594|N3594]] 08.03.03 The Measurements of the Deceleration Parameter: Replace "$2\ddot a/a=8\pi G\rho/3=kc^2/a^2-H_0^2$" and "$q_0=1+kc^2/(H_0^2a^2)$" by the correct matter-only results $\ddot a/a=-4\pi G\rho/3$ and $q_0=\Omega_m/2=\tfrac12[1+kc^2/(H_0^2a^2)]$ in the text itself.
- [[#N3594|N3594]] 08.03.03 The Measurements of the Deceleration Parameter: "Adding matter at half the critical density can give $q=0$, mimicking a flat matter-free Universe" is unclear: $q_0=\Omega_m/2-\Omega_\Lambda=0$ needs $\Omega_\Lambda=\Omega_m/2$ (e.g. $\Omega_m=0.5$, $\Omega_\Lambda=0.25$, not flat), and the "flat matter-free" model with $q=0$ does not exist ($k=0$ with $\rho=0$ and $\Lambda=0$ is static Minkowski); rephrase as "mimicking the empty Milne model".
- [[#N3595|N3595]] 08.04 The Reason Behind the Expansion of the Universe: Eq. (8.23) with $\Lambda>0$ (the sign Einstein and de Sitter used, and the sign in (8.3) and (8.21)) gives oscillating $\phi$, not exponential growth; the exponent $\sqrt{-\Lambda c^2}$ is real only for $\Lambda<0$. De Sitter's result is $H=\sqrt{\Lambda c^2/3}$ with $\Lambda>0$, so "$H=\sqrt{-\Lambda c^2}$" has both the wrong sign and a missing factor 3.
- [[#N3595|N3595]] 08.04 The Reason Behind the Expansion of the Universe: Eq. (8.24) uses $\ddot a/a=\ddot\phi/\phi$, which is not derived anywhere (no relation between $a$ and $\phi$ is given), and writes $-\Lambda/(\sqrt\Lambda)^2$ although (8.23) gives $\ddot\phi/\phi=-\Lambda c^2$ and $H^2=-\Lambda c^2$; state the assumed relation $a\propto\phi$ or drop the equation.
- [[#N3595|N3595]] 08.04 The Reason Behind the Expansion of the Universe: Fix the printed expressions in the text instead of retaining them with callouts: the caption relations need $G$ ($F/m=-(4\pi G/3)\rho a$, $\ddot a/a=-4\pi G\rho/3$) and the static potential is $\phi=-4\pi G\rho/\Lambda$.
- [[#N3596|N3596]] 08.05 The Cosmic Microwave Background Radiation: CMB energy density is $aT^4=7.566\times10^{-16}\times2.7255^4\approx4.2\times10^{-14}\,\mathrm{J/m^3}$, i.e. $4.6\times10^{-31}\,\mathrm{kg/m^3}$, not $5\times10^{-30}\,\mathrm{kg/m^3}$; it is comparable to the starlight value quoted in the first sentence, not larger.
- [[#N3596|N3596]] 08.05 The Cosmic Microwave Background Radiation: Write the dipole speed as $v=1.234\times10^{-3}c\approx370\,\mathrm{km/s}$ in the text itself instead of keeping "$370\,\mathrm{m/s}$" with a callout.
- [[#N3596|N3596]] 08.05 The Cosmic Microwave Background Radiation: Fig. 8.6(b): CMB temperature anisotropies after dipole removal are not "below $50\,\mu\mathrm{K}$"; Planck maps span roughly $\pm300\,\mu\mathrm{K}$ with an rms near $100\,\mu\mathrm{K}$ ($\Delta T/T\sim10^{-5}$ on large scales); correct the band or label it as a typical large-scale amplitude.
- [[#N3597|N3597]] 08.06 The Large Scale Distribution of Matter: "nearly isotropic and homogeneous on scales below ten per cent of the Universe's size" should be "on scales above about $100\,\mathrm{Mpc}$" (a few per cent of the Hubble radius); below that scale the distribution is filamentary, as 08.02.01 says.
- [[#N3598|N3598]] 08.06.01 The Dark Matter: The 21 cm line comes from cold neutral atomic hydrogen, not "hot-gas radiation"; correct the sentence.
- [[#N3598|N3598]] 08.06.01 The Dark Matter: "A galaxy typically has a central bulge containing most of its mass": in spirals the visible mass is often dominated by the disc, the total mass by the dark halo, and the example M33 is almost bulgeless; rephrase.
- [[#N3600|N3600]] 08.06.03 The Dark Energy: Fix $p=\epsilon/(3c)$ to $p=\epsilon/3$ in the text, and write the dark-matter bound as $p_{\mathrm{dm}}<10^{-3}\rho_{\mathrm{dm}}c^2$, instead of retaining the printed forms with callouts.
- [[#N3600|N3600]] 08.06.03 The Dark Energy: "The source gives the diagonal metric entries as $(-1,-1,-1,-1)$" is not a valid Lorentzian metric; the relevant signature is $(+1,-1,-1,-1)$ (or $(-1,1,1,1)$), and with $T_{\mu\nu}=\rho_\Lambda c^2\,\mathrm{diag}(1,-1,-1,-1)$ in the first convention one reads off $p=-\rho_\Lambda c^2$.
- [[#N3601|N3601]] 08.06.04 The Dark Energy and the Quantum Vacuum: "Zero-point energy is quantum energy present even at zero kinetic energy" is wrong: the ground state of an oscillator has nonzero kinetic energy ($\langle T\rangle=\hbar\omega/4$); say "present even at zero temperature, in the lowest-energy state". Also write $p\approx-\rho c^2$ in the text instead of keeping the callout.
- [[#N3602|N3602]] 08.06.05 An Interpretation of the Critical Density: Write the energy balance as $\tfrac12m\dot r^2=\tfrac{4\pi}{3}Gm\rho r^2$ in the text instead of keeping the missing $m$ with a callout.
- [[#N3602|N3602]] 08.06.05 An Interpretation of the Critical Density: The Newtonian estimate does not give exactly $\Phi_u=-c^2$: for a uniform sphere of critical density and radius $c/H_0$ the potential is $-\tfrac12c^2$ at the surface and $-\tfrac34c^2$ at the centre ($2\pi G\rho_cR^2$); state that $-c^2$ is an order-of-magnitude identification, or show the calculation that gives it exactly.
- [[#N3603|N3603]] 08.07 The Interpretation of the Expansion of the Universe: Write $\delta\ll d$ (not $d\ll\delta$) and $\delta E=p\,\delta p/m=(1-a_e/a_r)p^2/m$ in the text instead of retaining the printed forms with callouts.
- [[#N3603|N3603]] 08.07 The Interpretation of the Expansion of the Universe: The dust-cloud collapse time is $t_{\mathrm{ff}}=\sqrt{3\pi/(32G\rho_0)}\approx0.54/\sqrt{G\rho_0}$ (Oppenheimer–Snyder), not $1/\sqrt{G\rho_0}$; call the latter an order-of-magnitude estimate or give the exact value.
- [[#N3604|N3604]] 08.08 The Absolute Features of Our Universe: Item 3: neutrinos alone contribute at least about 0.1% of critical density ($\Omega_\nu\ge0.0013$ for the minimal mass sum $0.06\,\mathrm{eV}$, and up to about 0.5% allowed), so "Light and neutrinos contribute less than $0.1\%$" is wrong; photons contribute about 0.005%.
- [[#N3604|N3604]] 08.08 The Absolute Features of Our Universe: Item 4: write $q=-\ddot a/(aH_0^2)$ in the text instead of keeping the sign error with a callout; item 2: the Hubble law in frequency is $\delta\nu/\nu=-H d/c$ (or $z=Hd/c$).
- [[#N3606|N3606]] 09 References: Ref 3: "$25$(9–15), 47–51" is not a valid issue/page citation; give it as *Phys. Today* 25(1), 9–15 and 47–51 (1972) or whatever the actual letter pages are. Ref 4 lacks its year (Naturwissenschaften 6, 697–702, 1918).
- [[#N3611|N3611]] 09.04 Langevin's Twin-Paradox: "Kinematics is symmetric except for the brief inertial, gravity-like force in B's rest frame": B has no single inertial rest frame; its worldline consists of two inertial segments, and in B's outbound and inbound frames Earth's simultaneous time jumps at the turnaround. The asymmetry is in the worldlines, not only in the force, so the "real paradox" claim does not follow from STR as stated; label it as the author's view.
- [[#N3612|N3612]] 09.05 The Real Twin-Paradox in the STR: "The STR cannot choose $t_A>t_B$ or $t_B>t_A$": once each frame's burn sequence is specified, both worldlines are known in any inertial frame and $\int d\tau$ gives unique reunion readings (equal if the reversals are symmetric, otherwise the clock that changed velocity more ages less). Freezing the clocks during burns does not change this, since the difference accumulates on the coasting legs.
- [[#N3612|N3612]] 09.05 The Real Twin-Paradox in the STR: Subscript inconsistency: "relative dilation is $\Delta T_a-\Delta T_b$" uses lowercase $a,b$ while the rest of the note uses $A,B$.
- [[#N3613|N3613]] 09.06 The Predictions for Motional Time Dilation: The STR prediction for the Mumbai–Paris trip uses only the ground-relative speed $v$ in $-v^2/(2c^2)$, treating the rotating Earth surface as inertial. Standard relativity evaluates both clocks in the non-rotating Earth-centred inertial frame, giving the transported clock's rate offset $-(v^2+2\mathbf u_r\cdot\mathbf v)/(2c^2)$ relative to the laboratory clock, the same $u_rv/c^2$ term the note attributes only to an absolute frame (this is the Hafele–Keating east–west asymmetry and the Sagnac correction). The statements "The STR says the transported clock is slower throughout" and "a westward-circling clock can run faster ... only in an absolute-frame theory" are therefore incorrect.
- [[#N3613|N3613]] 09.06 The Predictions for Motional Time Dilation: The interpretation section's claim that (9.3) "repeats a factor where its reciprocal is needed" is wrong for inertial relative motion: reciprocal dilation $dt=\sqrt{1-v^2/c^2}\,d\tau$ in the other clock's rest frame is the correct symmetric statement; the asymmetry appears only for non-inertial worldlines. Correct or remove that sentence.
- [[#N3613|N3613]] 09.06 The Predictions for Motional Time Dilation: Fix in the text the items kept with callouts: $0.78\,\mathrm{s}$ should be $0.0785\,\mathrm{s}$ ($720\,\mathrm{ns/s}\times30.3\,\mathrm{h}$), $\cos\omega t+\theta$ should be $\cos(\omega t+\theta)$ in (9.9), and (9.11) needs $\cos\phi$ in its last term. State the $\cos\phi$ used for the "19 ns" outward gain (with $\cos\phi=1$, $u_rvT/c^2-v^2T/(2c^2)=35-10.8\approx24\,\mathrm{ns}$).
- [[#N3613|N3613]] 09.06 The Predictions for Motional Time Dilation: "Mumbai's laboratory moves through the Universe at about $u=390\,\mathrm{km/s}$" conflicts with the CMB dipole speed of $370\,\mathrm{km/s}$ quoted in 08.05 for the solar system; use 370 km/s and give the annual modulation $\pm30\,\mathrm{km/s}$ around it.
- [[#N3615|N3615]] 09.07.01 Time Dilation of Unstable Particles: In the expansion $\mechanical{v}'\approx\mechanical{v}\pm\mechanical{u}^2/\mechanical{c}$: expanding $(\mechanical{v}\pm\mechanical{u})(1\mp\mechanical{u}/\mechanical{c})$ at $\mechanical{v}\approx\mechanical{c}$ gives $\mechanical{v}-\mechanical{u}^2/\mechanical{c}$ for BOTH signs; the exact composition gives $\mechanical{v}'-\mechanical{v}=\pm\mechanical{u}(1-\mechanical{v}^2/\mechanical{c}^2)/(1\pm\mechanical{u}\mechanical{v}/\mechanical{c}^2)$, i.e. a shift of order $\pm\mechanical{u}/\mechanical{\gamma}^2$, not $\pm\mechanical{u}^2/\mechanical{c}$.
- [[#N3615|N3615]] 09.07.01 Time Dilation of Unstable Particles: Eq. (9.12) should follow from the exact identity $1-\mechanical{v}'^2/\mechanical{c}^2=(1-\mechanical{v}^2/\mechanical{c}^2)(1-\mechanical{u}^2/\mechanical{c}^2)/(1\pm\mechanical{u}\mechanical{v}/\mechanical{c}^2)^2$, giving $\mechanical{\Gamma}_{\mathrm{Ab}}\approx\mechanical{\Gamma}_{\mathrm{STR}}(1\mp\mechanical{u}\mechanical{v}/\mechanical{c}^2)$; for $\mechanical{u}=400\,\unit{km/s}$ the asymmetry is about $\pm0.13\%$ independent of $\mechanical{\gamma}$, not the $\approx\pm0.9\%$ implied by $\sqrt{1\mp2\mechanical{\gamma}^2\mechanical{u}^2/\mechanical{c}^2}$ at $\mechanical{\gamma}=70$. State this explicitly instead of only the generic caveat in "Interpretation and checks".
- [[#N3615|N3615]] 09.07.01 Time Dilation of Unstable Particles: The table lists $t$ as "Creation time" and $\mechanical{\tau}'$ as a lifetime, but the text writes $\mechanical{\tau}'=\mechanical{\tau}\sqrt{1-\mechanical{v}^2/\mechanical{c}^2}$ while the interpretation says the lab lifetime is increased by $\mechanical{\gamma}$; say which of $\mechanical{\tau},\mechanical{\tau}'$ is the proper lifetime so the two statements do not appear to contradict each other.
- [[#N3616|N3616]] 09.07.02 Experiments on Atomic Systems: Eq. (9.15) $\signal{\nu}'=\signal{\nu}(1\pm\mechanical{v}/\mechanical{c})\sqrt{1-\mechanical{v}^2/\mechanical{c}^2}$ is not the special-relativistic result for a moving source; the correct lab-frame frequencies are $\signal{\nu}'=\signal{\nu}\sqrt{(1\pm\mechanical{v}/\mechanical{c})/(1\mp\mechanical{v}/\mechanical{c})}\approx\signal{\nu}(1\pm\mechanical{v}/\mechanical{c}+\mechanical{v}^2/(2\mechanical{c}^2))$, i.e. the second-order term is $+\mechanical{v}^2/(2\mechanical{c}^2)$ relative to the static line (equivalently, wavelengths $\lambda_0(1\mp\beta+\beta^2/2)$, the mean-wavelength redshift Ives and Stilwell measured). Flag this in a note or correct it.
- [[#N3616|N3616]] 09.07.02 Experiments on Atomic Systems: Eq. (9.13)/(9.14): stating that $\signal{\nu}'=\mechanical{\gamma}\signal{\nu}$ at $\mechanical{\theta}=\pi/2$ "predicts an increased received frequency" is only true when $\mechanical{\theta}$ is measured in the source frame; say which frame defines $\mechanical{\theta}$ (in the lab frame the transverse result is $\signal{\nu}/\mechanical{\gamma}$, a decrease), otherwise the claimed "ambiguity" looks like a contradiction with experiment.
- [[#N3617|N3617]] 09.07.03 Experiments on the Comparison of Atomic Clocks: The caesium hyperfine frequency is $9\,192\,631\,770\,\unit{Hz}\approx9.19\,\unit{GHz}$ (the SI-second definition), not $9.18\,\unit{GHz}$; correct the text and the table row instead of attributing the wrong value to the source.
- [[#N3617|N3617]] 09.07.03 Experiments on the Comparison of Atomic Clocks: Eq. (9.18) left side "$-\mechanical{v}^2/(2\mechanical{c}^2)-\mechanical{v}_{\mathrm{ref}}^2/(2\mechanical{c}^2)$" must be the difference $-(\mechanical{v}'^2-\mechanical{v}_{\mathrm{ref}}^2)/(2\mechanical{c}^2)$ (transported minus reference); a sum of two dilations cannot produce the $\pm$ cross term on the right.
- [[#N3617|N3617]] 09.07.03 Experiments on the Comparison of Atomic Clocks: Symbol clash: the sentence after (9.18) says "Over $t$ seconds" but the formula uses $\mechanical{T}$, and $\mechanical{v}$ is used both for the lab-relative transport speed and (in the table) generically; use $\mechanical{T}$ consistently and write the transported clock's absolute velocity as $\mechanical{v}'$.
- [[#N3618|N3618]] 09.08 The Hafele-Keating Experiment: "J. C. Hafele and R. E. Keating of the US Naval Observatory": Hafele was a physicist at Washington University in St. Louis; only Keating was at USNO.
- [[#N3618|N3618]] 09.08 The Hafele-Keating Experiment: Table 9.2 row "Absolute-frame prediction $-185\pm10$, $+104\pm10$" should say these essentially coincide with Hafele and Keating's own published kinematic predictions ($-184\pm18$, $+96\pm10\,\unit{ns}$, computed in the Earth-centred nonrotating frame), and that their total predictions $-40\pm23$ and $+275\pm21\,\unit{ns}$ match the observations; otherwise the reader thinks the standard relativistic calculation predicts the "Einstein" row $-41$, $-49$.
- [[#N3618|N3618]] 09.08 The Hafele-Keating Experiment: Table "Physical quantities": the latitude row gives unit $\unit{rad}$ but the text and Table 9.1 use degrees; use degrees or convert.
- [[#N3621|N3621]] 09.09.02 Resolution Sans Acceleration: Fig. 9.4 labels each leg "T(1 − v²/4c²)"; each leg lasts $\mechanical{T}/2$, so the aged time per leg is $(\mechanical{T}/2)(1-\mechanical{v}^2/(2\mechanical{c}^2))=\mechanical{T}/2-\mechanical{T}\mechanical{v}^2/(4\mechanical{c}^2)$. Fix the labels (the same labels are copied into Fig. 9.5 of [[09.10 Einstein's Gravitational Resolution of the Paradox]]).
- [[#N3621|N3621]] 09.09.02 Resolution Sans Acceleration: "inertial observer C moving oppositely at relative velocity $-2\mechanical{v}$" is wrong in relativity (relative speed of C to B is $2\mechanical{v}/(1+\mechanical{v}^2/\mechanical{c}^2)$); state C moves at $-\mechanical{v}$ relative to A, which is the intended set-up.
- [[#N3622|N3622]] 09.10 Einstein's Gravitational Resolution of the Paradox: The callout "Einstein's twin-paradox resolution admitted that the STR alone was insufficient" is misleading: in the 1918 dialogue, the inertial-frame STR calculation already gives a unique answer; the GTR argument only describes the same result from the traveller's accelerated frame. Attribute the claim to the author or rephrase.
- [[#N3622|N3622]] 09.10 Einstein's Gravitational Resolution of the Paradox: Fig. 9.5(a,c) leg labels "T(1 − v²/4c²)" should be $\mechanical{T}/2-\mechanical{T}\mechanical{v}^2/(4\mechanical{c}^2)$ (each leg lasts $\mechanical{T}/2$), as in Fig. 9.4.
- [[#N3623|N3623]] 09.11 Summary: "Westward clocks returned older ... contrary to the STR as presented here" should add that the standard Earth-centred-inertial relativistic calculation by Hafele and Keating predicted this westward gain ($+275\pm21\,\unit{ns}$ total), so the summary does not imply the experiment contradicted standard relativity.
- [[#N3624|N3624]] 10 References: Ref. 7 should read R. A. Lyttleton, H. Bondi, Proc. R. Soc. Lond. A 252, 313–333 (1959) (author is Lyttleton, journal is Proc. Roy. Soc. A, not Proc. Phys. Soc.).
- [[#N3625|N3625]] 10.00 Cosmic Relativity - The Theory and Its Primary Fundamental Results: "density close to critical to about 3%" is outdated: Planck 2018 + BAO give $\Omega_k=0.001\pm0.002$, i.e. flatness to a few tenths of a per cent; update the value or mark it as the source's.
- [[#N3626|N3626]] 10.01 The Universe That Determines the Physics of Relativity: The Fig. 10.1 caption says "roughly 13 billion years of slowly expanding, matter-dominated history" whereas the text says ten billion; in ΛCDM, matter dominated only until about 9.8 Gyr after the big bang and dark energy has dominated since; align the caption with the text.
- [[#N3627|N3627]] 10.02 A Hypothetical Scenario in Electrodynamics: The potential at the centre of a uniformly charged sphere is $\electric{\phi}_e=3\electric{Q}/(8\pi\electric{\epsilon}_0\mechanical{R})=\electric{q}\mechanical{R}^2/(2\electric{\epsilon}_0)$, not $3\electric{Q}/(4\pi\electric{\epsilon}_0\mechanical{R})$; with $\electric{q}=10^{-59}\,\unit{C/m^3}$ and $\mechanical{R}=10^{26}\,\unit{m}$ this gives about $6\,\unit{kV}$ (order $10^4\,\unit{V}$ still holds).
- [[#N3627|N3627]] 10.02 A Hypothetical Scenario in Electrodynamics: $\magnetic{\mathbf A}=\mechanical{\mathbf v}\electric{\phi}/\mechanical{c}$ is the Gaussian-unit form; in the SI units used elsewhere in the note (with $\electric{\epsilon}_0$) it is $\magnetic{\mathbf A}=\mechanical{\mathbf v}\electric{\phi}/\mechanical{c}^2$ in $\unit{V\,s/m}$; fix the formula and the table's "unit convention unspecified".
- [[#N3629|N3629]] 10.04 Physics in the Gravitationally Charged Universe: "$\energy{H}=\mechanical{p}^2/(2\mechanical{m})-\mechanical{m}\mechanical{\Phi}_u$ ... Such a Hamiltonian produces observable noninertial effects": a spatially and temporally constant $\mechanical{\Phi}_u$ only shifts $\energy{H}$ by a constant and leaves Hamilton's equations unchanged; say that effects arise only from the velocity-dependent (vector-potential) terms introduced later.
- [[#N3629|N3629]] 10.04 Physics in the Gravitationally Charged Universe: "CMBR ... synchronised throughout the Universe better than one part in $10^5$" conflates temperature anisotropy ($\Delta T/T\sim10^{-5}$) with timing; converting to time needs $|dT/dt|$ (here $T\propto1/a$), so state it as a temperature uniformity, not a synchronisation accuracy.
- [[#N3630|N3630]] 10.05 The Gravitational Foundation of Cosmic Relativity: (10.5)–(10.6) declare the primed (moving) interval Minkowskian and rewrite it in unprimed coordinates, so the result is the metric of the moving-frame chart expressed in rest-frame coordinates, not $\mechanical{g}'_{\mu\nu}$; substituting $\mechanical{x}=\mechanical{x}'+\mechanical{v}t'$ into the rest-frame interval (10.3) gives $\mechanical{g}'_{00}=-(1-\mechanical{v}^2/\mechanical{c}^2)$ and $\mechanical{g}'_{0x}=+\mechanical{v}/\mechanical{c}$ (cross term $+2\mechanical{v}\,d\mechanical{x}'dt'$).
- [[#N3630|N3630]] 10.05 The Gravitational Foundation of Cosmic Relativity: "spatially homogeneous cosmic potential, $\nabla^2\mechanical{\phi}_u=0$" contradicts Poisson's equation $\nabla^2\mechanical{\phi}=4\pi\mechanical{G}\mechanical{\rho}\neq0$ for uniform density; the intended statement is $\nabla\mechanical{\phi}_u=0$ (no local force), which needs the cosmological boundary argument.
- [[#N3630|N3630]] 10.05 The Gravitational Foundation of Cosmic Relativity: Symbol clash: $\mechanical{\phi}$ is the azimuthal coordinate in (10.1) and $\mechanical{\phi}_u$ the cosmic potential, while $\mechanical{\Phi}_u$ is also the cosmic potential later in the note; use $\mechanical{\Phi}_u$ throughout for the potential.
- [[#N3630|N3630]] 10.05 The Gravitational Foundation of Cosmic Relativity: "potential scales as $\mechanical{\rho}\mechanical{R}_u^2\propto\mechanical{c}^2(1/t^2)t^2$" drops $\mechanical{G}$; write $\mechanical{\Phi}_u\sim\mechanical{G}\mechanical{\rho}\mechanical{R}_u^2$ with $\mechanical{\rho}\propto1/(\mechanical{G}t^2)$ and $\mechanical{R}_u\propto\mechanical{c}t$, giving $\mechanical{\Phi}_u\propto\mechanical{c}^2$.
- [[#N3632|N3632]] 10.06.01 The Modification of Duration and Distance: The spatial metric is called $\mechanical{\gamma}_{ab}$, the same letter as the Lorentz factor used in neighbouring notes (10.06.02–10.06.04); rename it (e.g. $h_{ab}$) to avoid a clash in the chapter.
- [[#N3633|N3633]] 10.06.02 Interpretation in Terms of the Gravitational Potentials: The sentence "The source also writes $\mechanical{A}_i=\mechanical{g}_{0i}/\mechanical{g}_{00}$" gives, with 10.05's components, $(\mechanical{v}_i/\mechanical{c})\mechanical{\gamma}^2$, which is neither dimensionally nor in its $\mechanical{\gamma}$ power equal to (10.11); state this mismatch explicitly in the note box.
- [[#N3634|N3634]] 10.06.03 The Time Dilation of Physical Clocks: The symbol $\mechanical{\lambda}_r$ is introduced for $1/\mechanical{\gamma}$ and never used again; drop it or use it in (10.13).
- [[#N3636|N3636]] 10.06.05 The Propagation of Light: "total duration $\mechanical{T}=\mechanical{L}/\mechanical{c}$" for a two-way trip over $\mechanical{L}_x$ should be $2\mechanical{L}/\mechanical{c}$ (and (10.14) correspondingly $2\mechanical{L}/\mechanical{c}'$); also unify $\mechanical{L}_x$ and $\mechanical{L}$.
- [[#N3638|N3638]] 10.07.01 Laws of Dynamics - Newton's Law of Motion: In (10.16), $\frac1{\mechanical{c}}\frac{d}{dt}(\mechanical{m}\mechanical{A}'_i)=+\frac{d}{dt}(\mechanical{\gamma}\mechanical{m}\mechanical{v}_i\mechanical{\Phi}_u/\mechanical{c}^2)$ with $\mechanical{A}'_i=\mechanical{\gamma}\mechanical{v}_i\mechanical{\Phi}_u/\mechanical{c}$, yet it is equated to $-\frac{d}{dt}(\ldots)$, which is then set equal to $+\frac{\mechanical{\Phi}_u}{\mechanical{c}^2}(\ldots)$; at least two signs are inconsistent. Write $\mechanical{F}_{\mathrm{react}}=-\frac{d}{dt}(\mechanical{\gamma}\mechanical{m}\mechanical{v}_i|\mechanical{\Phi}_u|/\mechanical{c}^2)$ and the applied force as its negative.
- [[#N3638|N3638]] 10.07.01 Laws of Dynamics - Newton's Law of Motion: (10.17) "$\frac{\mechanical{\Phi}_u}{\mechanical{c}^2}\mechanical{\gamma}\mechanical{m}\frac{d\mechanical{v}}{dt}=\frac{\mechanical{\Phi}_u}{\mechanical{c}^2}\mechanical{\gamma}\frac{d\mechanical{p}}{dt}$" has an extra $\mechanical{\gamma}$: for transverse acceleration $d\mechanical{p}/dt=\mechanical{\gamma}\mechanical{m}\,d\mechanical{v}/dt$, so the right side should be $(\mechanical{\Phi}_u/\mechanical{c}^2)\,d\mechanical{p}/dt$.
- [[#N3638|N3638]] 10.07.01 Laws of Dynamics - Newton's Law of Motion: "$\mechanical{g}_{0i}=-\mechanical{v}_i/\mechanical{c}=\mechanical{A}_i$" conflicts with (10.11) $\mechanical{A}_i=-\mechanical{\gamma}\mechanical{v}_i\mechanical{\Phi}_u/\mechanical{c}$ used earlier in the same note ($\mechanical{A}'_i$); state the normalisation $\mechanical{\Phi}_u/\mechanical{c}^2=1$, $\mechanical{\gamma}\approx1$ under which they agree, or use distinct symbols.
- [[#N3641|N3641]] 10.08.02 The Centrifugal Force: (10.20) carries the sign $-\mechanical{\Phi}_u/\mechanical{c}^2$ while (10.10) gives $\mechanical{\Phi}_u\approx-\mechanical{c}^2$, which would make the reaction point inward (centripetal); use $|\mechanical{\Phi}_u|$ so the result is outward.
- [[#N3642|N3642]] 10.08.03 The Coriolis Force: The Coriolis force in a frame rotating at $\mechanical{\boldsymbol\Omega}$ is $\mechanical{\mathbf F}=-2\mechanical{m}\mechanical{\boldsymbol\Omega}\times\mechanical{\mathbf u}=+2\mechanical{m}\mechanical{\mathbf u}\times\mechanical{\boldsymbol\Omega}$; the note's $-2\mechanical{m}_i\mechanical{\mathbf u}\times\mechanical{\boldsymbol\Omega}$ (in (10.22), the text and Fig. 10.4 caption, and $\mechanical{\mathbf a}_k=-2\mechanical{\mathbf u}\times\mechanical{\boldsymbol\Omega}$) has the opposite sign and would deflect northern-hemisphere winds to the left. The note's own "Interpretation and checks" states the correct form.
- [[#N3642|N3642]] 10.08.03 The Coriolis Force: In (10.22), $\mechanical{\mathbf A}_g=-\mechanical{\gamma}\mechanical{\Phi}_u\mechanical{\mathbf v}/\mechanical{c}$ gives $\nabla\times\mechanical{\mathbf A}_g=-(\mechanical{\gamma}\mechanical{\Phi}_u/\mechanical{c})\nabla\times\mechanical{\mathbf v}$, but the next step writes $\mechanical{\gamma}\mechanical{\Phi}_u/\mechanical{c}^2$; fix the power of $\mechanical{c}$ (and the coupling's units) and show $\nabla\times(\mechanical{\boldsymbol\Omega}\times\mechanical{\mathbf r})=2\mechanical{\boldsymbol\Omega}$ explicitly.
- [[#N3643|N3643]] 10.09 The Twist in Tropical Cyclones: "Its component at latitude $\mechanical{\lambda}$ is $\mechanical{\Omega}\sin\mechanical{\lambda}$" contradicts $\mechanical{\mathbf B}_g\approx-2\mechanical{\boldsymbol\Omega}$ and the caption; the vertical component is $2\mechanical{\Omega}\sin\mechanical{\lambda}$ (the Coriolis parameter $f$).
- [[#N3643|N3643]] 10.09 The Twist in Tropical Cyclones: $\mechanical{\Phi}_i$ in the $\mechanical{\mathbf B}_g$ formula is undefined (presumably $\mechanical{\Phi}_u$), and the force $-2\mechanical{m}\mechanical{\mathbf v}\times\mechanical{\boldsymbol\Omega}\sin\mechanical{\lambda}$ inherits the sign error of 10.08.03; the standard horizontal Coriolis force is $-\mechanical{m}f\,\hat{\mathbf z}\times\mechanical{\mathbf v}$ with $f=2\mechanical{\Omega}\sin\mechanical{\lambda}$.
- [[#N3646|N3646]] 10.10.02 Weightlessness in Free Fall and the EEP: (10.24) "$-\mechanical{m}\mechanical{\mathbf g}=-\mechanical{m}\nabla\mechanical{\phi}_l$" contradicts the note's own $\mechanical{\mathbf g}=-\nabla\mechanical{\phi}$; the gravitational force is $\mechanical{m}\mechanical{\mathbf g}=-\mechanical{m}\nabla\mechanical{\phi}_l=\mechanical{m}_i\mechanical{\mathbf a}$, so free fall gives $\mechanical{\mathbf a}=\mechanical{\mathbf g}$ (not $\mechanical{\mathbf g}=-\mechanical{\mathbf a}$), and the induced force (10.23) is $-\mechanical{m}_i\mechanical{\mathbf a}=-\mechanical{m}_i\mechanical{\mathbf g}$. Correct the chain instead of retaining it.
- [[#N3646|N3646]] 10.10.02 Weightlessness in Free Fall and the EEP: (10.23) uses $\mechanical{\Phi}$ without subscript and a partial derivative $\partial\mechanical{\mathbf v}/\partial t$ of a particle velocity, and the text uses $\mechanical{\phi}$ and $\mechanical{\phi}_l$ for the same local potential; use $\mechanical{\Phi}_u$, $d\mechanical{\mathbf v}/dt$ and one symbol $\mechanical{\phi}_l$.
- [[#N3646|N3646]] 10.10.02 Weightlessness in Free Fall and the EEP: The electromagnetic analogue "$\mechanical{F}=-\electric{e}\,d\magnetic{A}_i/(\mechanical{c}\,dt)$" with "$\magnetic{A}_i=\mechanical{v}_i\electric{\phi}/\mechanical{c}$" is Gaussian; in SI it is $\mechanical{F}=-\electric{e}\,d\magnetic{A}_i/dt$ with $\magnetic{A}_i=\mechanical{v}_i\electric{\phi}/\mechanical{c}^2$.
- [[#N3647|N3647]] 10.10.03 Two Kinds of Gravitational Forces and the Geodesic Principle: Beyond units, the sign is off: with $\mechanical{g}_{0i}=-\mechanical{v}/\mechanical{c}$, $-\mechanical{c}\,d\mechanical{g}_{0i}/dt=+d\mechanical{v}/dt$, not $-d\mechanical{v}/dt$; replace the displayed relation and the note box by $\mechanical{g}_a=-\mechanical{c}\,d\mechanical{g}_{0i}/dt=d\mechanical{v}/dt$ (or define the induced field with the opposite sign explicitly).
- [[#N3649|N3649]] 10.11 The EEP and the Time Dilation of Clocks in an Accelerated Frame: With $\mechanical{d}=\mechanical{x}_1-\mechanical{x}_2$ and uniform $\mechanical{\mathbf g}=-\nabla\mechanical{\phi}$ along $x$, $\mechanical{\phi}(\mechanical{x}_1)-\mechanical{\phi}(\mechanical{x}_2)=-\mechanical{g}\mechanical{d}$, so the small-separation form is $\Delta T=-T\mechanical{g}\mechanical{d}/\mechanical{c}^2$ unless $\mechanical{d}$ is defined as the height of C1 above C2 against the field; fix so the higher clock runs faster.
- [[#N3649|N3649]] 10.11 The EEP and the Time Dilation of Clocks in an Accelerated Frame: The Lorentz factor is written $\signal{\gamma}$; it is a kinematic quantity and should use $\mechanical{\gamma}$ as in the rest of the chapter.
- [[#N3652|N3652]] 10.12.02 Motional Time Dilation in Cosmic Relativity: $\signal{\gamma}$ for the Lorentz factor should be $\mechanical{\gamma}$, consistent with the rest of the vault.
- [[#N3652|N3652]] 10.12.02 Motional Time Dilation in Cosmic Relativity: "$\energy{\delta E}_g=\mechanical{m}\,\delta\mechanical{\phi}$" wraps the variation operator in the macro and conflicts in sign with $\energy{E}_g=-\mechanical{m}\mechanical{\Phi}_u$; write $\delta\energy{E}_g=-\mechanical{m}\,\delta\mechanical{\phi}$ or state the magnitude convention.
- [[#N3653|N3653]] 10.12.03 Synchronisation of Clocks in Cosmic Relativity: "uniform to a few microkelvin, ... better than one part in a million" is incorrect: after removing the $3.36\,\unit{mK}$ dipole, intrinsic CMB anisotropies are tens of $\unit{\mu K}$ ($\Delta T/T\sim10^{-5}$, as [[10.04 Physics in the Gravitationally Charged Universe]] says); the current mean is $2.7255\,\unit{K}$.
- [[#N3654|N3654]] 10.12.04 The Addition of Velocities in Cosmic Relativity: $\signal{\gamma}$ for the Lorentz factor should be $\mechanical{\gamma}$.
- [[#N3657|N3657]] 10.13.02 The Optical Aberration and the Fresnel Drag: "Refraction reduces the angle by $1/\signal{n}$, so the inferred additional aberration remains $\mechanical{v}/\mechanical{c}$": to go from $\mechanical{v}/(\mechanical{c}\signal{n})$ inside to $\mechanical{v}/\mechanical{c}$ outside, refraction must multiply the angle by $\signal{n}$ (small-angle Snell, $\theta_{\mathrm{out}}=\signal{n}\theta_{\mathrm{in}}$).
- [[#N3657|N3657]] 10.13.02 The Optical Aberration and the Fresnel Drag: The text calls the relative speeds $\mechanical{c}'\mp\mechanical{v}$, but (10.39) uses $\mechanical{c}/\signal{n}\pm\mechanical{v}/\signal{n}^2$; with (10.38), $\mechanical{c}'-\mechanical{v}=\mechanical{c}/\signal{n}-\mechanical{v}/\signal{n}^2$, so define $\mechanical{c}'_\pm=\mechanical{c}/\signal{n}\pm\mechanical{v}/\signal{n}^2$ explicitly as the apparatus-frame speeds against and along the motion.
- [[#N3658|N3658]] 10.14 The Unipolar Induction: (10.40) equates a scalar integral of $\electric{i}_1\,d\mechanical{l}\cdot\electric{i}_2$ with the vector $-\electric{q}\mechanical{v}\times\magnetic{\mathbf B}$, while the following text gives the Lorentz force $+\electric{q}\mechanical{v}\times\magnetic{\mathbf B}$; the force on a charge moving near a long wire is $\electric{q}\mechanical{\mathbf v}\times\magnetic{\mathbf B}$ with $\magnetic{B}=\magnetic{\mu}_0\electric{i}/(2\pi\mechanical{r})$. Fix sign and vector form.
- [[#N3660|N3660]] 10.16 Summary: The summary gives $\mechanical{B}_g=-2\boldsymbol{\Omega}\mechanical{\Phi}_u/\mechanical{c}^2$ whereas [[10.15 Cosmic Relativity and the Spin Angular Momentum]] gives $-2\boldsymbol{\Omega}$; state the normalisation $|\mechanical{\Phi}_u|=\mechanical{c}^2$ or use one form.
- [[#N3660|N3660]] 10.16 Summary: $\signal{\gamma}$ in the scalar and vector potentials should be $\mechanical{\gamma}$.
- [[#N3661|N3661]] 11 References: Ref. 8 (Krisher et al.) is Phys. Rev. D 42, 731–734 (1990), not "Phys. Rev. 42 ... (1980)".
- [[#N3664|N3664]] 11.01.01 Past Experiments on the One-Way Propagation of Light: The text describing Ruderfer's rotating disc points to "(Fig. 11.1)", but the Fig. 11.1 caption describes the Krisher et al. fibre experiment; either move the reference to the Krisher paragraph or add a separate schematic for the disc.
- [[#N3667|N3667]] 11.03.01 The Propagation of Light in a Moving Frame: For the looped path the stationary-frame travel time is not $\mechanical{L}/[\mechanical{c}_w(1-\mechanical{v}/\mechanical{c}_w)]$: summing segments gives $\Delta t\approx\mechanical{L}/\mechanical{c}_w+(\mechanical{v}/\mechanical{c}_w^2)\times$(A-to-B displacement along $\mechanical{\mathbf v}$), which is $\mechanical{L}/\mechanical{c}_w$ to first order when B is next to A (for the tabulated loop: $+2\mechanical{l}$ along, $-2\mechanical{l}$ against). Hence (11.8) gives $\Delta t'\approx\mechanical{L}/\mechanical{c}$ for light, not $\mechanical{L}/(\mechanical{c}-\mechanical{v})$, and the GT and Galilean (11.10) loop results also lose their first-order term.
- [[#N3667|N3667]] 11.03.01 The Propagation of Light in a Moving Frame: (11.9) divides the open-path displacement $\Delta\mechanical{x}'=\signal{\gamma}\mechanical{L}$ by the loop duration; for a loop the endpoint displacement is about zero and $\mechanical{L}$ is a path length, so the ratio is not a velocity.
- [[#N3667|N3667]] 11.03.01 The Propagation of Light in a Moving Frame: The Lorentz factor is written $\signal{\gamma}$; use $\mechanical{\gamma}$.
- [[#N3668|N3668]] 11.03.02 A Simple Demonstration of the Conflict Between the PoR and the Light Hypothesis: (11.11) uses $\mechanical{L}/[\mechanical{c}(1-\mechanical{v}/\mechanical{c})]$ for a light circuit of a loop co-moving with the detector; for a closed loop the first-order terms cancel (see [[11.03 The True Relative Velocity of Light - A Prelude to a Test]]), so the light circuit time is $\mechanical{L}/\mechanical{c}$ in the apparatus frame and $N$ is not $(\mechanical{c}-\mechanical{v})/(\mechanical{c}_s-\mechanical{v})$.
- [[#N3669|N3669]] 11.04 The Experiment on the One-Way Relative Velocity of Light: Fig. 11.5(a) states that the four mirrors are fixed and only source, optics and detector translate; then in the lab frame (mirrors and light at rest) standard relativity predicts a counter-propagating delay $2\mechanical{L}\mechanical{v}/\mechanical{c}^2$, i.e. $2\times(3.1\,\unit{m}/\mechanical{c})\times\mechanical{v}/\mechanical{c}\approx7\times10^{-17}\,\unit{s}$ per $\unit{m/s}$, which matches the plotted slope (350 mV per m/s at 10 mV per $2\times10^{-18}\,\unit{s}$). The result therefore does not discriminate; this must be stated, since criterion 1 (co-moving A, B and path) is not met.
- [[#N3669|N3669]] 11.04 The Experiment on the One-Way Relative Velocity of Light: The sound-test check is consistent ($\mechanical{T}\mechanical{v}/\mechanical{c}_s=26\,\unit{ms}/343\approx76\,\unit{\mu s}$ per m/s versus a plotted slope of $80\,\unit{\mu s}$ per m/s), which confirms that the "$5\,\unit{ms}$" precision must be $5\,\unit{\mu s}$; correct it rather than retaining it in a note box.
- [[#N3671|N3671]] 11.06 Cosmic Relativity and Clock Synchronisation: (11.14) defines $\mechanical{\mathbf v}_r$ as receiver velocity but then uses $\mechanical{\mathbf v}$; use one symbol.
- [[#N3672|N3672]] 11.07 Experimental Tests of Time Dilation - Atomic Clocks: $\mechanical{\mathbf l}_i$ in (11.17) is not defined; state that $\mechanical{\mathbf l}_i=\mechanical{\mathbf v}_it_i$ is the directed segment.
- [[#N3673|N3673]] 11.08 Experimental Tests of Time Dilation - GNSS and GPS: GPS satellites at $26\,560\,\unit{km}$ orbital radius move at $\sqrt{\mechanical{G}\mechanical{M}/r}\approx3.87\,\unit{km/s}$, not $3.6\,\unit{km/s}$.
- [[#N3673|N3673]] 11.08 Experimental Tests of Time Dilation - GNSS and GPS: "Bidou" should be BeiDou, and Japan's system is QZSS (Quasi-Zenith Satellite System), not "QNSS"; QZSS and NavIC use geosynchronous inclined as well as geostationary orbits.
- [[#N3674|N3674]] 11.08.01 Time Dilations in the GNSS Satellites: With $\mechanical{G}\mechanical{M}=3.986\times10^{14}\,\unit{m^3/s^2}$, $\mechanical{R}_0=6371\,\unit{km}$, $\mechanical{R}_s=26\,560\,\unit{km}$: $\mechanical{G}\mechanical{M}/(\mechanical{R}_0\mechanical{c}^2)=6.95\times10^{-10}$ (not $7.3\times10^{-10}$), the gravitational shift is $0.53\,\unit{ns/s}$ ($45.7\,\unit{\mu s/day}$), and the motional shift with $\mechanical{v}_s=3.87\,\unit{km/s}$ is $-0.083\,\unit{ns/s}$ ($-7.2\,\unit{\mu s/day}$), not $-0.07$; net $+38.5\,\unit{\mu s/day}$.
- [[#N3676|N3676]] 11.09 The Absence of a Relative Time Dilation in Accelerated Frames: Replace the retained values in the text by the correct ones already identified in the note box: $10\,\unit{mm}$ of light path is $33\,\unit{ps}$, $10^{-13}\,\unit{s}$ corresponds to $30\,\unit{\mu m}$, and a $10\,\unit{m}$ vertical separation on Earth accumulates about $0.1\,\unit{ns}$ per day.
- [[#N3676|N3676]] 11.09 The Absence of a Relative Time Dilation in Accelerated Frames: $\mechanical{f}_g=d\mechanical{A}_g/dt$ uses the macro letter $\mechanical{f}$ for a field per unit mass while the chapter otherwise writes induced acceleration as $-\mechanical{c}\,d\mechanical{g}_{0i}/dt$; state units and normalisation.
- [[#N3678|N3678]] 11.10.01 An Early History of the Relevant Ideas: The text dates Lodge's work to 1893 while citing ref. [15] from 1897; cite both papers (Phil. Trans. A 184, 727 (1893) and 189, 149 (1897)) or adjust the year.
- [[#N3679|N3679]] 11.10.02 The Experiments by G. Sagnac: The symbol $\mechanical{v}=\mechanical{R}\signal{\omega}$ in (11.26) uses $\signal{\omega}$ while the general formula uses $\boldsymbol{\omega}$ without macro, and 11.08.02 uses $\boldsymbol{\omega}$ for Earth rotation; use one convention for angular velocity in the chapter.
- [[#N3680|N3680]] 11.10.03 The Michelson-Gale Experiment: "Earth's rotation rate $2\pi/86400\,\mathrm{rad/s}$" is the solar-day value; the rotation rate relative to inertial space is the sidereal $2\pi/86164\,\mathrm{s}\approx7.292\times10^{-5}\,\mathrm{rad/s}$.
- [[#N3681|N3681]] 11.10.04 The Proof of the Galilean Nature of a Rotating Frame: The "moving-frame line element" is written in unprimed $dx$; substituting $x=x'\pm vt$ gives $ds^2=dx'^2\pm2v\,dx'\,dt-c^2(1-v^2/c^2)dt^2$, and the null condition $ds=0$ then yields $dx'/dt=c\mp v$, which is the check the note should display.
- [[#N3681|N3681]] 11.10.04 The Proof of the Galilean Nature of a Rotating Frame: "$c'=R\,d\phi/dt=c\mp R\omega$" uses the stationary angle; the relative light speed is $c'=R\,d\phi'/dt$ (with $d\phi/dt=c/R$ in the stationary frame).
- [[#N3684|N3684]] 12 References: Entry 5 is garbled: "A tribute to G., ed. by G. Umesh et al. (Ramachandran, ...)" should read "A tribute to G. Ramachandran, ed. by G. Umesh et al. (Sriranga Digital Software Technologies, ...)"; entry 18's title is *The Principles of Quantum Mechanics*.
- [[#N3686|N3686]] 12.01 Cosmic Relativity and Quantum Dynamics: "$\Delta x\,\Delta p\ge\hbar$" is not the standard bound; for standard deviations the Kennard relation is $\Delta x\,\Delta p\ge\hbar/2$. State it and keep the source's form only as a quoted variant.
- [[#N3687|N3687]] 12.02 The True Nature of the Schrodinger Equation: "momentum represented in the source by $i\hbar\nabla$" has the wrong sign; the position-space operator is $\hat{\mathbf p}=-i\hbar\nabla$, and the sign fixes the direction of the probability current in (12.10).
- [[#N3687|N3687]] 12.02 The True Nature of the Schrodinger Equation: "The two path probabilities are written as $a^2$ and $b^2$" (and the coefficients $a,b,c$ in (12.16)) treat complex amplitudes as real; the probabilities are $|a|^2$ and $|b|^2$.
- [[#N3689|N3689]] 12.04 The Quantum Interference of Single Particles: Symbol clash: $a,b$ are both the path weights and the labels in $S(a)$, $S(b)$, and (12.22) defines $\zeta_B$ while (12.23)–(12.24) use $\zeta$. Write $S_1,S_2$ for the path actions and use one name for the combined wave.
- [[#N3692|N3692]] 12.07 The Minuteness of the Quantum Zero-Point Energy: Symbol clash: $p$ is momentum ($p$, $p_0$) and also pressure ($p=-\rho c^2$) in the same note; rename the pressure $P$.
- [[#N3693|N3693]] 12.08 The Dirac Equation and Relativity: "$\hat p_j=i\hbar\,\partial/\partial x_j$" has the wrong sign; the operator is $\hat p_j=-i\hbar\,\partial/\partial x_j$.
- [[#N3696|N3696]] 13 References: Fix the entries that can be verified: Pauli 1940 is Phys. Rev. **58**, 716–722 (not 48); Berry 1984 is Proc. R. Soc. Lond. A **392**, 45–57; Uhlenbeck's initial is G.; Duck and Sudarshan, Am. J. Phys. **66**, 284 is 1998; "Lamoroux" is Lamoreaux; Bose, Z. Phys. **26** starts on page 178.
- [[#N3697|N3697]] 13.00 Cosmic Gravity and the Quantum Spin: "the source writes the electromagnetic coupling as $E=\boldsymbol\mu\cdot\mathbf B$"; the dipole energy is $E=-\boldsymbol\mu\cdot\mathbf B$, which matters because the gravitational analogy is built on it.
- [[#N3697|N3697]] 13.00 Cosmic Gravity and the Quantum Spin: Torque (13.3) $\mathbf T=\mathbf s\times\mathbf B_g/2$ does not follow from energy (13.2): $H=\tfrac12\mathbf s\cdot\mathbf B_g=-\mathbf s\cdot\boldsymbol\Omega$ gives $d\mathbf s/dt=\tfrac12\mathbf B_g\times\mathbf s=-\boldsymbol\Omega\times\mathbf s$, the familiar apparent precession of a free gyroscope in a rotating frame, whereas (13.3) gives the opposite sign.
- [[#N3698|N3698]] 13.01 The Physical Meaning of Spin: The table calls $s$ the "magnitude", but the text uses $s=\hbar/2$ as the maximal projection ($+s,\dots,-s$); the magnitude of spin-½ angular momentum is $\sqrt{s(s+1)}\,\hbar=(\sqrt3/2)\hbar$. Distinguish the quantum number $s$, the magnitude, and the projection $m_s\hbar$.
- [[#N3699|N3699]] 13.02 Spin as the Fundamental Gravitomagnetic Moment: (13.6) $d\mathbf s/dt=\tfrac12\mathbf s\times\mathbf B_g$ is inconsistent with (13.5): the Heisenberg or Poisson equation from $H=\tfrac12\mathbf s\cdot\mathbf B_g$ gives $d\mathbf s/dt=\tfrac12\mathbf B_g\times\mathbf s=-\tfrac12\mathbf s\times\mathbf B_g$.
- [[#N3700|N3700]] 13.03 Cosmic Gravitational Effects on Spin: With $\mathbf s=\hbar\boldsymbol\sigma/2$, the derived term $\hbar\boldsymbol\sigma\cdot\boldsymbol\Omega$ in (13.10) equals $2\,\mathbf s\cdot\boldsymbol\Omega$, not "$+\mathbf s\cdot\boldsymbol\Omega$". The minimal-coupling route gives a gyrogravitational factor 2, like $g=2$, which conflicts in magnitude as well as sign with (13.2) $E_g=-\mathbf s\cdot\boldsymbol\Omega$. State this explicitly instead of the vague normalisation note.
- [[#N3701|N3701]] 13.03.01 Emphasising the Spin-Phase Puzzle: Here $\mathbf B_g=+2\boldsymbol\omega$ and $E_g=+\mathbf s\cdot\boldsymbol\omega$, whereas 13.00 and 13.02 use $\mathbf B_g=-2\boldsymbol\Omega$ and $E_g=-\mathbf s\cdot\boldsymbol\Omega$; state the orientation of $\boldsymbol\omega$ relative to the orbit so that the signs agree within the chapter.
- [[#N3704|N3704]] 13.04 Spin Transport in Chiral Molecules and Spintronics: Equating the per-state energy $\hbar\Omega/2$ ($=s\Omega$ with $s=\hbar/2$) with the per-state Zeeman energy $\tfrac g2\mu_BB=\mu_BB$ gives $B=\hbar\Omega/(2\mu_B)=mv/(er)\approx5.7\times10^3\,\mathrm{T}$. The printed $B_{eq}=\hbar\Omega/(2g_m\mu_B)$ and $B_f=mv/(2er)\approx2.8\times10^3\,\mathrm{T}$ set a per-state energy equal to the full splitting $g\mu_BB$ and halve the field.
- [[#N3704|N3704]] 13.04 Spin Transport in Chiral Molecules and Spintronics: Room-temperature thermal energy is $k_BT\approx4.1\times10^{-21}\,\mathrm{J}=0.026\,\mathrm{eV}$, not $3\times10^{-21}\,\mathrm{J}$; the ratio to 0.66 eV is about 25.
- [[#N3706|N3706]] 13.05.01 The Dawn of the Spin-Statistics Connection: "Dirac named the integer-spin particles bosons ... in his 1926 paper" is wrong: Dirac coined both "fermion" and "boson" in a 1945 lecture. His 1926 paper derived the antisymmetric (Fermi–Dirac) statistics.
- [[#N3711|N3711]] 14 References: Bose, Z. Phys. **26**, starts on page 178 (178–181), not 168–171.
- [[#N3715|N3715]] 14.03 The 2-D Dynamics of Electrons in a Magnetic Field: The Fig. 14.4 graph draws levels at heights 0.5, 1, 2, 3 (labels ½ℏω, ℏω, 2ℏω, 3ℏω), which is not equally spaced and contradicts $E_n=(n+\tfrac12)\hbar\omega_c$. Redraw at 0.5, 1.5, 2.5, 3.5 with labels $(n+\tfrac12)\hbar\omega_c$ and keep the source labels in the caption only.
- [[#N3717|N3717]] 14.04 The Fractional Quantum Hall Effect: Fig. 14.7 draws a deep longitudinal-resistance minimum at $\nu=1/4$, but 1/4 is an even-denominator filling without an FQHE plateau (the chapter itself says so in 14.06.01 and 14.07.01). Replace it with an odd-denominator state such as $3/7$ or $2/9$, or draw 1/4 without a minimum.
- [[#N3728|N3728]] 14.10 The Quantum Hall Effects in Graphene: "Two spin projections and two sublattices add a fourfold degeneracy" is wrong: the fourfold degeneracy comes from spin and valley ($K$, $K'$). The two sublattices form the pseudospin components of each Dirac spinor.
- [[#N3728|N3728]] 14.10 The Quantum Hall Effects in Graphene: With the stated rule that successive orbit areas differ by one flux quantum ($\pi r_0^2B=h/e$, so $r_0^2=2\hbar/(eB)$), (14.17) gives $E_n=v_F\sqrt{\hbar eBn}$, a factor $\sqrt2$ below the printed (and correct) $v_F\sqrt{2\hbar eBn}$. The printed step works only if $r_0=l_0=\sqrt{\hbar/(eB)}$; add this to the note.
- [[#N3730|N3730]] 14.12 The Wavefunctions in the QHE: Symbol clash: $m$ is the single-particle angular-momentum index in (14.22) and the Laughlin exponent in (14.23); use, for example, $\ell$ for the former and $q$ (with $\nu=1/q$) for the latter.
- [[#N3732|N3732]] 15 References: Entry 7: "Stud. Hist. Phil. Set." should be "Stud. Hist. Phil. Sci." (Studies in History and Philosophy of Science).
- [[#N3735|N3735]] 15.02 Quantum Mechanics of Entanglement: (15.4) writes "$\Psi'=\psi_A\psi_B$" after A is found positive; the updated state is $\psi_{A+}\psi_B$ (up to normalisation), as the right-hand side shows.
- [[#N3738|N3738]] 15.04.01 The Correlations in the LHVT: With $a=0^\circ$, $a'=90^\circ$, $b=45^\circ$, $b'=-45^\circ$ (Fig. 15.3a), the $135^\circ$ pair is $(a',b')$, not $(a,b')$ as the text states. With $-\cos\theta$, the combination $(ab)+(a'b)+(a'b')-(ab')$ then evaluates to 0. Use $b'=+135^\circ$ (so $(a,b')=135^\circ$ and the other pairs $45^\circ$, giving $|B|=2\sqrt2$) or move the minus sign to $(a'b')$.
- [[#N3739|N3739]] 15.05 The Proof of Strict Locality in Quantum Correlations: The quantities table lists $s,s_+,s_-$ twice with conflicting units (J·s in one row, dimensionless "units of ℏ" in another), while (15.16)–(15.20) use them as dimensionless; keep one row with the dimensionless meaning.
- [[#N3748|N3748]] Universal Clock of Cosmic Relativity: The main metric prints "$r^2a\theta^2$"; it must be $r^2d\theta^2$.
- [[#N3748|N3748]] Universal Clock of Cosmic Relativity: "$-ds^2$ is the Spacetime Interval" and the unrendered "\((-+++)\)" are wrong or broken: $ds^2$ is the interval, with signature $(-,+,+,+)$ written in math delimiters.
- [[#N3748|N3748]] Universal Clock of Cosmic Relativity: "Static Universe ($a(t)=1$)" is misleading: $a=1$ at one instant is only a normalisation; a static universe needs $\dot a=0$ at all times, which for nonzero matter requires $\Lambda$ (the Einstein static universe) and is not a general special case of FLRW.
- [[#N3749|N3749]] AC impedance, Maxwell waves, and energy flux: The Physical quantities table lists symbols and meanings that belong to other notes: $\electric{V}$ potential, $\electric{q}_1,\electric{q}_2$, $\electric{Q}$ "charge along the semicircular arc", $\mechanical{A}$ "area of the surface charge", $\electric{\Phi}_{E,\mathrm{net}}$, $\electric{I}_2$–$\electric{I}_6$ "bridge branch", $N$ turn count, $\energy{P}$ "resistive element" (here $\energy{P}$ is the isotropic source power) and $\electric{\mathcal{E}}$ "charging loop"; delete or correct these, and add the missing $\magnetic{\Phi}_{\mathrm m}$, $\electric{\Phi}_{\mathrm E}$, $\electric{\vec J}$ and $\electric{I}_{\mathrm{through}}$.
- [[#N3749|N3749]] AC impedance, Maxwell waves, and energy flux: Symbol clashes: $\vec A$ is used for the area vector, for a generic field in the divergence definition and in the triple-product identity $\vec A\times(\vec B\times\vec C)$ (where $\vec B$ also looks like the magnetic field), and $\mechanical{p}$ (momentum) sits next to $\mechanical{p}_{\mathrm{rad}}$ (pressure); use $\vec F$ or $\vec u,\vec v,\vec w$ for the generic vectors and $P_{\mathrm{rad}}$ for the pressure.
- [[#N3749|N3749]] AC impedance, Maxwell waves, and energy flux: In "Electromagnetic wave speed", $1/\sqrt{\mu_0\varepsilon_0}=2.998\times10^8\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ rounds to $3.00\times10^8$, not "$\approx2.99\times10^8$"; also in "Inductor in an AC circuit" write $\electric{\mathcal E}_L=-\circuit{L}\,\mathrm d\electric{i}_L/\mathrm dt$ with the lowercase instantaneous current the note's convention requires.
- [[#N3750|N3750]] Acoustic Doppler shift and wave optics practice: The Physical quantities table gives wrong meanings: $\signal{\tau}$ is "amplitude decay time" but here it is the source period, $\mechanical{M}$ is "reduced mass" but here it is the rope or wire mass, $\mechanical{\theta}$ is "local tangent angle" but here it is the Doppler direction angle and the ray angles, and $d$ "string dispersion coefficient" never appears (the note's $\mechanical{d}$ is the lateral offset); rebuild the table from the symbols actually used.
- [[#N3750|N3750]] Acoustic Doppler shift and wave optics practice: Symbol clashes: $\mechanical{u}$ is the source speed in the Doppler derivation but the observer speed in "Doppler shift for a moving observer", alongside $\mechanical{v}_s,\mechanical{v}_o$; $\mechanical{A}$ is the wave amplitude and the wire cross-section in Exercise 78; $\mechanical{v}$ is the wave speed and the mass velocity in Quiz 2; use $u_s,u_o$ consistently and a distinct symbol for the cross-section.
- [[#N3750|N3750]] Acoustic Doppler shift and wave optics practice: In "Two coherent sources", a point "2 m in front of $S_1$" with sources 1 m apart is $\sqrt5\approx2.24\,\mathrm m$ from $S_2$ if "in front" means perpendicular; state that the point lies on the line through both sources (collinear geometry) for the 3 m distance to be consistent. Also note that 60 mph is $26.8\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, so Exercise 8-8 should say the notes' $26.6$ is a rounding of that value.
- [[#N3751|N3751]] Conducting boundaries, image charges, and Green functions: "For a point charge on the right of a plane held at zero potential, use the potential of two charges on the right-hand side" is wrong as written: the image $-\electric{Q}$ sits on the left at $x=-\mechanical{a}$; say "in the right-hand region, use the potential of the real charge and its mirror image on the left". Also the sphere image is called $\electric{q}$ in one paragraph and $\electric{q}'$ in the next; pick one.
- [[#N3752|N3752]] Electric potential on the axis of a charged disk: The Sources links go to "#Dipole in an electric field" and "#Concave mirror", neither of which treats a charged disk; link instead to "Superposition, electric flux, and Gauss’s law problems#Charge density" (or "#A plane of charge") and to the disk derivation in [[Electric potential, capacitors, and Kirchhoff calculations#Potential on the axis of a charged disk]].
- [[#N3753|N3753]] Electric potential, capacitors, and Kirchhoff calculations: In the line-integral example, $\mathrm d\mechanical{\vec s}=5\,\mathrm d\mechanical{x}\,\hat\imath+3\,\mathrm d\mechanical{y}\,\hat\jmath+\mathrm d\mechanical{z}\,\hat k$ is not a displacement element; it must be $\mathrm dx\,\hat\imath+\mathrm dy\,\hat\jmath+\mathrm dz\,\hat k$, giving $\mathrm dV=-500xy^2\,\mathrm dx-30\,\mathrm dy$. Moreover $\vec E=500xy^2\hat\imath+30\hat\jmath$ has $\nabla\times\vec E=-1000xy\,\hat k\neq0$, so it is not an electrostatic field and $\Delta V$ depends on the path; state the path or choose a curl-free field.
- [[#N3753|N3753]] Electric potential, capacitors, and Kirchhoff calculations: Air breaks down at about $3\times10^6\,\mathrm{V\,m^{-1}}$, not $3\times10^5$; and in "Molecular view" the field of the bound surface charge is $\electric{E}_{\mathrm{induced}}=\electric{\eta}_{\mathrm{induced}}/\electric{\varepsilon}_0$, not $/\electric{\varepsilon}$.
- [[#N3753|N3753]] Electric potential, capacitors, and Kirchhoff calculations: $\electric{\sigma}$ is used for conductivity in "Current density" while the table also lists $\electric{\sigma}$ as surface charge density; and the table lists symbols the note never uses or with wrong meanings ($\electric{Q}$ "semicircular arc", $\electric{I}_2$–$\electric{I}_6$ and $\circuit{R}_1$–$\circuit{R}_6$ "bridge", $\electric{V}_0$ "bridge sketch", $N$, $\Delta\electric{V}_L$, $\electric{v}_R$, $\electric{E}_0$ as "sinusoidal wave amplitude" though here it is the field without dielectric, $\theta$, $\mechanical{d}$ "slits or wire diameter"); rebuild it from the note's symbols.
- [[#N3755|N3755]] Electrostatic multipoles and matching at charge sources: The Physical quantities table is wrong for this note: $\mechanical{R}$ is described as a "Gaussian sphere radius" around a central charge (here it is the shell, sphere or charge radius), $\electric{V}_0$ appears twice including an unused "screened-potential coefficient" in $\mathrm{V\,m}$, and $\alpha$ is called a "Gaussian profile coefficient" in $\mathrm{m^{-2}}$ although here it is a dimensionless projection coefficient; add the missing $\electric{\phi}$, $\electric{\rho}$, $\electric{\rho}_0$, $\electric{p}$, $\electric{Q}_{ij}$, $\electric{q}'$, $\electric{Q}_{\mathrm{in}}$ and the coefficients $A_{\ell m},B_{\ell m},C_{\ell m},D_{\ell m}$.
- [[#N3755|N3755]] Electrostatic multipoles and matching at charge sources: Symbol clashes: $\phi$ is the azimuth in the first sections while $\electric{\phi}$ is the potential (later the azimuth becomes $\varphi$); $C=\sqrt{4\pi/3}$ clashes with the coefficients $C_{\ell m}$; $\electric{q}$ is both the dipole charge and the monopole moment; use $\varphi$ for the azimuth throughout and rename the constant.
- [[#N3756|N3756]] Electrostatic sources, potentials, and field energy: The Physical quantities table lists $\electric{\rho}_0$ twice, the second time as the "coefficient of $\cos\theta$ in the charged sphere", which belongs to the multipole note, and lists $\electric{\vec p}$, $\electric{\varepsilon}$, $c$ and $n$, which this note never uses; add the missing $\electric{\phi}$, $\energy{U}$, $\energy{W}$, $\electric{Q}$, $\electric{V}_0$, $\mechanical{R}$, $\mechanical{a},\mechanical{b}$.
- [[#N3756|N3756]] Electrostatic sources, potentials, and field energy: Symbol clashes: $\phi$ is both the azimuth and (as $\electric{\phi}$) the potential in the same integrals (use $\varphi$ for the azimuth), and $a$ is used for the delta-rectangle width, the screening parameter and (as $\mechanical{a}$) the inner shell radius; in "Potential of a uniformly charged sphere" the density switches from $\electric{\rho}$ to $\electric{\rho}_0$ mid-section.
- [[#N3757|N3757]] Field superposition and Gauss-law review: The Physical quantities table gives $\electric{Q}$ as "charge distributed along the semicircular arc", lists $\mechanical{s}$ twice with different meanings (dipole separation and object distance), lists $\electric{\sigma}$ also as conductivity, and includes unused entries ($\electric{\varepsilon}$, $N$, $\electric{\eta}$, $\electric{\Phi}_{E,\mathrm{net}}$, $\magnetic{\vec B}$, two rows with no symbol); rebuild it from the symbols the note uses.
- [[#N3758|N3758]] Fixed-string normal modes and Fourier coefficients: In "Selecting modes with a clamp", the claim that only $n=5q$ survive is misleading: a clamp splits the string into two independent strings (0.5 m and 2 m, or 1 m and 1.5 m), each with its own modes $\omega=m\pi v/\ell_i$; the $n=5q$ full-length modes are only those in which both segments vibrate at a common frequency. State this and give the new fundamentals $\pi v/(2.0\,\mathrm m)$ and $\pi v/(0.5\,\mathrm m)$ for the first clamp position.
- [[#N3758|N3758]] Fixed-string normal modes and Fourier coefficients: The Physical quantities table lists unused or wrong entries: $\mechanical{F}$ "restoring force", $\signal{\alpha}$ "response phase relative to the driving cosine" (here it is the spatial phase of $f(x)$), $\mechanical{b}$ twice including "pulse height", and $d$ "dispersion coefficient"; add the missing $\mechanical{A}_n$, $\mechanical{B}_n$, $\mechanical{L}$, $\mechanical{v}$, $\signal{\nu}_1$, $\energy{E}_n$, $\energy{K}$, and give the ramp slope a symbol other than $k$, which clashes with the spring constant $\mechanical{k}$ in Exercise 3-14.
- [[#N3759|N3759]] Induction, circuit transients, and filter measurements: The Physical quantities table lists meanings the note never uses: $\electric{Q}$ "charge distributed along the semicircular arc" (here capacitor charge), $\mechanical{A}$ "area over which the surface charge is distributed" (here loop area), $\electric{I}_2$–$\electric{I}_6$ "bridge branch" currents (here $\electric{I}_1$, $\electric{I}_2$ are coil currents), plus unused $\energy{U}$, $\electric{\varepsilon}$, $\electric{v}_R$, $\electric{v}_L$, $\magnetic{\mu}$; it also omits the resistance $\circuit{R}$, $\electric{I}_0$, $\electric{V}_{\mathrm{bat}}$ and $\electric{Q}_{\max}$, $\electric{I}_{\max}$; rebuild it from the symbols actually used.
- [[#N3760|N3760]] Laplace equation in Cartesian and spherical geometries: Symbol clash: $\phi$ is both the electrostatic potential $\electric{\phi}$ and the azimuthal angle in $\electric{\phi}(\mechanical{r},\theta,\phi)$, $\partial^2/\partial\phi^2$ and $Y_{\ell m}(\theta,\phi)$; use $\varphi$ for the azimuth (as the companion magnetic-materials note does). Likewise $a$ is the period ($k_n=2\pi n/a$), the Fourier coefficients $a_n$, $a(k)$, and later the inner shell radius $\mechanical{a}$; rename the period (e.g. $\Lambda$).
- [[#N3761|N3761]] Magnetic forces and fields of wires and loops: Physical quantities table: $\Delta\mechanical{r}$ is described as "Difference in distance traveled by the two interfering waves" but here it is the radius difference $\mechanical{r}_{26}-\mechanical{r}_{24}$ of two isotopes; $\electric{Q}$ "charge distributed along the semicircular arc" (only $\electric{Q}_{\mathrm{enc}}$ appears), $\electric{I}_2$–$\electric{I}_6$ "bridge branch" (here $\electric{I}_1$–$\electric{I}_3$ are Ampère-loop currents), and $\mechanical{m}$ "supported by the electric force or suspended by the string" are wrong; $\electric{\varepsilon}$ and $\magnetic{\mu}$ are unused.
- [[#N3761|N3761]] Magnetic forces and fields of wires and loops: The current-element step replaces $\electric{q}\mechanical{\vec v}$ by $\electric{I}\Delta\mechanical{\vec x}$ but the next formula uses $\electric{I}\Delta\mechanical{\vec s}$ and the loop section uses $\mathrm{d}\mechanical{\vec\ell}$; use one symbol for the directed element throughout.
- [[#N3762|N3762]] Magnetic materials, bound currents, and interface problems: Symbol clashes: in the linear-sphere matching the coefficients $A$, $B$, $C$, $D$ collide with the vector potential $\magnetic{\mathbf A}$ and field $\magnetic{\mathbf B}$ (rename to $\alpha,\beta,\gamma,\delta$), and $\mechanical{R}$ is both the center-to-center separation of $\electric{\rho}_1,\electric{\rho}_2$ and the sphere/cylinder radius while the expansion then calls the separation $\mechanical{\mathbf r}$; also, the interior term $B/\mechanical{r}^2$ must be set to zero for regularity at the origin before matching.
- [[#N3763|N3763]] Maxwell equations, retarded potentials, and conservation: Symbol clash: $\circuit{I}_0$ is a current in "Infinite wire with a switched current" but a current per time in "Infinite wire with a linearly increasing current" (the text even admits this); rename the slope (e.g. $\dot{\circuit{I}}_0$ in $\unit{A\,s^{-1}}$). In the opening lines the potential coefficients $B$, $C$, $D$ also collide with the field $\magnetic{B}$.
- [[#N3764|N3764]] Mechanical oscillation and traveling-wave problems: Symbol clashes: $k$ is the spring constant, the torsion constant and the wave number; $T$ is the period and the tensions $T_1,T_2$; $I$ is the moment of inertia and $\signal{I}$ the intensity; give distinct symbols (e.g. $\kappa$ for the torsion constant) and apply the vault macros ($\mechanical{}$, $\energy{}$, $\signal{}$) consistently; the quantity table lists only $\energy{P}$ and $\signal{I}$ and must include $x$, $v$, $a$, $m$, $k$, $\omega$, $f$, $T$, $A$, $b$, $\lambda$, $\mu$, $F$, $L$, $I$.
- [[#N3765|N3765]] Moving sources and electrodynamics review problems: Symbol clashes: $\theta$ is both the polar angle from $\hat{\mathbf z}$ (rotating dipole, sphere potential) and the in-plane trajectory angle from the $\mechanical{x}$ axis in Set 7 problem 1; $\mechanical{R}$ is both the sphere radius and the Liénard–Wiechert source-to-observer distance; use e.g. $\alpha$ for the trajectory angle and $s$ for the distance.
- [[#N3766|N3766]] Oscillator and wave-mode review calculations: Physical quantities table: $\mechanical{b}$ appears twice, the second as "Pulse height and half-width" which this note never uses; $d$ "String dispersion coefficient" is unused; $\signal{\alpha}$ is described as the response phase relative to the driving cosine, but in the note it is the phase constant of the free solution (the steady lag is $\signal{\delta}$); and the $\mechanical{T}$ row refers to a period $\signal{T}$ that does not appear.
- [[#N3766|N3766]] Oscillator and wave-mode review calculations: Symbol clashes: in "Nondispersive wave equation and energy" $T$ is both the tension $\mechanical{T}$ and the transmission coefficient, and $\mechanical{k}$ (bulk modulus) sits next to the wave number $\signal{k}$; tension is also written $\mechanical{F}_T$ in the standing-wave formula; $\mechanical{A}$ is the profile height while $A_m$, $A_0$ are Fourier coefficients and $\mechanical{A}(\signal{\omega})$ the resonance amplitude.
- [[#N3768|N3768]] Polarization, interference, refraction, and lenses: Symbol clashes: $\mechanical{p}_{\mathrm{rad}}$ is a radiation pressure (Pa) while $\mechanical{p}$ is momentum in the next section, and the integer fringe order $m$ shares its letter with the mass $\mechanical{m}$; use a distinct pressure symbol (e.g. $\mechanical{P}_{\mathrm{rad}}$ with power kept as $\energy{P}$) and $n$ or $m_{\mathrm{order}}$ for the order.
- [[#N3768|N3768]] Polarization, interference, refraction, and lenses: Physical quantities table: $\mechanical{s}$ is listed as "Dipole separation" (here it is the object distance), $\mechanical{A}$ as "area over which the surface charge is distributed" (here a cross-sectional area), $\energy{P}$ as "power in the resistive element" (here beam or pulse power), $\mechanical{m}$ as "mass supported by the electric force"; $\mechanical{r}$ and $\magnetic{\mu}$ are unused, while $\mechanical{\ell}$, $\mechanical{D}$, $\Delta y$, $\energy{I}_0$ and the order $m$ are missing.
- [[#N3769|N3769]] Pulse reflection, wavefronts, and refraction problems: Physical-quantities table: $\mechanical{b}$ appears twice, and the "Damping coefficient, kg s^-1" row should be deleted because $b$ is only the pulse height and half-width here. $\mechanical{M}$ is listed as "Reduced mass" but is the string mass in 6-1(a). $\mechanical{\theta}$ is listed as "Local tangent angle" but is used for ray angles measured from the normal. $\mechanical{c}$ is "Wave speed" but the note uses it for the vacuum speed of light (and $ct$ in the Fig. 53 caption).
- [[#N3769|N3769]] Pulse reflection, wavefronts, and refraction problems: The table omits symbols the note uses: $\mechanical{v}$, $\mechanical{v}_y$ (transverse velocity; it shares the letter with the wave speed, so name it $\partial\mechanical{y}/\partial\mechanical{t}$ or $\mechanical{u}_y$), $\mechanical{L}$, $\mechanical{g}$, $\mechanical{A}$, $\signal{f}$, $\signal{T}$ (period), $\mechanical{\ell}$, $\mechanical{m}_s$, $\mechanical{m}_b$, $\mechanical{\alpha}$.
- [[#N3771|N3771]] Radiation from antennas and electromagnetic multipoles: Physical-quantities table: $\mechanical{L}$ is listed as "Gaussian cylinder length" and $\mechanical{d}$ as "Plate separation". Here they are the length of the straight antenna and the length (or quadrupole charge spacing) of the tapered antenna. The table also omits $k$, $\magnetic{\mathbf A}$, $\electric{\phi}$, $\electric{\rho}$, $\circuit{\mathbf J}$, $\electric{\mathbf p}$, $\magnetic{\mathbf m}$, $\electric{Q}_{ab}$, $\mechanical{a}$, $\mechanical{r}$, and $\theta$.
- [[#N3771|N3771]] Radiation from antennas and electromagnetic multipoles: Symbol clash: $\electric{Q}$ means the point charge ($\pm Q(t)$ and $-Q$ at $\pm d/2$) and also, as $\electric{Q}_{ab}$ or $\electric{\mathbf Q}$, the quadrupole tensor in $\mathrm{C\,m^2}$, so $Q_{xx}=\tfrac{2Q}{3}(d/2)^2$ mixes the two in one line. Rename the charge (e.g. $q$). Also, $\mechanical{a}$ is used for the loop area while $a,b$ index the tensor.
- [[#N3771|N3771]] Radiation from antennas and electromagnetic multipoles: "Radiated power": $d^2P/(d\Omega\,d\omega)$ is called "fluence", but fluence is energy per unit area. Jackson's spectral quantity $d^2I/(d\omega\,d\Omega)$ is energy radiated per unit solid angle per unit frequency (J s/sr), not a power. Mark the page's label as a misnomer.
- [[#N3772|N3772]] Resonance, coupled modes, and Fourier practice: Symbol clashes: $\mechanical{M}$ is the string mass ($\mu=M/L$, HW2 p3 $M\simeq1.4$ kg) and also the reduced mass in the coupled-oscillator limit. $\signal{\omega}_1$ is the string fundamental and also the free damped frequency $\sqrt{\omega_0^2-\gamma^2/4}$ in the formula review. Uncolored $k$ is the ramp slope next to the spring stiffness $\mechanical{k}$. Rename one of each pair (e.g. $\mu_r$, $\omega_d$, $s$ for the slope).
- [[#N3772|N3772]] Resonance, coupled modes, and Fourier practice: Table: $\signal{\beta}$ is described as an "Overdamped rate offset" in $\mathrm{s^{-1}}$, but the note uses it as a phase in $B e^{-\gamma t/2}\cos(\omega_1t+\beta)$. The second $\mechanical{b}$ row ("Pulse height") and the $d$ row ("dispersion coefficient") describe symbols this note never uses. $\mechanical{F}$ is called "Restoring force" but only the drive amplitude $\mechanical{F}_0$ appears. $\mechanical{k}$, $\mechanical{L}$, $\mechanical{v}$, $\mechanical{A}_n$, $\mechanical{B}_n$, and $\energy{E}_n$ are missing.
- [[#N3773|N3773]] Spherical harmonics and magnetic dipole boundary problems: The polarization paragraph links "[[#Magnetic potential of a uniformly magnetized block|the section on Homework review ·]]" for the profile $P_r=P_0r^2\cos\theta$. That target is the magnetized-block section, which does not contain this profile, and the display text is garbled. Point to the profile stated just above under Problem 6-2.
- [[#N3773|N3773]] Spherical harmonics and magnetic dipole boundary problems: Problem 6-2: the text reports the handwritten result "$\mathbf H=0$" and then states $\mathbf H=-\mathbf M$ inside without saying which is right. With $\mathbf B=0$ everywhere, $\mathbf H=-M_0\hat{\mathbf r}$ inside and $0$ outside. Say explicitly that the handwritten $\mathbf H=0$ holds only outside, since the magnetic charge $-2M_0/r$ inside and $\sigma_m=M_0$ on the surface cancel only in total.
- [[#N3774|N3774]] Steady currents, vector potentials, and magnetic multipoles: The physical-quantities table lists only $U$, $I_{\mathrm{enc}}$, and $\mathbf m$. Add $\magnetic{\mathbf B}$, $\magnetic{\mathbf A}$, $\circuit{\mathbf J}$, $\circuit{I}$, $\magnetic{\mu}_0$, $\chi$, $\mechanical{R}$, $\mechanical{\rho}$ (cylindrical radius, distinct from the charge density $\electric{\rho}$ used in the Coulomb analogy), $\mechanical{\rho}_0$, $\electric{q}$, and $\electric{\mathbf p}$. Note also that $\mathbf m$ is the first moment of the current distribution only in the sense of $\tfrac12\int\mathbf r'\times\mathbf J$.
- [[#N3776|N3776]] Superposition, electric flux, and Gauss’s law problems: The displayed equation $\mechanical{\vec F}=\partial_x\energy{U}\,\hat\imath+\partial_y\energy{U}\,\hat\jmath+\partial_z\energy{U}\,\hat k$ in "Electrostatics" is still shown without the minus sign; display the correct $\mechanical{\vec F}=-\nabla\energy{U}$ and drop the sentence "The vector expression on this line is written with positive derivatives" instead of correcting it only in a callout.
- [[#N3776|N3776]] Superposition, electric flux, and Gauss’s law problems: "Kirchhoff's laws": the displayed equations remain inconsistent ("$\electric{V}_0=\electric{I}\circuit{R}_1-\dots=0$" and $\electric{I}_4$ leaving both nodes in $\electric{I}_2=\electric{I}_4+\electric{I}_5$, $\electric{I}_3=\electric{I}_4+\electric{I}_6$); write a consistent set, e.g. $\electric{V}_0-\electric{I}\circuit{R}_1-\dots=0$ and $\electric{I}_3+\electric{I}_4=\electric{I}_6$ if $\electric{I}_4$ flows from the $\electric{I}_2$ node to the $\electric{I}_3$ node, consistent with Fig. 3.
- [[#N3776|N3776]] Superposition, electric flux, and Gauss’s law problems: The physical-quantities table lists many symbols the note never uses or with wrong meanings: $\electric{\varepsilon}$, $N$ (turn count), $\electric{q}_C$ as capacitor charge (here it is the 1 nC charge at vertex C), $\Delta\mechanical{r}$ as path difference, $\mechanical{s},\mechanical{o},\mechanical{s}_o$ as object distance (clashes with dipole separation $\mechanical{s}$), $\electric{e}/\mechanical{m}$, $N\magnetic{\Phi}_B$, $\electric{V}_{\mathrm{in}},\electric{V}_{\mathrm{out}}$, $\mechanical{D}_i$, $\mechanical{D}_{0i}$, $\electric{\sigma}$, and descriptions mentioning slits, wire diameter, pendulum, screen, coil, and mirror; prune it to the symbols actually used and add the missing ones ($\electric{Q}_1,\electric{Q}_2,\electric{Q}_{\mathrm{enc}},\electric{Q}_{\mathrm{tot}},\electric{q}_A,\electric{q}_B$).
